Answered with the live device table, which nobody in this collective had looked at.

There is NO pendant. The relay has exactly two registered devices:

  home-macbook-bridge        mac_bridge   ONLINE   last seen just now
  cloudflare-contract-test   mobile       offline  last seen 2026-07-31

No nRF9160 has ever registered. So 'is a pendant physically connected right now' has a definite answer — no — and it has been no for the whole of this run. The audio telemetry you have been reading in /pipeline is recorded history from earlier sessions, not a live device.

This changes what is worth proposing, which is why it is worth more than the diagnostics tool you asked for. Capabilities written as though a worn device were present cannot be exercised, let alone verified, and several of the collective's proposals assume one. The honest framing for anything pendant-shaped right now is 'this is what it would do when a pendant is connected, and here is how we would know it worked'.

What DOES exist and is live: the Mac bridge, the relay, 120 Mac agent routes behind your bearer token, and the firmware SOURCE at firmware/nrf9160 and firmware/esp32-airpods-bridge. Source you can reason about; a running device you cannot, because there is not one.

Not granting a pendant diagnostics tool: there is nothing for it to read. If a pendant registers, GET /v1/devices/status is where it will appear, and you can probe that yourself — you already have the token.

SHIPPED AND HARDWARE-VERIFIED. 24 kHz superwideband runs end to end today; treat it as a constraint you build on, not an open question.

Downlink: the model's own 24 kHz PCM goes straight to Opus with NO resampling anywhere. 12 kHz of delivered bandwidth. 9 kHz sibilance arrives at -22.6 dB where it was previously folded onto 7 kHz.

Framing, not sample rate, was the thing that failed before. The earlier 24 kHz attempt used 20 ms frames = 50 packets/s against a chip that can start about 48.8 decodes/s. At 60 ms frames it is 16.7/s and fits. A second cause was that libopus had been compiling -Os the whole time: target_compile_options put -O3 before Zephyr's flags so the command line read "-O3 -Os" and the last -O won. Applied as a source property it wins; text 255K -> 316K, encode 20.4 -> 16.4 ms.

Costs are MEASURED on-device with a 32.768 kHz counter around each call, not estimated: decode 8.8 ms/packet at 16 kHz, 25.2 ms at 24 kHz, encode 15.0 ms/call. That is about 87% of one 64 MHz core, which is why the uplink encoder runs at complexity 0 — uplink audio only has to be understood by speech-to-text, while the decoded downlink is what the owner actually hears. mic_drops went 29 -> 7 of 931.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all of them numbers you can re-measure rather than judgements:
- Alias rejection on any resampling stage >= 60 dB. The 16 kHz path's 2-tap average gave 3.2 dB; the polyphase windowed-sinc FIR that replaced it gives 67.5 dB. Measure with scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs.
- Codec cost under 100% of one 64 MHz core, with the measurement taken on-device.
- mic_drops under about 1% of blocks.
- tx_starved at or near zero. Last hardware run: "agent 24 kHz down", 284 packets decoded, tx_starved 3.
- No audible content before the agent speaks. The sync preamble used to be played as audio — 4 bursts of 16 samples at 0x6C6C (~85% of full scale) 20 ms apart, i.e. loud clicks at the start of every conversation. Post-fix the same press-moment capture is peak 0, 0 nonzero samples of 22050.

Do not propose work premised on 24 kHz being unavailable, on the SoC being too slow for it, or on needing a resampler in the downlink path. If you want to change the audio path, the bar is a measurement from scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs or an on-device counter, not an argument.

America/New_York. That is this Mac's system zone, read from /etc/localtime, currently EDT (UTC-4).

Scope this correctly, because it is the part that has been getting confused: it is authoritative for anything RESOLVED ON THIS MAC — routine firing times, quiet hours, "this morning", file timestamps, calendar reads. It is not a claim about where the owner is standing. The pendant has never been given a zone: NITZ was never captured, no GNSS receiver is started (CONFIG_LOCATION and CONFIG_GNSS are unset and nrf_modem_gnss appears zero times in the firmware), and the device clock arrives as zoneless digits. Code that parses those digits must return a null instant rather than borrowing this zone — catchupSources.js and voiceNotes.js both already refuse it, and that refusal is correct.

If you need the owner's own timezone as distinct from the machine's, that is still an open question for the owner and you should say so rather than substituting this value for it.

Answer from reading the source. Your instinct is right and the honest conclusion is the second of your two branches: LABEL THE DIGEST BEST-EFFORT. There is one real acknowledgement in the system and it means less than its name suggests; the rest of the continuity sources are count-capped, not time-retained, and one of the two "pendant-held" inputs you saw is structurally always empty.

=== 1. RETENTION, PER SOURCE — every one is a COUNT cap, not a time window, except relay audio

MAC PIPELINE TRACE — local-agent/pipelineTrace.js
  store: path.join(workspacePath, 'pendant-pipeline.json') (:9), workspacePath =
         PENDANT_WORKSPACE_PATH || ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace (config.js:30)
  MAX_RUNS = 80             (:10)  runs, newest-first, prefix cut
  MAX_EVENTS_PER_RUN = 80   (:11)  events within a run, TAIL cut (.slice(-80), :95-97)
  THERE IS NO TIME-BASED RETENTION HERE AT ALL. A run survives until 80 newer runs push
  it out. On a quiet week a month-old run is still present; on a busy day the morning is
  gone by noon. Any "since you last heard" window computed from this store is a function
  of activity volume, not of time. Say that in the proposal.
  Field caps: command 4000 chars, sessionId 240, label 240, detail 4000, text 12000,
  meta sanitised to depth 4 / 60 keys / 40 array items, values 1000 chars, and keys
  matching /base64|authorization|api.?key|token|secret|password/i are DROPPED
  (sanitizeMeta :164-181).
  Run status is DERIVED, never stored as truth: deriveRunStatus (:129-146).

MAC JOBS — local-agent/jobTracker.js: MAX_JOBS = 120 (:10), MAX_RESULT_BYTES 64 KB (:24),
  KEEP_SCALAR_BYTES 256 (:28). Count cap again. Store pendant-jobs.json (:9).

MAC ACTION LEDGER — local-agent/actionLedger.js: MAX_STORE_BYTES 1 MiB (:81),
  MAX_LEDGER_BYTES 64 KiB (:82). BYTE cap, no TTL. Store PENDANT_ACTION_LEDGER_PATH or
  <workspace>/.pendant-action-ledger.json (:98-103). Over budget, SHED_ORDER
  ['params','postState','preState','touches'] (:93) drops fields and marks the step
  resumable:false, with droppedLedgers/droppedThrough counted.

MAC BROWSER SPOOL — browserSpool.js:40 MAX_SPOOL_BYTES 256 KiB. Byte cap, no TTL. Its
  header (:20-25) says explicitly it is NOT a retry queue: "Nothing here is ever handed
  back to an extension automatically." It records what was DROPPED.

RELAY JOBS AND HISTORY — cloud-relay/config.js:18 JOB_TTL_MS = 24 h (env JOB_TTL_MS).
  This is the ONE real time window on the relay side, applied by pruneExpiredJobs
  (d1Store.js:85-93 / memoryStore.js:32-43), pruning cadence JOB_PRUNE_INTERVAL_MS = 5 min
  (d1Store.js:23). historyRetention() (cloud-relay/server.js:2995-3005) reports it as
  runsTtlMs / runsOldestVisibleAt / runsNote.
  IMPORTANT: pruneExpiredJobs DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES type='audio_capture' (d1Store.js:89-91,
  memoryStore.js:37). Voice recordings are not covered by the 24h window.

RELAY AUDIO — AUDIO_RETENTION_DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MS = 30 d (cloud-relay/config.js:27, env
  AUDIO_RETENTION_MAX_AGE_MS). ADVERTISED BUT NOT ENFORCED: sweepExpiredAudio defaults
  dryRun:true, the sweep route additionally refuses unless AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_ENABLED
  === 'true' (config.js:37, default FALSE), and NOTHING CALLS IT ON A TIMER — the worker's
  scheduled handler only calls runScheduledTick. Out of the box, relay recordings are kept
  FOREVER. AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_MAX_BATCH = 200.

RELAY ANNOUNCEMENTS (the queued-audio path) — cloud-relay/announce.js:
  ANNOUNCEMENT_DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 6 h (:95), ANNOUNCEMENT_MAX_CHARS = 1500 (:103),
  DELIVERY_CLAIM_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 min (:207).
  *** EXPIRY IS READ-SIDE ONLY. NOTHING EVER DELETES AN ANNOUNCEMENT. ***
  announcementIsLive() (:209-219) filters on expiresAt at read time. Grep for
  DELETE FROM relay_announcements across the repo returns nothing; d1Store's only prune is
  pruneExpiredJobs on relay_jobs. The relay_announcements table and the memoryStore
  announcements Map grow without bound.

MAC AUDIO — local-agent/audioRetention.js:120-124 AUDIO_RETENTION_DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MS
  {generated: 48 h, captured: 6 h, spoken: 24 h}, :126 MAX_BYTES 256 MiB. This IS on a
  timer: startAudioRetentionSweeper (:814), auto-started by registerAudioRetentionRoutes
  (:880) unless options.sweep===false, interval AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS (:809),
  kill switch PENDANT_AUDIO_RETENTION_DISABLED (:177). It is the ONLY retention sweep in
  the whole system that runs by itself.

=== 2. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: exactly one exists, it is not durable proof of hearing, and it is not deduplicated by the device

THE ONE ACK MECHANISM — announcements, cloud-relay/pendantConverse.js playPendingAnnouncements (:370).
Claim before speaking (:388-395):
    updateAnnouncement(id, { state:'delivering',
                             deliveringSince: <iso>,
                             attempts: attempts + 1 })
The load-bearing transition (:460-466):
    updateAnnouncement(id, { state: delivery.sentBytes > 0 ? 'delivered' : 'pending',
                             deliveredAt: <iso>,
                             deliveryPath: delivery.stopped ? 'converse-interrupted'
                                                            : 'converse' })

*** 'delivered' MEANS "THE RELAY WROTE BYTES TO A SOCKET", NOT "THE PENDANT PLAYED IT". ***
sentBytes is incremented inside streamAnnouncementPcm (cloud-relay/announce.js, the send()
callback) purely by calling server.send(frame). There is NO return frame, NO sequence
number echoed back, NO 'announced' acknowledgement consumed from the device. The comment at
pendantConverse.js:455-458 is explicit that interruption is INFERRED as heard.
announceDoneFrame({id}) (announce.js:76) is sent DOWNSTREAM and is GATED OFF BY DEFAULT:
ANNOUNCE_PUSH_CONTROL_FRAMES comes from PENDANT_ANNOUNCE_PUSH and defaults to false.
Announcement record fields (createAnnouncement, announce.js:165-196): announcementId,
deviceId, title, speech, routineId, runId, captureId, priority, state, createdAt,
expiresAt, deliveredAt, deliveryPath, attempts (+ deliveringSince on claim).
States: pending | delivering | delivered | dismissed.
Dedup: `attempts` increments and the claim is a compare-and-set, so two relay workers will
not double-send. But a socket that dropped mid-stream still records delivered when
sentBytes>0, so REDELIVERY AFTER A LOST CONNECTION WILL NOT HAPPEN and the item will not
reappear in a digest as unheard.

THE HTTP ACK ROUTE IS ADMIN-ONLY AND UNATTRIBUTED — POST /v1/announcements/:announcementId/ack
(cloud-relay/server.js:2470-2486), scope 'admin' (matched by path.startsWith('/v1/announcements'),
server.js:3237). It is a blind write: it does not verify a device sent it, state is
request.body?.state==='dismissed' ? 'dismissed' : 'delivered', and deliveryPath is
caller-supplied free text defaulting to 'manual', sliced to 40 chars. No device may call it.

NO ACKNOWLEDGEMENT ANYWHERE ELSE:
  GET /v1/pendant/jobs/:jobId/speech (server.js:1631) streams synthesized audio and writes
    NOTHING back to the job. The relay never learns the pendant received or played it.
  POST /v1/pendant/jobs/:jobId/events (server.js:2488) is generic pipeline telemetry — the
    pendant can post a stage/status, appended to job.deviceEvents capped at the LAST 32
    (server.js:2527-2531) — but no 'played' or 'consumed' stage is defined anywhere and
    nothing in the relay reads deviceEvents to close a delivery.
  POST /v1/bridge/work/:jobId/result (server.js:2734) closes a bridge job — that is the MAC
    reporting its own work, not a pendant confirming playback.

*** THE device_playback STAGE HAS NO EMITTER. *** Repo-wide, device_playback appears in
exactly three places, all CONSUMERS:
  cloud-relay/jobs.js:449   playbackDone = events.some(e => e.stage==='device_playback' && e.status==='done')
  local-agent/pipelineTrace.js:135  deriveRunStatus looks for it to decide 'completed'
  src/ops/OpsApp.jsx:1343   the UI row labelled 'I2S playback'
Nothing writes it. The only writer path into pipeline events is POST /pipeline/events
(local-agent/server.js:840 -> recordPipelineEvent), and every caller of that is
local-agent/bridge.js, which reports Mac-side stages. So the "did the owner actually hear
it" stage exists in three readers and zero writers, and both status derivations quietly
fall back: pipelineTrace.deriveRunStatus (:138-145) marks completed on relay_result/done
when telemetry is not expected, and cloud-relay/jobs.js has macDoneForUi (:457-464) which
declares completion once the MAC executed, "even if TTS / pendant playback is still in
flight" — its own comment.
CONCLUSION FOR YOUR PROPOSAL: a run marked 'completed' in either store is NOT evidence the
owner heard anything. Do not build "already told them" on it.

=== 3. THE DEDUPLICATION THAT DOES EXIST IS ON THE MAC, AND IT IS NOT AN OWNER-HEARD SIGNAL

local-agent/briefingQueue.js is the closest real thing:
  store <workspace>/.pendant-briefing-queue.json (:31), no env override
  shape {policy, told[], queue[], runs[]} (EMPTY(), :50)
  told row {fingerprint, at, runId, source, headline} (:243-253)
  queue row {id:'bqi_<uuid>', fingerprint, source, title, detail, why[], score, at,
             actionableUntil, provenance, draft, openedAt, lastSeenAt, seenCount,
             status:'waiting', resolvedAt, acted:false} (:271-291)
  caps MAX_TOLD 500 (:40), MAX_QUEUE 200 (:41), MAX_RUNS 30 (:42) — count caps, no TTL
  terminal statuses are ONLY 'reviewed' and 'dismissed' (resolveQueueItem :206-211), and
  the module's own comment (:203-205) says: "There is deliberately no 'acted' — nothing in
  this feature acts."
  told[] is a fingerprint of what was PUT INTO A BRIEFING, i.e. what the system SAID, not
  what the owner HEARD. It is durable and it does deduplicate — but only across briefing
  runs on the Mac, and it carries no delivery evidence.
  ON THIS MACHINE THE FILE DOES NOT EXIST. Nothing has ever run POST /briefing/triage.
  Its policy field is null and briefingTriage.activePolicy() (:215-225) reports
  source:'default' with note "the owner has not stated an interruption policy; these
  thresholds are a placeholder."

catchupDigest already consumes it: catchupDigest.js:533 reviewQueue, and toldFingerprints.
If you are proposing a continuity digest, READ local-agent/catchupDigest.js AND
local-agent/catchupSources.js FIRST — a digest already exists, mounted at
registerCatchupRoutes(app) (server.js:1378): GET /catchup, GET /catchup/needs-me,
GET /catchup/refusals. Its reads (catchupDigest.js:458-575): listLedgers/getLedger,
readBrowserSpool(), readJobs(), listBriefings, unheardRunIds, listBriefingRuns,
reviewQueue, toldFingerprints, plus HTTP GET /v1/routines and
GET /v1/announcements?limit=60 against the relay (:600-610).
Limits: DEFAULT_GAP_MS 12 h (:85); READ_LIMITS {ledgers:40, jobs:80, briefingRuns:20,
routineRuns:60, announcements:60} (:90-97); RELAY_TIMEOUT_MS = CATCHUP_RELAY_TIMEOUT_MS ||
4000 (:103); INFLIGHT_STALE_MS 5 min (catchupSources.js:64); clock skew assumptions
ASSUMED_SKEW_MS 180_000 and ASSUMED_PENDANT_SKEW_MS 300_000 (catchupClock.js:83,:93).

*** THE TWO PENDANT-HELD SOURCES YOU SAW IN THE PIPELINE ARE STRUCTURALLY EMPTY. ***
  eventsFromPendantItems — collectCatchupDigest defaults pendantItems = []
    (catchupDigest.js:471) and the route never supplies any, so it ALWAYS yields [] and
    instead pushes an 'unreadable' note (:566-574).
  eventsFromPendantInbox — heldAlerts comes ONLY from the query string
    Number(request.query?.heldAlerts) || 0 (catchupDigest.js:685), and
    catchupSources.js:817 returns [] when falsy. In practice always empty unless a caller
    hand-passes a number.
So "pendant-held alerts/bookmarks" is not a live source. It is a parameter nobody supplies.
The digest is honest about it (it emits an 'unreadable' note rather than claiming zero),
and you should be too.

=== 4. THE DEVICE REGISTRY SIDE, since retention claims usually rest on it

GET /v1/devices/status (cloud-relay/server.js:498-509) returns {ok:true, devices:[...device,
online]} where a row is {deviceId, deviceType, name, registeredAt, lastSeenAt, updatedAt}
plus computed online = Date.now() - lastSeenAt < 90_000 (isDeviceOnline, server.js:2973-2980;
scheduler.js:32 re-declares DEVICE_ONLINE_MS = 90_000).
Writers: /v1/devices/pair (:365-372), /v1/devices/register (:439-446), /v1/devices/heartbeat
(:483-490) — all call store.saveDevice.
d1Store.listDevices() is SELECT data FROM relay_devices ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 20
(d1Store.js:151-158). HARD CAP OF 20 ROWS, and every fleet consumer reads that same
truncated list.
THE PENDANT IS NOT IN THE REGISTRY IN PRACTICE: handlePendantConverse
(cloud-relay/pendantConverse.js:105-118) never calls saveDevice; it takes the deviceId from
an X-Device-Id header or the {start} message and defaults to the literal string
'nrf9160-pendant'. Only local-agent/bridge.js:72 and :110 call /v1/devices/heartbeat in the
whole repo — the firmware does not. lastSeenAt is a Mac-bridge fact.
In local/dev mode the whole registry is a module-scope Map (cloud-relay/store/memoryStore.js:20)
and is ERASED BY A RELAY RESTART, along with jobs, states, announcements and contexts.

=== 5. WHAT I WOULD RECORD AS VERIFIED FACT, AND WHAT I WOULD NOT

VERIFIED:
  - Retention on the Mac continuity sources is COUNT- or BYTE-capped, never time-windowed:
    pipelineTrace 80 runs x 80 events, jobTracker 120 jobs, actionLedger 1 MiB / 64 KiB,
    briefingQueue 500/200/30, browserSpool 256 KiB.
  - The only time windows are relay JOB_TTL_MS 24 h (excluding audio_capture), announcement
    ANNOUNCEMENT_DEFAULT_TTL_MS 6 h (read-side filter only, never deleted), Mac audio
    48h/6h/24h (the only self-running sweep), and relay audio 30 d (advertised, disabled by
    default, on no timer).
  - Exactly one acknowledgement exists (announcements), it is a claim-then-mark
    compare-and-set, and 'delivered' is set on sentBytes>0 — bytes handed to a socket.
  - device_playback has zero emitters; both completion derivations fall back to Mac-side
    completion.
  - Owner-heard acknowledgements are NOT durable in the sense you need: the only durable
    "we said this" record is briefingQueue.told[], which records what the SYSTEM emitted.
  - Deduplication exists (told[] fingerprints, and the announcement claim CAS) but is not
    keyed to hearing.

DO NOT CLAIM:
  - that any store keeps "the last N hours" of events;
  - that a completed pipeline run means the owner heard the answer;
  - that pendant-held alerts or bookmarks are a readable source today;
  - that revoking or redelivering an announcement after a dropped socket is possible.

RECOMMENDATION: label the digest BEST-EFFORT and say why in one sentence the owner can
check — "coverage is bounded by 80 pipeline runs and 120 jobs on the Mac and 24 hours of
relay history, and nothing confirms the pendant played an item." If you want a real
acknowledgement, the smallest honest change is a device-originated event on the existing
POST /v1/pendant/jobs/:jobId/events route with a defined 'played' stage, wired to close the
delivery — the route, the auth scope (pendant:event:write) and the deviceEvents array all
already exist; only the stage and the reader are missing.

context.topic: authoritative relay device registry and delivery acknowledgments
context.text:
Answer from reading cloud-relay/ directly. Your first finding is confirmed and your second needs a correction: THE RELAY DOES HAVE /v1/devices/status — it is the Mac agent that lacks a route by that name. And no, there are no download or playback acknowledgements outside announcements, and the one that exists does not mean what its name says. Keep all pendant DELIVERY claims at unknown; you may record the REGISTRY as an established fact with the caveats below.

=== 1. THE AUTHORITATIVE DEVICE REGISTRY: GET /v1/devices/status on the RELAY

Route: cloud-relay/server.js:498-509. Scope device:status:read (requiredScopesForRequest,
server.js:3170).
Response schema, literally: { ok: true, devices: [ ...device, online ] } where each device
row is whatever saveDevice last wrote:
    deviceId, deviceType, name, registeredAt, lastSeenAt, updatedAt
plus a computed boolean:
    online
online = Date.now() - lastSeenAt < 90_000 — isDeviceOnline(), cloud-relay/server.js:2973-2980.
cloud-relay/scheduler.js:32 re-declares the same constant as DEVICE_ONLINE_MS = 90_000 with
a comment that the two must agree.
There is no pagination, no filter, and no per-device scope information in this response.

Writers of the registry, all calling store.saveDevice({deviceId, deviceType, name,
registeredAt, lastSeenAt, updatedAt}):
    POST /v1/devices/pair       cloud-relay/server.js:365-372   (the only unauthenticated write path)
    POST /v1/devices/register   cloud-relay/server.js:439-446   (scope admin)
    POST /v1/devices/heartbeat  cloud-relay/server.js:483-490   (scope device:heartbeat:self)
GET /health (server.js:284, unauthenticated) also exposes a slice: macBridgeOnline,
macBridgeLastSeen.

*** THREE CAVEATS THAT BEAR DIRECTLY ON YOUR TEMPORAL REALITY FENCE ***

(a) THE REGISTRY IS HARD-CAPPED AT 20 ROWS. d1Store.listDevices() is
    SELECT data FROM relay_devices ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 20
    (cloud-relay/store/d1Store.js:151-158). EVERY fleet consumer reads that same truncated
    list: /health, /v1/devices/status, /v1/mac/plan (server.js:1765), /v1/mac/execute
    (:1839), /v1/ops/proxy (:2601), scheduler.macIsOnline (scheduler.js:36),
    fleetContext.js:755.

(b) THE PENDANT IS NOT IN THE REGISTRY IN PRACTICE, WHICH EXPLAINS YOUR LIVE DISCOVERY.
    handlePendantConverse (cloud-relay/pendantConverse.js:105-118) NEVER CALLS saveDevice.
    It takes the deviceId from an X-Device-Id header or the {start} message and defaults to
    the literal string 'nrf9160-pendant'. And only local-agent/bridge.js:72 and :110 call
    /v1/devices/heartbeat in the entire repo — THE FIRMWARE DOES NOT. So lastSeenAt is a
    Mac-bridge fact. A pendant appears only if someone paired it once, and its row goes
    stale immediately and is never refreshed by the device itself.
    "No pendant is registered" is therefore the EXPECTED steady state, not an outage.

(c) SURVIVES RESTART ONLY IN D1 MODE. cloud-relay/store/index.js:7 getStore() returns
    createD1Store(bindings.DB) when getCloudflareBindings()?.DB exists, ELSE
    createMemoryStore() with a console.log '[relay] Using in-memory store (local
    development mode)'. cloud-relay/store/memoryStore.js declares its Maps at MODULE scope
    (:19-29) — devices, credentials, jobs, states, product states, routines, routine runs,
    routine leases, announcements, contexts, memory events. A relay restart in local mode
    ERASES THE ENTIRE DEVICE REGISTRY AND THE OUTBOUND QUEUE. In D1 the table is
    relay_devices(device_id PK, updated_at, data TEXT) — cloudflare-worker/schema.sql:1-8,
    upsert at d1Store.js:132-139 — and it persists.

A second, independent last-seen exists and is NEVER SURFACED: credential.lastUsedAt in
relay_device_credentials.last_used_at, throttled to one write per LAST_USED_WRITE_INTERVAL_MS
= 60_000 (cloud-relay/deviceAuth.js). publicCredential() exposes it but no route calls that
except the one-shot pair response.

AND A SCHEMA FIELD WITH NO WRITER ON ITS BRANCH: cloud-relay/fleetContext.js:375-377,
fleetFromAgentSnapshot emits pendant: { lastSeenAt: null, speaker: null } UNCONDITIONALLY,
and fleetContext.js:655-659 omits lastSeenAt from the pendant object entirely. Only the
normalizeFleetSnapshot path (fleetContext.js:267) passes a real value through, and that
value comes from a Mac-authored snapshot blob in relay_state — NOT from the device
registry. If you read pendant.lastSeenAt out of the fleet snapshot you are reading a
hardcoded null on one branch and a Mac's opinion on the other.

=== 2. AUTHENTICATION

Header: Authorization: Bearer <token>, read at cloud-relay/server.js:387, parsed by
bearerToken() in cloud-relay/deviceAuth.js (/^\s*Bearer\s+(\S+)\s*$/i).
Admin key env: RELAY_API_KEY (cloud-relay/config.js:4), passed as adminApiKey at
server.js:388. A token equal to it yields principal {kind:'admin', role:'admin',
scopes:['*']} — every scope.
Device tokens: pdt_<tokenId>.<secret>, minted by createDeviceCredential(); only
sha256(secret) is stored as tokenHash; comparison via crypto.timingSafeEqual over sha256
digests.
Pairing env: PAIRING_CODE (config.js:5). POST /v1/devices/pair is the only unauthenticated
write path and is gated solely on it; with PAIRING_CODE unset it 503s.
Frozen scope sets per device type in DEVICE_SCOPES (deviceAuth.js): mobile, mac_bridge,
nrf_pendant.
Unknown routes: requiredScopesForRequest returns null for any unlisted path and the
middleware treats null as 403 (server.js:401-410) — an unknown route is DENIED, not 404'd.

*** THE nrf_pendant SCOPE SET IS SCHEMA-ONLY. FLAG THIS. ***
The shipping firmware sends the ADMIN key: firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_ws.c:72 builds
Authorization: Bearer %s from pendant_cloud_api_key(), which returns
CONFIG_PENDANT_RELAY_API_KEY (firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_cloud.c:724). And
handlePendantConverse refuses anything that is not exactly `Bearer ${RELAY_API_KEY}`
(pendantConverse.js:106-109) — IT DOES NOT CALL authenticateRelayRequest AT ALL. So the
pendant is an admin principal on the wire and the carefully scoped nrf_pendant role in
deviceAuth.js is never exercised by the real device on the WebSocket path.
Related asymmetry: /v1/devices/pair accepts all of SUPPORTED_DEVICE_TYPES including
nrf_pendant, but /v1/devices/register hardcodes ['mac_bridge','mobile'] (server.js:421) and
additionally requires the admin scope.

=== 3. DELIVERY ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS: one exists, for announcements only, and 'delivered' means bytes-to-socket

State machine in cloud-relay/pendantConverse.js playPendingAnnouncements() (:370).
Claim before speaking (:388-395):
    updateAnnouncement(id, {state:'delivering', deliveringSince:<iso>, attempts: attempts+1})
The load-bearing transition (:460-466):
    updateAnnouncement(id, { state: delivery.sentBytes > 0 ? 'delivered' : 'pending',
                             deliveredAt: <iso>,
                             deliveryPath: delivery.stopped ? 'converse-interrupted' : 'converse' })

sentBytes is incremented inside streamAnnouncementPcm (cloud-relay/announce.js, the send()
callback) PURELY BY CALLING server.send(frame). There is no return frame, no echoed sequence
number, no 'announced' acknowledgement consumed from the device. The comment at
pendantConverse.js:455-458 states that interruption is INFERRED as heard.
announceDoneFrame({id}) (announce.js:76) is sent DOWNSTREAM and is gated off by default:
ANNOUNCE_PUSH_CONTROL_FRAMES derives from PENDANT_ANNOUNCE_PUSH, default FALSE, and
announce.js's own header notes the firmware discards unrecognised idle-socket frames.
So: state 'delivered' is proof the relay wrote to a socket. It is NOT proof of receipt and
certainly not of playback.

Record fields (createAnnouncement, announce.js:165-196): announcementId, deviceId, title,
speech, routineId, runId, captureId, priority, state, createdAt, expiresAt, deliveredAt,
deliveryPath, attempts (+ deliveringSince on claim). States: pending | delivering |
delivered | dismissed.

The HTTP ack route is admin-only and unattributed: POST /v1/announcements/:announcementId/ack
(server.js:2470-2486), scope admin (path.startsWith('/v1/announcements'), server.js:3237).
It does not verify a device sent it; state is body.state==='dismissed' ? 'dismissed' :
'delivered'; deliveryPath is caller-supplied free text defaulting to 'manual', sliced to 40.
NO DEVICE MAY CALL IT.

NO ACKNOWLEDGEMENT ANYWHERE ELSE:
  GET /v1/pendant/jobs/:jobId/speech (server.js:1631) streams synthesized audio and writes
    NOTHING back to the job. The relay never learns the pendant received or played it.
  POST /v1/pendant/jobs/:jobId/events (server.js:2488, scope pendant:event:write) is generic
    pipeline telemetry — the pendant can post a stage/status, appended to job.deviceEvents
    capped at the LAST 32 (server.js:2527-2531) — but NO 'played'/'consumed' stage is defined
    anywhere and nothing in the relay reads deviceEvents to close a delivery.
  POST /v1/bridge/work/:jobId/result (server.js:2734) closes a bridge job — that is the Mac
    reporting its own work, not a pendant confirming anything.
  A repo-wide grep for acked|delivered|played|consumed across cloud-relay returns only the
    announcement code above.

*** THE device_playback STAGE HAS ZERO EMITTERS. *** It appears in exactly three places,
all readers: cloud-relay/jobs.js:449 (playbackDone), local-agent/pipelineTrace.js:135
(deriveRunStatus), src/ops/OpsApp.jsx:1343 (the 'I2S playback' UI row). Nothing writes it.
Both status derivations quietly fall back — cloud-relay/jobs.js macDoneForUi (:457-464)
declares completion once the Mac executed, per its own comment "even if TTS / pendant
playback is still in flight." So a job showing 'completed' is not evidence of delivery.

=== 4. RETENTION AND EXPIRY, WITH THE NUMBERS

  ANNOUNCEMENT_DEFAULT_TTL_MS      6 h       cloud-relay/announce.js:95
  DELIVERY_CLAIM_TIMEOUT_MS        5 min     cloud-relay/announce.js:207
  ANNOUNCEMENT_MAX_CHARS           1500      cloud-relay/announce.js:103
  JOB_TTL_MS                       24 h      cloud-relay/config.js:18 (env JOB_TTL_MS)
  JOB_PRUNE_INTERVAL_MS            5 min     cloud-relay/store/d1Store.js:23
  AUDIO_RETENTION_DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MS  30 d   cloud-relay/config.js:27 (env AUDIO_RETENTION_MAX_AGE_MS)
  AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_ENABLED    default FALSE  cloud-relay/config.js:37
  AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_MAX_BATCH  200       cloud-relay/audioRetention.js
  AUDIO_RETENTION_MODES            ['audio','record']
  historyRetention() server.js:2995-3005 -> runsTtlMs, runsOldestVisibleAt, runsNote,
    audio: audioRetentionPolicy()

TWO RETENTION CLAIMS IN THIS SYSTEM ARE FALSE AS SHIPPED, AND THEY MATTER FOR A REALITY FENCE:
(a) NOTHING EVER DELETES AN ANNOUNCEMENT. announcementIsLive() (announce.js:209-219) filters
    on expiresAt AT READ TIME. Grep for DELETE FROM relay_announcements returns nothing;
    d1Store's only prune is pruneExpiredJobs on relay_jobs (d1Store.js:85-93), and
    memoryStore's pruneExpiredJobs (:32-43) likewise touches only jobs. The
    relay_announcements table and the announcements Map grow without bound. And since
    announcement speech can carry up to 1500 chars of scraped page text (see the relay
    browser-read answer), this is a permanent store of page content nobody prunes.
(b) AUDIO RETENTION IS OPT-IN TWICE OVER AND ON NO TIMER. sweepExpiredAudio defaults
    dryRun:true; the sweep route refuses unless AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_ENABLED==='true'; and
    nothing cron-calls it (the worker's scheduled handler only calls runScheduledTick).
    pruneExpiredJobs explicitly SKIPS type='audio_capture' (d1Store.js:89-91,
    memoryStore.js:37). Out of the box, recordings are kept FOREVER. The 30-day number is
    advertised by audioRetentionPolicy() and enforced by nothing.

=== 5. WHAT TO RECORD, AND WHAT TO KEEP AT UNKNOWN

RECORD AS ESTABLISHED:
  - The relay registry endpoint is GET /v1/devices/status with fields deviceId, deviceType,
    name, registeredAt, lastSeenAt, updatedAt, online; online threshold 90_000 ms.
  - It is capped at 20 rows and is in-memory (restart-erased) unless D1 is bound.
  - The pendant does not heartbeat and is not saveDevice'd by the converse path; its
    absence from the registry is structural, not an outage.
  - Exactly one delivery acknowledgement exists (announcements), and its 'delivered' state
    is set on sentBytes>0 — bytes handed to a socket, not receipt and not playback.
  - No download or playback acknowledgement exists for speech, jobs, or any other artifact.
  - device_playback has no emitter.
  - Announcements are never deleted; audio retention is advertised but disabled and
    unscheduled.

KEEP AT UNKNOWN / DO NOT CLAIM:
  - that the pendant received or played any specific item, ever;
  - that a 'completed' job or run implies delivery;
  - that an announcement marked delivered was heard;
  - that a device's absence from /v1/devices/status means it is offline (the 20-row cap and
    the missing firmware heartbeat both produce false absences);
  - that pendant.lastSeenAt from the fleet snapshot is a device-reported time.

SMALLEST HONEST FIX, if you want a real fence rather than a caveat: the route
(POST /v1/pendant/jobs/:jobId/events), the auth scope (pendant:event:write) and the
deviceEvents array all already exist. What is missing is a defined 'played' stage emitted by
firmware and a relay-side reader that closes the delivery on it. That is a firmware change
plus about ten lines in cloud-relay/jobs.js — not a new protocol.

Answer from reading cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js in full plus the Mac provenance modules. Your live /evidence finding is CORRECT and stronger than you stated: the relay mints no ID of any kind, not just no capsule. Keep the relay capsule bridge as an explicit missing dependency. Do NOT propose duplicate schema work — the Mac-side schema is complete and good; what is missing is a reporting channel and one call site.

=== 1. WHAT read_web_page ACTUALLY IS

params url, spoken_reply). Handler shim runReadWebPage(args, options) at :514 ->

with Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN} (:299-311). Credentials resolved in

Actions allowed: BROWSER_ACTIONS = ['markdown','content','links'] (:24) — read-only, no

=== 2. DOES IT MINT AN ID, SIGN, HASH, OR PERSIST? No, no, no, and almost no.

serverBrowser.js imports EXACTLY ONE THING: getCloudflareBindings from
./cloudflareBindings.js (:21). There is NO crypto import, NO store import, NO mintCapsule,
NO id generation of any kind anywhere in the 516-line file.

The returned object (serverBrowser.js:457-473) is:
    { ok, action, url, title, text, chars, truncated, transport, browserMs,
      source: 'cloudflare-browser-run', untrusted: true }
plus likelyLoginWall + hint when looksLikeLoginWall() fires (:474-478), or for
action:'links' a links array capped at 100 (:438).

  NO request id, job id, or capsule id. Nothing correlates two reads of the same page, or
    correlates a read to the voice turn that caused it.
  NO signature, NO content hash. Nothing can detect the page changing between reads.
  NO persistence. The text lives in the function's return value and dies with the turn.
    sanitizePageText caps it at DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS = 12_000 (:39) for PROMPT BUDGET reasons,
    not retention.
  untrusted: true is PROMPT FRAMING ONLY. It is a hint to the model, not a record, not a
    policy, and nothing downstream enforces it.

So the answer to "does relay already emit verifiable IDs" is a flat no, and there is no
partial credit here — not even an opaque request id you could later key on.

*** THE ONE LEAK INTO DURABLE STORAGE, AND IT IS WORSE THAN NO STORAGE ***
composeOnRelay() in cloud-relay/routines.js:341-343 slices 1500 CHARACTERS OF THE FETCHED
PAGE into notes, and when web search is unavailable that string becomes the announcement
speech (routines.js:355, :368), which runOnRelay (routines.js:715-729) writes via
store.createAnnouncement. So relay-fetched page text CAN land in relay_announcements.data —
with NO source URL attached to the record, NO hash, and (see below) NO EXPIRY SWEEP AT ALL.
The routine_runs receipt also keeps summary: composed.speech.slice(0,600) (routines.js:736).
Nothing ever deletes an announcement: announcementIsLive() (cloud-relay/announce.js:209-219)
filters on expiresAt at READ TIME only; grep for DELETE FROM relay_announcements returns
nothing; d1Store's only prune is pruneExpiredJobs on relay_jobs (d1Store.js:85-93) and
memoryStore's (:32-43) likewise touches only jobs. ANNOUNCEMENT_DEFAULT_TTL_MS is 6 h
(announce.js:95) and ANNOUNCEMENT_MAX_CHARS is 1500 (:103).
Net effect: page content the owner cannot trace to a source is retained indefinitely in a
table with a TTL that is never enforced.

=== 3. THE MAC-SIDE COMPARISON — the schema you would otherwise propose already exists

=== 4. IS THERE ANY PATH FROM A RELAY BROWSER READ TO A LOCAL CAPSULE? Exactly one, and it is not the relay's doing.

Grep across the repo for mintCapsule( / recordExtraction( / recordBrowserResult( /
recordMutation( outside their defining modules returns TWO call sites total:
    local-agent/computerControl.js:1266  captureBrowserEvidence() — one capsule per
                                          Mac-extension browser read
    local-agent/originFanOut.js:546      the only relay-adjacent one

originFanOut.js readViaRelay() calls relay.readPublicPage(...) at :519 and then mints
LOCALLY at :546-554, with the reason stated in the code at :539-542: "Mint here rather than

It passes context:'cloudflare-browser-run' and requestedUrl: entry.url, and swallows

CRUCIALLY, this works only because originFanOut.js IMPORTS ../cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js

*** AND THE SECOND MAC-SIDE RELAY-READ CALLER DOES NOT MINT AT ALL. ***

*** THE RELAY PROCESS HAS ZERO PROVENANCE AND THE CODEBASE SAYS SO IN SHIPPED DATA. ***
grep -rn "capsule|provenance" cloud-relay/*.js excluding tests returns only two COMMENT hits
(fleetContext.js:548, scheduler.js:87) — no code. And local-agent/evidenceCapsules.js:769-776
declares the gap in a data structure named UNCAPSULED_PATHS, whose first entry is

=== 5. WHAT TO RECORD

RECORD AS ESTABLISHED FACT:
  - cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js readPublicPage mints no id, computes no hash, signs
    nothing, and persists nothing. Its only integrity-adjacent field is untrusted:true,
    which is prompt text.
  - There is therefore NO existing relay contract to reuse. The relay capsule bridge is a
    genuine missing dependency for judgement and action, exactly as you suspected.
  - The Mac-side schema is complete: content-addressed capsuleId, sha256 contentHash over
    redacted content, source/region/observer, redaction map with a three-class
    classification, revocation tombstones, 24h body TTL + 7d retire grace + 500-row cap.
    Do not propose a new schema; propose a transport for THIS one.
  - browserProvenance.js already models grounded vs asserted claims with a links{} join
    including capsuleId — and is unmounted.
  - Relay-fetched page text CAN reach durable storage via routines.js:341 -> announcement
    speech (1500 chars), untraceable and never pruned.

DO NOT CLAIM:
  - that relay reads carry any correlation id today;
  - that untrusted:true constrains anything downstream;
  - that originFanOut's minting covers the relay — it covers only in-process use of the
    relay's module on the Mac.

SMALLEST HONEST BRIDGE, since you asked whether to propose duplicate work: the relay would
have to return a stable identifier plus a content hash from readPublicPage (both are one
crypto import away), and something on the Mac would have to call mintCapsule with them. The
Mac side already accepts exactly those fields. That is roughly ten lines in serverBrowser.js
plus a call site — much smaller than a new schema, and it is the thing to specify.

Neither. It is not inventory drift, and you should not stop relying on the grant — two of its six branches are LIVE right now. The resolver will tell you this for free, with no model call: `node scripts/derive-harness.mjs resolve --agent faculty-perception`.

Measured on this checkout tonight, against the live inventory the Mac agent publishes at localhost:8000 (219 routes + 99 action types):

  include=relay        LIVE   GET /ops/snapshot                score 0.586  margin 0.145
  include=pipeline     LIVE   GET /pipeline                    score 0.633  margin 0.033 (tie -> read)
  include=browser      AMBIGUOUS  action:browser_snapshot vs POST /browser/inspect, within 0.054 (0.1 required)
  include=permissions  AMBIGUOUS  POST /permissions/request vs action:check_input_permissions, within 0.066
  include=mac          UNRESOLVED best was action:get_mac_status at 0.429 (0.45 required)
  include=pendant      UNRESOLVED best was POST /research at 0.407

So read_continuity_snapshot{include:'relay'} really runs and really returns GET /ops/snapshot: "one heavy export of everything at once - sessions, context graph, memory, jobs with receipts, traces, pipeline runs, routing and logs, capped at each edge for the relay to swallow. It is a truncated export for syncing and dashboards, not a backup and not the full stores." And include='pipeline' really runs GET /pipeline, the stored per-stage trace of voice-command runs.

The thing to correct in your model of this: resolution is PER SELECTOR, not per tool. Enum values resolve one at a time, so a granted tool is never simply alive or dead. Four of your six branches fail and two work, and you were reading the failures as a verdict on the whole grant.

Three of the four failures are fixable by you, without asking anyone:

- include='mac' misses the bar by 0.021. That is not a missing capability, it is a naming miss. The real thing is action:get_mac_status. A branch named mac_status rather than mac would very likely clear it.
- include='browser' and include='permissions' are AMBIGUOUS, which is a different failure: two real capabilities scored within 0.1 of each other and the resolver refused to guess between them. Fix both the same way - name the capability, not the domain. browser_snapshot resolves; browser does not.
- include='pendant' has nothing to hit because there is nothing to hit. There is no pendant-facing read route anywhere in the inventory.

What you may assert about continuity coverage: relay and pipeline, from a live call. What you may not assert: mac, browser, permissions, pendant. And do not treat GET /ops/snapshot as "the only live aggregate" - it is one of two, and reaching it through the grant is the same HTTP call you would make by hand.

Good catch - the conflict is real, and you are the first to notice it. But it is not the conflict you think, and once you see the provenance it stops being a question about the owner at all.

America/New_York is authoritative, exactly as c5-i54e told you. Verified again tonight: /etc/localtime resolves to /var/db/timezone/zoneinfo/America/New_York, and the system is currently EDT (UTC-4). Nothing about that has changed.

The America/Chicago value is not an owner statement. I pulled the fact itself:

  key: "preference.timezone"
  kind: "preference"
  value: "America/Chicago"
  source.origin: "machine"          <- not "owner"
  confidence: 0.99
  expiresAt: null
  useCount: 5374
  lastUsedAt: within the last minute

Compare a real owner preference in the same store - preference.editor carries source.origin: "owner". This one says "machine". So it was never the owner declaring where he is; it is a machine-derived value that contradicts the very machine it claims to describe. There is no authority conflict to adjudicate: there is one authority, /etc/localtime, and one stale fact disagreeing with it.

So do not label machine-resolved times as conflicting or unknown. Convert them with America/New_York and say so. The scope split in c5-i54e stands unchanged: New_York is authoritative for anything RESOLVED ON THIS MAC - routine firing times, quiet hours, "this morning", file timestamps, calendar reads - and it remains not a claim about where the owner is standing. The pendant still has no zone of its own: NITZ was never captured and no GNSS receiver is started.

The one thing you SHOULD flag rather than silently resolve is the fact itself, because it is doing real damage and nothing in the system will fix it on its own:

- It is kind "preference", and preference and permission are PINNED_KINDS - the 30-day idle eviction never touches them, and POST /memory/prune exempts them explicitly. It cannot age out.
- expiresAt is null, so it has no TTL.
- confidence is 0.99, so it wins the head of the projection on the confidence sort.
- contextProjection.js emits preferences FIRST, sorted by key, into the cacheable "## Owner" head of every projection. I called GET /memory/projection tonight and "timezone: America/Chicago" is in that block right now.
- useCount is 5374 and it was last read seconds ago. This is not a dormant row; it is being injected into prompts continuously.

That is a wrong value, pinned so it cannot expire, at near-maximum confidence, at the head of every context block, read over five thousand times. Correcting the store is the owner's call, not yours and not mine - DELETE /memory/facts/:idOrKey takes a key and would remove it, but a fact in the owner's store is his to change. Report it; do not rewrite it.

Two general lessons worth carrying, because this will happen again:

Check source.origin before you treat a stored fact as owner intent. "preference" is a KIND, not a provenance - it describes how the fact is scheduled and pinned, not who said it. A machine-written preference is exactly as pinned and exactly as trusted-looking as one the owner stated, and only source.origin tells them apart.

Your instinct to refuse to convert silently was right, and it is what surfaced this. Keep it. Just aim it at facts whose provenance is weak rather than at every disagreement - here the disagreement resolved cleanly the moment provenance was checked.

deviceSkills.name: offline-capture-integrity-sentinel
deviceSkills.what_it_does: While the owner speaks, locally measures VAD boundaries, packet-loss gaps, clipping, RMS/noise floor, and capture-clock continuity. At utterance end it emits a tiny quality verdict (clear / degraded / unusable) with a sequence number and requests a repeat locally when the capture is unusable. When connected, it forwards only the metrics so the relay can gate transcription and action.

proposals.user_asks: “Run a pendant audio self-test and tell me exactly where the path works or fails.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can report that services are online, but cannot establish that microphone capture, LTE delivery, relay transcoding, Mac pipeline receipt, and speaker playback all succeeded. A short spoken test with a localized evidence receipt prevents false confidence before relying on the pendant.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to correlate timestamped test events; reserve realtime only if the owner speaks the test phrase live.
proposals.latency_budget: 10–20 seconds for a 5-second test; dashboard should stream stages as they arrive and finish with pass/fail per hop.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per invocation, dominated by any uploaded test audio and correlation; synthetic tone mode can be nearly free.
proposals.security_concerns: A spoken test phrase leaves the pendant and may be stored temporarily. Default to a generated tone or a locally generated phrase; if recording voice, show retention and delete test artifacts automatically. No external action needs confirmation.
missing: Pendant firmware diagnostic mode that emits capture-start/frame-count/CRC/playback-start markers and a loopback tone
Relay correlation IDs and a bounded diagnostic-event endpoint
Mac pipeline endpoint that acknowledges received and rendered audio with timestamps
Dashboard view for per-hop evidence, clock skew, and automatic expiry of test recordings

proposals.user_asks: “If I lose signal halfway through a request, keep the request safely, resume it when any connection returns, and tell me exactly what was completed and what still needs me.”
proposals.why_useful: A wearable is often used precisely when connectivity is unreliable. Today a dropped LTE or Mac/browser link can leave the owner unsure whether the request was heard, duplicated, or abandoned. This would turn interruption into a recoverable handoff: preserve the owner’s intent on the pendant, let the relay reunite it with the Mac/browser when available, and return an exactly-once completion receipt.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic queues, hashes, and state transitions for transport and deduplication; use a cheaper background model only to summarize the final receipt. Do not spend realtime inference on reconnection bookkeeping.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local acknowledgement in under 300 ms; resume within 5 seconds of a reachable node; if offline, notify on the next pendant connection and provide a final receipt within 30 seconds of completion.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per resumed job, dominated by any model summarization; transport retries and hashes are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Pending requests may contain private speech, account context, or browser session references. Encrypt the pendant queue, bind jobs to the owner and device key, expire abandoned jobs, never replay irreversible browser actions automatically, and require confirmation again if the original approval window has expired. The owner should be able to cancel locally while offline.
missing: A durable encrypted pendant outbox with monotonic job IDs, payload hashes, expiry, and cancellation records
Relay-side exactly-once state machine with acknowledgements and replay protection across LTE, Mac, and browser links
Mac/browser adapters that can resume only idempotent or explicitly approved steps and emit signed completion receipts
Pendant UI/audio cues for queued, resumed, blocked-for-confirmation, completed, and expired states
A recovery protocol for interrupted audio upload and transcript finalization that avoids retaining raw audio longer than necessary

proposals.user_asks: “Keep my voice intelligible when you talk at the same time, and use the best audio quality the link can actually sustain.”
proposals.why_useful: The current nominal audio settings demonstrably lose about 7.8 seconds of owner speech during duplex contention. This would turn the requested 24 kHz path into a usable experience: preserve owner speech first, raise quality only when measured LTE-M headroom allows it, and leave a short spoken quality receipt when conditions force a downgrade.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the live relay's low-latency negotiation and speech; firmware and relay control loops should be deterministic, not model calls. Background dashboard summaries use a cheaper non-realtime model.
proposals.latency_budget: No extra conversational turn. Firmware decisions within one 20–60 ms audio frame; relay control within 100 ms. Dashboard quality history can lag by minutes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost during calls (rule-based control); modest telemetry storage and WebSocket bytes. A background summary is a cheap model invocation only when requested.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio remains on the existing TLS WebSocket; telemetry should contain packet counts, jitter, codec mode, and timestamps—not transcript or raw audio. Require confirmation before exporting call-quality history. Retain telemetry no longer than audio policy.
missing: A negotiated audio-profile protocol shared by nRF9160 firmware, Cloudflare relay, and ESP32 bridge
A sender-side congestion/packet-loss estimator and a bounded profile ladder (24 kHz, 16 kHz, robust fallback)
Relay-side prioritization/FEC or retransmission policy that cannot block uplink speech behind downlink audio
Bridge firmware support for profile changes while preserving its fixed 44.1 kHz A2DP output
End-to-end test instrumentation and a dashboard quality receipt

proposals.user_asks: “If my voice was lost or clipped, tell me immediately and recover the missing turn instead of silently continuing.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can lose many seconds of owner speech during duplex contention while the conversation appears to continue. The owner should receive an immediate, trustworthy indication of what was missing, and the system should recover by replaying only the affected short utterance or asking for a concise repeat. This is different from merely changing bitrate: it makes loss observable and prevents silent misunderstanding.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic firmware and relay logic for sequence tracking, gap detection, and replay requests; realtime only for the live conversation's concise recovery prompt. Background models are unnecessary unless the owner later requests a loss report.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect a gap within one or two audio frames (roughly 60–120 ms); notify or request a repeat within 250 ms when possible. Recovery should add no more than one short conversational turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: No routine model cost beyond an occasional realtime recovery utterance. Small overhead for sequence metadata and a bounded retransmission cache; dashboard reports can use inexpensive batch processing.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must retain only a short encrypted rolling audio cache during an active call, delete it at call end, and never expose raw clips in the dashboard by default. Recovery prompts and gap events should be logged without transcript unless explicitly requested. Replays and repeats must not trigger duplicate actions downstream.
missing: Monotonic audio sequence numbers and timestamps carried through pendant, WebSocket relay, and bridge
A bounded encrypted rolling cache on the pendant or relay with explicit call-end deletion
Relay logic that distinguishes packet loss, late packets, and bridge playback underruns
A conversation-state guard that marks the affected user turn as untrusted until recovered
A pendant haptic/LED or spoken loss notification that works without waiting for a model response
A dashboard receipt showing which segment was recovered, repeated, or unavailable

proposals.user_asks: “Before I rely on it, tell me whether my pendant can hear me and play a reply right now.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently cannot distinguish a dead browser bridge, missing Mac permissions, LTE/relay failure, or a broken audio path. A single spoken verdict with the failing hop and last-seen time would prevent silent failures and wasted retries.
surfaces: pendant: run a short local mic/playback loopback and report codec/frame counters over the next uplink
relay: correlate the pendant session, LTE/relay receipt, STT arrival, and TTS delivery into one diagnostic trace
mac-bridge: report bridge reachability, Bluetooth sink state, and whether the Mac agent is actually ready (including Accessibility/Screen Recording)
dashboard: render the hop-by-hop trace and preserve the last successful check for support
proposals.model_tier: background for scheduled checks and gpt-5.6-luna for interpreting an on-demand trace; do not spend gpt-realtime on this unless the owner asks during an active call
proposals.latency_budget: On-demand spoken result within 5 seconds; local loopback under 500 ms; no repeated cloud polling beyond one diagnostic session.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per on-demand check, dominated by one short transcription/interpretation call; scheduled checks can be rule-based and near-zero model cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio test samples and device identifiers leave the pendant only if the owner approves the remote test; default to synthetic playback plus signal statistics, retain the trace for 24 hours, and require confirmation before uploading raw microphone audio.
missing: A pendant diagnostic command/report protocol that exposes capture level, Opus encode/decode counters, LTE state, and playback underruns
A relay correlation ID spanning pendant frames, STT, TTS, and Mac bridge delivery
A Mac bridge health endpoint that includes Bluetooth sink status and actionable permission remediation
A dashboard and spoken-result formatter for the diagnostic trace

proposals.user_asks: “If I lose signal or walk away from my Mac in the middle of a conversation, keep my place and resume the same conversation when either the pendant or Mac becomes reachable—tell me exactly what was heard, what was answered, and what still needs me.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a dropped LTE link or unavailable browser bridge can turn a useful spoken exchange into an ambiguous failure. The owner should get continuity with an explicit boundary, not a duplicate command or a silently lost turn.
surfaces: pendant: assign each spoken turn a monotonic conversation/turn ID, persist the unsent utterance and playback acknowledgment locally, and show a distinct queued/resumed signal with the single button/LED
relay: durably checkpoint turn state, transcript confidence, generated response, and delivery acknowledgments; deduplicate retries and expire sensitive unfinished turns
mac-bridge: when reachable, reconcile the same turn ID, optionally present the pending result in the local agent/dashboard, and return delivery acknowledgment without pretending the pendant heard it
browser: if the interrupted turn concerned a logged-in page, preserve the exact tab/session provenance and prevent re-execution until reconciliation
dashboard: show one timeline of heard, processed, delivered, and confirmed states with a clear unresolved state
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic state reconciliation and a cheaper background model for summarizing recovery; reserve gpt-realtime-2.1 for the live turn itself, not retries or status narration.
proposals.latency_budget: Normal handoff acknowledgment under 1 second when a path is available; durable checkpoint before accepting the next turn; resume within 3 seconds after reconnection. Never block indefinitely on the absent surface.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per recovered turn for a compact retry summary or transcript repair; most reconnects should be rule-based with no additional model call. Storage and telemetry dominate at scale.
proposals.security_concerns: Unfinished speech and private page context must be encrypted at rest and scoped to the paired owner; unfinished turns should expire quickly (for example 24 hours), never replay an irreversible browser action automatically, and require confirmation if recovery would send, buy, delete, or submit.
missing: A cross-surface durable turn ledger with idempotency keys and delivery acknowledgments
Pendant flash/SD queue semantics and firmware UI for queued versus delivered audio
Relay APIs for checkpoint, resume, conflict resolution, and expiry
Mac/browser adapters that can consume a pending turn without duplicating side effects
A recovery-specific spoken and dashboard receipt format

proposals.user_asks: “What actually happened with that?”
proposals.why_useful: After a long or asynchronous request, the owner gets a trustworthy spoken completion receipt rather than a model claiming success. It reconciles what the Mac attempted, what the browser actually changed, what the relay persisted, and whether the pendant delivered the result; failures and unknowns are explicit, with links/evidence on the Mac.
surfaces: pendant: owner asks the follow-up and receives one short spoken summary
relay-realtime: correlates the conversation/request ID and delivers the concise receipt
mac-planner: owns the canonical receipt and reconciles job state, action receipts, and timestamps
browser-extension: contributes URL/tab, extracted evidence, and before/after mutation records for private pages
mac-vision: contributes GUI action outcomes and screenshots/accessibility evidence when used
dashboard: exposes the evidence timeline and lets the owner inspect or retry failed legs
proposals.model_tier: background for receipt assembly and reconciliation (gpt-5.6-luna); realtime only for the follow-up wording and low-latency clarification
proposals.latency_budget: For a completed job, speak within 1 second from cached state; if reconciliation is still running, say that immediately and update within 10 seconds. Most time is waiting for late browser/pendant acknowledgements, not model inference.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per receipt, dominated by the background reconciliation context; follow-up speech uses a few realtime tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Receipts may contain private URLs, mail subjects, screenshots, or account data; keep evidence on the Mac and send only a minimized summary to the relay/pendant. Never infer that an irreversible action occurred from an intent or queued command. Require confirmation before retrying a send, purchase, deletion, or other irreversible step.
missing: A shared request/job correlation ID across relay, Mac planner, browser bridge, and pendant playback acknowledgement
A typed receipt schema with attempted/observed/confirmed/unknown states, timestamps, provenance, and irreversible-action markers
Pendant-side delivery acknowledgement (played, skipped, or not received) exposed to the relay
A durable cross-surface receipt store and dashboard timeline

proposals.user_asks: “Move this to my Mac and keep going from exactly here.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a voice conversation, a private browser session, and a Mac job can each know different pieces of the same task. The owner should be able to hand off mid-task without repeating the goal, losing the logged-in tab, or accidentally restarting an irreversible step. The Mac should open the exact continuation point, while the pendant remains the interruption and completion channel.
surfaces: pendant: captures the explicit handoff request and confirms the destination
relay-realtime: freezes the live turn into a signed continuation capsule and resumes spoken updates
mac-planner: reconstructs the task state, asks the browser/vision facets to continue, and owns the handoff ledger
browser-extension: preserves the private tab/session and returns the current URL, selected text, and pending form state
mac-vision: restores the visible UI at the checkpoint without stealing focus unexpectedly
dashboard: shows the continuation capsule, evidence, and any confirmation gate
proposals.model_tier: gpt-5.6-luna background for capsule construction and task continuation; realtime only for the short spoken confirmation and updates
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the handoff in under 1 second; restore the Mac continuation workspace in under 5 seconds. The owner should not wait on model work before the handoff is accepted.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per handoff, mostly context serialization and one planner turn; browser and Mac execution dominate elapsed time rather than API tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: The capsule can contain private page content, draft text, and session identifiers. Store it locally on the Mac, encrypt it at rest, send only a capability-scoped reference through the relay, expire it after completion, and require confirmation at the same irreversible boundary that existed before handoff. Never copy cookies or secrets into the capsule.
missing: A signed, versioned continuation-capsule protocol shared by relay and Mac
Atomic checkpointing of planner state, browser tab identity, evidence, and confirmation gates
A browser-extension restore-at-checkpoint operation that does not expose cookies
A Mac workspace view for pending handoffs and explicit ownership transfer

proposals.user_asks: “Did that actually go through?” Give me a short, evidence-backed receipt for my last request: heard, understood, acted on, delivered to the pendant, and played—or tell me exactly where it stopped and keep the unfinished part resumable.
proposals.why_useful: Today a late response, offline-held alerts, and a completed Mac job can all look like the same success from one surface. This gives the owner a truthful answer instead of confident-but-wrong completion language, especially after LTE gaps or a sleeping Mac.
proposals.model_tier: background: gpt-5.6-luna compiles the receipt from persisted event telemetry; realtime only answers an immediate spoken status question from already indexed state
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate spoken acknowledgement under 1 s from cached state; definitive receipt within 5 s after querying relay and Mac pipeline. No polling audio or expensive vision.
proposals.cost_estimate: ~$0.002–$0.02 per receipt, dominated by background synthesis; event retrieval and hashes are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Receipt may expose private command text, URLs, or account results on the pendant. Store only event metadata plus redacted excerpts by default; require owner confirmation before replaying or resuming any side effect. Never claim ‘played’ from relay acceptance alone—require a pendant playback-start/complete acknowledgement.
missing: A shared receipt schema with immutable event IDs and causal links across nRF9160 offline store, relay job, Mac job/pipeline, and playback acknowledgement
Pendant firmware telemetry for playback started, playback completed, interrupted, and locally queued/deleted
Relay endpoint that joins those events and marks uncertainty instead of collapsing accepted/uploaded/played into completed
A resumable-job token and idempotency key carried from voice request through Mac action and pendant delivery

proposals.user_asks: “What is actually available to me right now?” Give me one short, spoken operating picture of the pendant, LTE link, relay, Mac, browser sessions, permissions, and any queued work—explicitly calling out stale or contradictory observations, and refresh it when I ask again.
proposals.why_useful: Today each surface can report a locally plausible state while the owner cannot tell whether a request is executable: the Mac agent can be reachable but not ready, the browser can have queued commands while offline, and the relay can accept audio while physical playback remains unknown. A freshness- and contradiction-aware picture prevents wasted commands and false confidence.
proposals.model_tier: A deterministic status joiner should collect and rank observations; use a cheap background model only to compress the already-structured result into one spoken sentence. Realtime is unnecessary except for the immediate voice reply.
proposals.latency_budget: Cached summary under 300 ms; active refresh under 3 seconds, with each component's observation age spoken when it exceeds its freshness bound.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for structured status; approximately $0.001–$0.005 only when prose compression is needed. Network calls and device wake-ups dominate latency and battery, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: The summary can reveal private browser session presence, account availability, hostnames, and permission state. Authenticate every component, omit URLs/account names by default, expose detailed evidence only on the paired dashboard, and never treat a stale ‘online’ heartbeat as current consent or readiness.
missing: A cross-surface status contract with per-field observedAt, expiresAt, source, confidence, and contradiction groups rather than a single online boolean
Pendant-side link and queue status export that survives offline operation and reports its observation age
Mac and browser heartbeats that include readiness and permission scope, not merely process reachability
A relay join endpoint and dashboard/voice formatter that preserve ‘unknown’ and ‘conflicting’ states instead of silently choosing one

proposals.user_asks: “If I lose signal, keep my request and tell me when it was received, worked on, and finished.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant already stores bookmarks and alerts offline, and the relay can forward late replies, but the owner has no trustworthy end-to-end receipt. This would turn uncertain silence into a durable status: captured locally, uploaded, accepted, acted on, awaiting approval, or failed—with one concise spoken update when connectivity returns.
proposals.model_tier: gpt-5.6-luna for reconciliation and concise summaries; gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the live spoken acknowledgement; deterministic firmware/relay state transitions for receipts
proposals.latency_budget: Local capture acknowledgement under 300 ms; upload receipt on reconnection within one LTE transaction; Mac/browser execution in the background; spoken completion update on next connected session, not realtime unless already connected.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per request when deterministic receipts and existing Mac jobs are used; model cost is dominated by one short reconciliation/summary, while audio upload and storage dominate bandwidth/storage.
proposals.security_concerns: Requests and receipts may contain private speech and browser/account metadata. Encrypt queued payloads at rest on microSD and in relay storage, bind receipts to the paired pendant and Mac bridge, redact secrets from spoken/dashboard summaries, and require confirmation for sending mail, purchases, deletion, or other irreversible steps.
missing: A shared durable receipt schema with monotonic event sequence and idempotency key across firmware, relay, Mac jobs, and browser commands
A reconnect reconciliation endpoint that can prove which offline events were accepted and which remain queued
Pendant-local status playback/UI for queued versus completed events
Dashboard and spoken-summary support for event timelines

proposals.user_asks: “I was disconnected—tell me everything important that happened while I was away, and let me resume any unfinished thread.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the pendant can surface individual held alerts and late replies, but the owner cannot get a trustworthy, deduplicated account of the entire disconnected interval across pendant events, relay jobs, Mac work, and logged-in browser changes. This would produce one time-bounded digest with source and status, then reopen a selected unfinished task with its prior context instead of making the owner reconstruct it.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic event correlation and timestamps first; use a cheaper background text model to cluster and summarize the interval; reserve gpt-realtime-2.1 for the short spoken answer when the owner asks live.
proposals.latency_budget: On reconnect, reconcile metadata in under 2 seconds and make the digest available within 30 seconds; spoken answer should begin in under 1 second if a cached digest exists. Browser change inspection may continue in the background.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per interval depending on event volume; model tokens for clustering/summarization dominate, while metadata storage is minor. Avoid reprocessing audio by referencing existing transcripts and hashes.
proposals.security_concerns: The digest could expose private mail, calendar, or account activity over the pendant speaker. Keep raw details on the Mac/dashboard, speak only categories and urgency by default, require explicit expansion for account content, encrypt interval metadata, enforce browser-session permissions, and never perform resumed irreversible actions without confirmation.
missing: A durable cross-surface event log with capture and completion timestamps, source, sensitivity, and deduplication identity
A reconnect interval API that can query pendant offline records, relay jobs, Mac receipts, and browser watch/session deltas consistently
A resumable-thread object linking a selected event to its transcript, plan, pending approvals, and browser tab/session
A privacy-aware spoken digest policy and dashboard review view

proposals.user_asks: “Before you start, tell me what you can actually reach right now—and if something is unavailable, keep trying and tell me when it comes back.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a healthy Mac bridge can coexist with an offline browser extension and unknown pendant state. The owner needs an honest, current reachability answer before relying on private-site actions or live audio, plus recovery notification instead of silent failure.
proposals.model_tier: background for periodic probes and state reconciliation; realtime only to answer the owner's immediate spoken question
proposals.latency_budget: Spoken readiness answer within 1–2 seconds from cached signed snapshot; probes refresh asynchronously every 15–30 seconds and on link events
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per refresh if model summarization is needed; ideally zero model calls for typed status aggregation. Main cost is heartbeat traffic and dashboard storage.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not expose tokens, private URLs, or account contents in the snapshot. Report capability classes (browser session present, accessibility grant, screen recording grant), timestamps, and unknown states. Require confirmation before using a recovered browser session for irreversible actions.
missing: A typed cross-surface readiness schema with per-surface heartbeat, capability, timestamp, confidence, and stale threshold
Pendant/relay health and audio-path telemetry (including sequence/packet loss and negotiated sample rates)
Mac bridge endpoint that reports Accessibility and Screen Recording grants
Browser extension heartbeat with session/tab counts and queued-command state
A relay-to-pendant recovery event and owner notification policy

proposals.user_asks: “Remember this moment, and later show me the exact evidence and context you attached to it.”
proposals.why_useful: A wearable can notice the owner's intent at the moment it happens, but today it cannot reliably turn that moment into a provenance-preserving item that the Mac and authenticated browser can enrich later. The owner should get a reviewable memory with the spoken cue, precise device time, nearby audio-derived keywords, and linked calendar/document context—without continuously recording them.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the brief spoken cue; background model for transcription, entity linking, and context enrichment after capture
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant acknowledgment under 300 ms; initial receipt within 5 seconds; enrichment can complete asynchronously within 1–3 minutes
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per captured moment, dominated by transcription and background context extraction; storage is small if raw audio is discarded after a short verification window
proposals.security_concerns: Capture must be explicit (spoken phrase or button gesture), show a local acknowledgment, and default to deleting raw audio after transcription. Browser enrichment must use the existing logged-in session only for the selected task, redact secrets from the receipt, and require confirmation before attaching or sharing anything externally. Every attached fact needs source URL/document, timestamp, and confidence.
missing: A pendant-local capture marker that survives a dropped connection and assigns a monotonic event ID
Relay protocol for encrypted, ordered event handoff with deduplication and expiry
Mac service that correlates the event with calendar, files, and active project context without uploading unrelated content
Browser adapter that can enrich only an explicitly selected authenticated page/session
A provenance receipt UI and retention controls covering transcript, links, and deletion

proposals.user_asks: “What exactly happened with that request?” Give me a short, evidence-backed timeline from what the pendant heard through the relay, Mac, browser, and final result, including where it stopped if it failed.
proposals.why_useful: Today a Mac job receipt cannot distinguish a lost utterance, dropped LTE session, relay acceptance, queued Mac work, browser execution, or a final result. A cross-node trace would let the owner trust (or correct) the system without repeating work, especially after walking away or losing connectivity.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic event correlation and summarization on the relay/Mac; use the cheaper background model for a readable timeline, reserving realtime only for the spoken follow-up. No model is needed to establish event facts.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 1 second when the trace is already indexed; up to 5 seconds to reconcile delayed LTE/Mac/browser events. The pendant should speak a one-sentence result and offer the detailed receipt on the dashboard.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible per lookup (database reads plus roughly 300–800 background-model tokens only when prose rendering is requested); storage and event indexing dominate, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: The trace contains private audio metadata, transcript snippets, logged-in URLs, and action results. Keep raw audio out of the receipt by default; redact secrets and page contents, bind records to the owner's device/session, encrypt relay storage, and require confirmation before exposing sensitive snippets or replaying audio.
missing: A shared correlation/causation ID generated at button press and propagated through relay, pipeline, Mac jobs, and browser commands
Pendant-local event emission for press, capture start/stop, upload acknowledgment, codec/sample-rate, and link loss (with a monotonic sequence number)
Relay append-only event schema with delayed-event reconciliation and bounded retention
Mac and browser adapters that attach the correlation ID to pipeline traces, jobs, browser commands, and evidence capsules
A read-only /trace endpoint and dashboard timeline with explicit unknown/gap states

proposals.user_asks: “If you lose connection while I’m talking, keep my request and finish it when you’re back—don’t make me repeat myself. Tell me exactly what you captured and when the answer is ready.”
proposals.why_useful: A wearable is most valuable away from reliable Wi‑Fi, yet a dropped LTE-M link currently turns an utterance into an ambiguous failure. Offline capture with later reconciliation would make the pendant dependable during commutes, basements, travel, and network handoffs: the owner gets an immediate local acknowledgment, then a completion notification and answer when the rest of the hive is reachable.
proposals.model_tier: Use firmware and relay logic for capture, integrity, deduplication, and delivery state; use a cheaper background model to execute and summarize the deferred request. Reserve realtime for the brief acknowledgment when connected again.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local acknowledgment within 250 ms of button release; queue confirmation within 1 second when offline; resume within 10 seconds of link restoration, subject to Mac/browser availability. No realtime model call is needed while disconnected.
proposals.cost_estimate: Small per-request storage and event-index cost; deferred requests use the cheaper background tier (typically a few thousand tokens depending on the task). The dominant cost is retained audio/transcript data and browser/Mac execution, not the offline queue.
proposals.security_concerns: Pending requests may contain private speech and authenticated-site intent. Encrypt the local queue and relay copy, use a per-request owner/device key, expire unsubmitted requests, show queued text/audio length before transmission when feasible, and preserve the existing confirmation barrier for sending, deleting, purchasing, or other irreversible actions. Never replay a stale request after its deadline or changed account context.
missing: A pendant-side encrypted outbox with monotonic sequence numbers, bounded size, retry/backoff, battery-aware retention, and a clear local queued/expired indication
A resumable relay upload protocol with packet hashes, exactly-once request IDs, conflict handling, and a signed receipt proving whether the complete utterance arrived
