The owner loses the relationship between what they were viewing, what they asked the relay to do, and what the Mac was changing. This gives them a true pause/resume boundary across devices and outages without pretending old state is current.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic capture, hashing, redaction, and diffing; a cheaper text model may label the checkpoint. Use realtime only to answer the spoken resume request.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture in under 3 seconds; resume preview in under 2 seconds, with restoration requiring explicit confirmation per action.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low API cost: local state reads and content hashes dominate; at most 1–2k tokens to summarize a checkpoint. Storage is bounded metadata plus redacted capsule bodies.
proposals.security_concerns: Never checkpoint passwords, cookies, raw audio, or secret page bodies. Encrypt the checkpoint at rest, bind restoration to the original owner/device trust, and require confirmation before opening apps, navigating, or mutating files. A checkpoint must label unavailable or expired sources rather than silently replay them.
missing: A cross-surface checkpoint schema that joins browser capsule IDs, Mac action-ledger state, relay job/context IDs, and pendant health sequence
An atomic capture barrier or per-source sequence numbers so the checkpoint can prove which observations belong to the same instant
A restore planner that supports only reversible actions and produces a preflight diff; expired/revoked evidence must remain withheld
A durable encrypted store/transport so the checkpoint can move between the Mac, relay, and a future registered pendant

proposals.user_asks: "Put the pendant in guest mode for the next hour." Let another person use the physical device for basic conversation while preventing access to my memories, browser sessions, files, routines, and announcements; when guest mode ends, provide a signed audit of everything the guest could reach and revoke the temporary trust.
proposals.why_useful: A wearable is physically shareable, but today its identity and the owner's context are effectively fused. This lets the owner lend it safely, use it at a demo or in a household, and recover with confidence instead of handing over a live personal agent.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic capability isolation, scoped tokens, and audit logs; use a small model only to explain the resulting access report. Realtime is only the conversation surface.
proposals.latency_budget: Enter guest mode in under 2 seconds; revoke immediately on button press or timeout; produce the access report within 5 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low inference cost; dominant work is secure session/token management and bounded audit storage. No browser or Mac action should run unless explicitly granted to the guest session.
proposals.security_concerns: Guest audio and transcripts must be isolated and optionally discarded. Never inherit owner cookies, memory projection, files, or voice identity. Require a local physical gesture/PIN to enter and exit, use expiring least-privilege credentials, and make revocation work while offline with a local deny-list.
missing: A pendant-local guest/owner session boundary with an offline timeout and physical exit gesture
Relay credentials scoped to guest conversation only, with no access to owner memory, announcements, routines, or jobs
Mac and browser policy enforcement that rejects guest-originated actions and keeps owner sessions separate
A tamper-evident audit joining device session, relay calls, Mac/browser attempts, and revocation time

proposals.user_asks: "Make sure I actually get the spoken result, even when it is a long briefing." The system should hand off large audio without putting PCM into the relay's job/result record, verify each transfer, and tell me plainly if only the Mac rendered it.
proposals.why_useful: A live pipeline just failed after rendering 480,000 bytes of 24 kHz PCM: the bridge tried to persist a 62,301,439-byte serialized result and Cloudflare rejected it at 32 MiB. Today this can lose a perfectly good spoken briefing while the trace misleadingly contains a completed TTS stage. This capability makes long briefings dependable across Mac → relay → bridge → (when present) pendant, while preserving the honest distinction between rendered, transferred, and heard.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic streaming/chunk verification and existing job machinery; reserve realtime model only for the brief's language, not transport. No LLM is needed to move bytes or diagnose limits.
proposals.latency_budget: Start playback as soon as the first verified chunks are available; add under 1 second manifest setup and bounded chunk retries. A failed transfer should be reported immediately, not after the entire response is serialized.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost. Storage/network cost is proportional to audio (roughly 0.96 MB/minute for 24 kHz mono PCM before compression); chunk hashes and a small manifest dominate little.
proposals.security_concerns: Use per-job opaque IDs, authenticated chunk upload/download, short-lived manifests, SHA-256 and byte-range checks, and never log PCM or spoken secrets. Require confirmation only for external actions, not playback. Expire abandoned manifests and keep the owner's existing audio-retention policy.
missing: A streaming/chunked audio handoff contract that keeps PCM out of D1 job rows and bridge result RPC arguments
A relay/bridge receipt that records manifest, byte count, hash, and transfer completion separately from the text result
A Mac fallback that can play locally or retain a compact answer when the pendant is absent, rather than marking the run failed

proposals.user_asks: "If a scheduled briefing fails, recover it and tell me what happened without making me ask again." The system should detect a failed routine across the relay and Mac, preserve a compact text receipt, retry only the failed delivery leg, and give me a short spoken recovery notice when a device is available.
proposals.why_useful: The live morning-news routine rendered audio but ended with a failed pipeline because a 62 MB bridge result exceeded Cloudflare's 32 MiB RPC limit. The owner currently gets neither the briefing nor a trustworthy explanation; routine status can say completed at other stages while the final run is failed. This turns silent loss into one bounded recovery and an honest notice.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic failure classification and retry policy. Use a cheaper background model only if the compact text receipt must be re-summarized; do not spend realtime tokens on retries or transport diagnosis.
proposals.latency_budget: Classify within seconds of a failed pipeline event. Retry the delivery leg once after a short backoff; if it fails again, leave the compact receipt and speak one sentence on the next available connection.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually zero extra model calls; one retry may duplicate transfer bandwidth. If summarization is needed, under one cheap text call per failed run.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not retry destructive actions—only generated briefing delivery. Bind retries to an idempotency key and preserve source URLs/capsule IDs where available. Expire retained text/audio according to policy; do not put raw PCM in job records.
missing: A failure classifier that distinguishes content-generation failure from audio-transfer/storage failure
An idempotent delivery-only retry endpoint and a durable compact text receipt separate from audio bytes
A next-connection notification policy that does not claim the owner heard the original failed delivery

proposals.user_asks: "Watch this page and tell me only what materially changed since yesterday, with the exact before-and-after evidence." The system should maintain a user-approved watch over a browser page, detect semantic changes rather than cosmetic ones, and deliver a concise spoken alert with citations and a way to inspect the old and new regions.
proposals.why_useful: Today the browser can read the current tab, and the Mac can store individual evidence capsules, but the owner cannot ask the system to establish a durable, cross-session change claim. A page can change between visits and the system has no owner-facing before/after witness, so an alert would be an unsupported summary rather than perception grounded in two observations.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic content-addressed snapshots, DOM/region normalization, and hashes for change detection. Use a cheap background model only to classify whether a diff is materially relevant; use realtime only to speak an already-verified alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture and compare on the watch schedule, typically under 10 seconds after the page is available. Alert generation should be under 2 seconds after a confirmed material diff; no continuous realtime inference.
proposals.cost_estimate: Browser capture and hashing are negligible. Background classification is one small text-model call per changed region, not per poll. Storage is bounded by retaining redacted region summaries and hashes rather than whole pages.
proposals.security_concerns: The owner must explicitly approve each watched URL/region. Redact secrets and authenticated-page fields before persistence; never send page bodies to the relay unless the watch policy permits it. Use revocable watch IDs, encrypted local storage, retention limits, and require confirmation before following links or acting on a change.
missing: A durable watch object linking URL, region selector, cadence, owner policy, and last accepted capsule
A semantic diff engine that compares redacted content-addressed capsules while distinguishing cosmetic layout changes from material text/data changes
A scheduler-to-browser capture path that can reacquire the watched tab or request a fresh authenticated browser read
An alert receipt containing old/new capsule IDs, changed claims, confidence, and source timestamps

proposals.user_asks: "Keep working on that question after I walk away, and bring me back the answer with the sources you actually checked." The pendant should create a bounded research handoff, the relay should preserve the task and its evidence requirements, the Mac/browser should continue it asynchronously, and the next available device should receive a compact result with unresolved parts clearly separated.
proposals.why_useful: Today a spoken request, a relay job, a Mac planner run, and a browser read are separate records. The owner cannot leave with a half-formed question and later receive a verifiable continuation: there is no durable task identity that carries the owner's constraints, partial findings, source evidence, and unanswered subquestions across the wearable, relay, Mac, and browser.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background planner for decomposition, retrieval, and reconciliation; reserve realtime only for the initial handoff and final spoken delivery. Deterministic IDs and evidence joins should do the continuity work, not an LLM transcript recap.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the handoff in one spoken turn. Background work may take minutes; when complete, queue a short result and make the full evidence available on the Mac. Do not block the pendant on research.
proposals.cost_estimate: One background planning call plus retrieval/model calls proportional to the number of subquestions; typically far cheaper than keeping realtime active. Storage is small task metadata plus bounded evidence references.
proposals.security_concerns: The owner must explicitly choose whether authenticated browser pages may be used. Scope credentials to the browser session, redact secrets from task summaries, bind every claim to a capsule or source URL, and require confirmation before any external action discovered during research.
missing: A durable cross-surface research-task record with owner constraints, expiry, priority, and partial-result states
A handoff protocol from pendant speech to relay job to Mac/browser work that preserves one task ID and deduplicates retries
A claim-level evidence join so every returned statement distinguishes observed, inferred, and unresolved
A completion policy that queues the result without claiming it was heard

proposals.user_asks: "Answer only with what you can verify right now; label anything inferred or stale." The system should run a live evidence gate across the Mac, browser, relay, and (when connected) pendant before speaking, attach freshness and provenance to each factual claim, and refuse to turn a missing observation into a confident sentence.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can expose raw status and historical traces, but a spoken answer can still blend current observations, cached memory, machine-derived preferences, and inferred completion without telling the owner which is which. The owner needs a deliberate reality mode for high-stakes questions: a short verified answer, an explicit unknown, and a reason for the gap rather than plausible narration.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic freshness/provenance gates and source-specific policies first. Use a small text model only to compress verified evidence into speech; realtime is needed only for the interactive request, not evidence collection.
proposals.latency_budget: For local Mac/browser facts, under 2 seconds; for cross-surface checks, up to 10 seconds with progress spoken once. If a source is unavailable, answer immediately with the bounded unknown instead of waiting indefinitely.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: mostly authenticated reads and local joins. One short synthesis call per answer; no expensive model call for a rejected or empty evidence set.
proposals.security_concerns: Never disclose hidden credentials or raw secret-bearing evidence while explaining provenance. Use source-specific freshness windows, distinguish owner-origin from machine-origin facts, and require confirmation before treating an inferred claim as an action trigger.
missing: A claim-level evidence envelope with source, observedAt, freshness deadline, confidence, and status (observed/inferred/stale/unknown)
A policy engine defining freshness and authority per source instead of one global timestamp
A realtime response formatter that cannot erase uncertainty labels when shortening the answer
A user-visible drill-down on the Mac for the exact observations behind a spoken claim

proposals.user_asks: Before you do anything consequential, tell me whether the target, permissions, session, and delivery path are actually valid right now — and stop if any part is only assumed.
proposals.why_useful: Prevents the most damaging class of failure: acting on a stale tab, revoked session, wrong app, unreachable relay, or a pendant that never acknowledged playback. It turns perception into a hard boundary before judgement/action.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background/state checks first; realtime only to explain a failed preflight in the owner's voice.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 500 ms for cached checks; up to 2 s when a browser snapshot or relay probe is required.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for structured checks; one short realtime turn only on failure. Dominant cost is browser/relay round trips.
proposals.security_concerns: Never expose page contents or secrets in the preflight summary. Browser session identity and permission state leave the device only as redacted booleans. Consequential action still requires owner confirmation when target or scope changed.
missing: A versioned preflight contract consumed by plan/execute
Browser snapshot freshness and target identity bound into the action receipt
A relay-side device/playback truth field rather than socket-write delivery

proposals.user_asks: Find contradictions in what you remember about me and what the Mac, browser, relay, and clock say now, then show me exactly which source you trusted and what you refused to infer.
proposals.why_useful: The system currently injects a pinned machine-authored America/Chicago preference while the Mac is America/New_York. A contradiction auditor would prevent stale machine facts from silently steering schedules, reminders, and spoken answers.
proposals.model_tier: Background structured comparison; use the realtime tier only to summarize a contradiction the owner asks about.
proposals.latency_budget: Run on context refresh in under 1 s; interactive explanation under 3 s.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: deterministic normalization and hashes dominate; no model call for ordinary comparisons.
proposals.security_concerns: Compare provenance and metadata, not private values where possible. Do not rewrite owner facts automatically. Any proposed correction must be explicitly confirmed by the owner.
missing: A provenance-aware contradiction route that returns competing facts plus authority scope
A quarantine state for machine-authored pinned preferences
An origin-aware context projection that marks unresolved contradictions

proposals.user_asks: Show me the evidence chain for one answer or action: what the browser displayed, what the Mac did, what the relay accepted, and which links in the chain are missing or stale.
proposals.why_useful: A claim-level evidence chain is different from a generic activity digest: it lets the owner audit one consequential answer instead of trusting a completed job. It exposes uncapsuled relay reads and distinguishes 'Mac executed' from 'owner heard'.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic evidence joining and freshness checks; cheap text model only to render the chain in plain language.
proposals.latency_budget: Interactive lookup under 2 s; archival indexing asynchronous.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low model cost. Storage and hashing are the main costs; cap bodies and retain digests/tombstones, not secrets.
proposals.security_concerns: Redact secrets before persistence; content-address claims; enforce capsule revocation and per-surface authorization. Never claim hearing from relay bytes or Mac completion.
missing: Relay browser-read ID/hash transport into the Mac capsule store
Mounted browser provenance routes and an end-to-end correlation ID on voice, browser, job, and playback events
A defined device_playback emitter when a pendant exists

proposals.user_asks: When I move from my Mac to the pendant, continue the exact task where I left off: tell me what is open, what I was trying to do, what remains uncertain, and let me resume without repeating myself.
proposals.why_useful: Today the surfaces share fragments but not a trustworthy task handoff. The owner should be able to leave the desk and resume from the wearable with the same target, evidence, pending decision, and safe next step—not a generic summary.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap structured state extraction and deterministic joins; realtime only to speak the compact handoff on the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture a handoff in under 1 second when the owner says 'pause this'; resume speech within 2 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low model cost; storage and browser snapshot capture dominate. Keep only redacted state, hashes, and bounded screenshots/evidence references.
proposals.security_concerns: Handoff must bind to the owner's authenticated session and redact secrets, private page text, and credentials. Resuming a consequential action requires confirmation if the target changed.
missing: A cross-surface task-handoff object with immutable target/evidence references and unresolved assumptions
Pendant registration and bidirectional event delivery
A Mac/browser hook that snapshots resumable state at pause and validates it at resume

proposals.user_asks: Keep me from accidentally exposing private information: detect when a browser page, Mac screen, or pendant utterance contains a secret or sensitive context, then prevent it from being spoken, copied, uploaded, or used in an action unless I explicitly approve.
proposals.why_useful: The current system can join logged-in browser sessions, Mac automation, relay speech, and durable evidence, but the owner has no cross-surface privacy boundary. A single mistaken read-aloud or browser submission could leak credentials, financial data, or a private conversation.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic local classifiers and secret detectors first; a small background model for ambiguous classification; realtime only for an immediate spoken warning.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 150 ms for known secret patterns; under 1 second for screen/browser classification; never block ordinary non-sensitive interaction.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low model cost with local pattern matching and bounded redacted previews. Screen analysis is the dominant compute cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Classification and redaction should happen locally before relay upload. Store only hashes and labels by default. Explicit approval must be scoped to one destination, one field, and one action, then expire.
missing: A shared sensitivity taxonomy and policy engine across browser, Mac vision, relay speech, and evidence storage
Pre-upload redaction hooks for screenshots, page reads, speech transcripts, and action parameters
A pendant-visible approval protocol that works offline and records the owner's decision

proposals.user_asks: After you act across my browser, Mac, relay, and pendant, show me a causal undo plan—not just the last command—so I can reverse the whole change safely and know what cannot be undone.
proposals.why_useful: Existing job undo is local and step-oriented. Real tasks span browser mutations, files, messages, reminders, and spoken commitments; the owner needs dependency-aware recovery before an accidental chain becomes permanent.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic action graph and inverse-operation registry; use a slower model only to explain tradeoffs when inverses conflict.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview under 1 second for a recent task; execute each reversible step with receipt confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low model cost; bounded ledger growth and occasional browser/Mac verification dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: Never invent an inverse. Mark irreversible effects explicitly, require confirmation for destructive reversal, and preserve an append-only audit record without message/page secrets.
missing: A cross-surface causal action graph linking browser command IDs, Mac job IDs, relay jobs, and owner confirmations
Inverse operations for common browser and Mac mutations, with pre/post state hashes
A dependency-aware planner that refuses unsafe reversal order

proposals.user_asks: “Do this task for me, and show me proof it really happened—not just that the Mac said it ran.”
proposals.why_useful: This would be the system's most useful trustworthy behavior: a spoken request could cross the relay, authenticated browser, and Mac, then return a concise result grounded in before/after evidence. It would distinguish planned, attempted, verified, and owner-heard instead of calling a Mac-side completion “done.”
surfaces: pendant voice request and (when connected) spoken result
relay intent/job correlation and policy gate
Mac planner and action ledger for reversible execution
browser extension for authenticated page state and mutation
Mac vision for visual before/after verification when DOM evidence is insufficient
relay receipt returned to the pendant
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the short conversational turn; a cheaper background planner/verifier model for multi-step execution and evidence comparison.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 s; execute in the existing job budget (roughly 10–60 s); speak a 1-sentence verdict plus an optional evidence detail. Destructive or irreversible steps still require confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.03 per task with planner/verifier calls; browser and Mac execution dominate latency, not tokens. Screenshot verification adds one vision call only when structured state cannot prove the result.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence must be redacted before relay storage and retain source URL, timestamp, and content hash. Never expose secrets from authenticated tabs. Require confirmation for send/delete/purchase. If verification is unavailable or state changed, say “attempted, not verified,” never infer success.
missing: A single cross-surface receipt schema joining actionLedger step keys, browser command IDs, evidence capsule IDs, relay job IDs, and verification outcome
A relay-side reader that refuses completed=true unless an independent postcondition verifier passes
A pendant playback/consumption event when a real pendant is deployed; current relay delivery is only bytes-to-socket

proposals.user_asks: “Before you click or submit anything in my browser, tell me whether the page you are relying on is still the same page I approved.”
proposals.why_useful: Authenticated web pages can change after the owner approves an action. A cross-surface freshness fence would prevent submitting to a changed tab, wrong account, or altered form, while giving the owner a concrete reason for any pause instead of a vague failure.
surfaces: pendant for the approval and spoken stale-page warning
browser extension for authenticated DOM snapshot, tab identity, and postcondition check
Mac vision for a visual fallback when DOM capture is incomplete
relay for policy, approval token, and tamper-evident correlation
Mac planner/action ledger for the actual mutation and undo path
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap deterministic hash/diff first; invoke a small verifier model only for semantic changes (for example, whether a changed total or recipient is material). Realtime speaks only the warning or final confirmation.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture and compare in <500 ms before a click; semantic verification under 2 s. If the tab, URL, account identity, or relevant field changes, pause and ask rather than proceed.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for hashes and structured diffs; <$0.01 for ambiguous semantic comparison. Browser snapshot transfer and one optional screenshot dominate latency.
proposals.security_concerns: Hash only redacted relevant fields, never upload passwords, tokens, or full page bodies to the relay. Bind approval to tab/session pseudonym, URL origin, locator, content hash, and short expiry. A changed page invalidates approval; destructive actions remain confirmation-gated.
missing: A browser-side approval token bound to the evidence capsule/content hash and expiring after one mutation
A preflight hook in browser_run_actions and Mac action execution that enforces the token instead of merely recording provenance
A shared semantic-diff contract so browser DOM and Mac vision can agree on what changed

proposals.user_asks: “Is the thing I’m seeing on my Mac actually the same thing the relay and browser think is happening?”
proposals.why_useful: The system currently exposes several partial truths: relay job state, Mac receipts, browser tab state, and pipeline traces can disagree or go stale. A spoken discrepancy report would identify the first contradictory observation, its age, and the safest next check instead of silently choosing one source.
surfaces: pendant for a short discrepancy alert and follow-up question
relay for job/session state and server timestamps
Mac agent for permissions, process reachability, action receipts, and pipeline trace
browser extension for live tab/session identity and pending command state
Mac vision for a visual confirmation of what is actually rendered
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic rules should align timestamps, IDs, hashes, and freshness first; use a low-cost reasoning model only to summarize contradictions. Realtime is reserved for the spoken answer.
proposals.latency_budget: Routine check in 1–2 s; visual fallback under 5 s. It must return “consistent,” “contradictory,” or “not observable,” with the oldest observation age.
proposals.cost_estimate: <$0.01 when structured snapshots suffice; one vision call costs more and is used only on disagreement or missing DOM evidence.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep raw authenticated page content on the Mac; send only redacted claims, hashes, IDs, and timestamps to relay. Treat a missing source as unknown, not false. Never let a consistency check authorize a destructive action by itself.
missing: A normalized observation envelope with source, capturedAt, freshness policy, subject ID, content hash, and confidence
A contradiction detector that compares relay jobs, Mac receipts, browser state, and pipeline events without treating completed as heard
A user-facing explanation format that names which source won and why, or explicitly reports unresolved disagreement

proposals.user_asks: “Give me a temporary permission to do exactly this one kind of thing across my Mac and logged-in browser, and let me revoke it from the pendant at any time.”
proposals.why_useful: Today consent is fragmented: the relay, Mac planner, and browser extension can each be trusted, but there is no owner-visible, scope-limited delegation that follows one request across all three. This would let the owner safely authorize a bounded task without repeatedly confirming harmless steps, while retaining an immediate physical stop control.
surfaces: pendant button/voice to display, confirm, and revoke a short-lived delegation
relay to mint a signed, single-purpose capability token and enforce its expiry, audience, and action limits
Mac planner/action ledger to require and record the token before each action
browser extension to enforce the same token against tab origin, session, and allowed mutation types
Mac vision only as a read-only verifier that cannot expand the delegation
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic policy and signature checks; no expensive model for authorization. Realtime is used only to explain the scope and expiry in one short sentence.
proposals.latency_budget: Issuing or revoking under 300 ms when connected; every action adds under 50 ms for local token validation. Offline pendant revocation must be queued monotonically and honored on the next link before any new delegated action.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; cryptographic checks and small event records dominate. Hardware work is firmware button/LED state plus a bounded revocation journal, not routine SD writes.
proposals.security_concerns: Bind the token to owner identity, task ID, allowed verbs, target origins/apps, maximum count, expiry, and a nonce; prevent model text from widening scope. Revocation must fail closed, survive relay restart, and be visible in receipts. Never delegate password extraction, arbitrary shell, purchases, deletion, or message sending without a separate confirmation.
missing: A shared capability-token format and verifier implemented by relay, Mac, and browser
A pendant-side bounded revocation record and a relay endpoint that accepts device-authenticated revocations
Action and browser harness enforcement hooks; recording a token in the ledger is insufficient if executors do not reject missing or mismatched tokens
A user-facing scope preview that names the exact apps, sites, and verbs before approval

proposals.user_asks: “When you use a personal fact about me, show me where it came from, whether I said it, and let me correct only that fact without rewriting my whole memory.”
proposals.why_useful: A machine-derived preference can currently look indistinguishable from owner intent, remain pinned indefinitely, and be injected into every prompt. The owner needs a provenance-aware correction interaction—especially for timezone, permissions, and routines—so a stale or sampled value cannot quietly steer actions.
surfaces: pendant voice for “why do you think that?” and a short correction
Mac memory store for source.origin, confidence, use history, expiry, and targeted replacement/tombstone
relay context projection so corrected provenance propagates to realtime voice and scheduled work
Mac planner/judgement to downgrade or quarantine machine-derived facts until resolved
browser only when a fact was inferred from an authenticated page, linking the source capsule without exposing its secret contents
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic provenance display, conflict detection, and targeted fact mutation; a cheap summarizer can turn the record into one spoken sentence. Realtime is not needed for background reconciliation.
proposals.latency_budget: Answer provenance in under 1 s from local memory; apply a confirmed correction and invalidate projections within 2 s. Scheduled jobs must use the new value on their next invocation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; invalidating cached projections and propagating a tombstone are the main engineering work.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not speak secret fact values by default. Distinguish owner, machine, browser, and inferred origins; never let a low-authority browser observation overwrite an owner fact automatically. Require confirmation to delete or replace an owner-origin fact, and retain an audit tombstone without retaining sensitive body text.
missing: A first-class provenance and authority field in every memory projection consumer, not just the stored fact
A targeted owner correction route that atomically replaces/quarantines one key and invalidates relay/Mac caches
Conflict policy for owner versus machine-derived values, including a visible warning instead of confidence-only sorting
Voice-safe redaction for secrets and a compact “source and last confirmed” explanation

proposals.user_asks: “Mark this moment so I can come back to it later.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can capture an actionable thought without stopping to organize it: the pendant records the utterance, the Mac records the exact visible app/browser state, and the relay preserves a resumable checkpoint. Later “take me back to that moment” opens the same page/app and reads the owner's note, instead of relying on an ungrounded memory.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the short spoken intent and confirmation; a cheaper background model extracts a title and next action from the note and context.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 1 s; capture Mac/browser state within 3 s; resume within 5 s when the browser bridge and Mac are online.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per checkpoint, dominated by one short realtime turn; background extraction can use a low-cost text model.
proposals.security_concerns: The checkpoint may contain screen text, logged-in URL, and a voice transcript. Store a redacted evidence capsule and URL host by default, require explicit confirmation before capturing sensitive page bodies, and never send browser cookies or credentials to the relay.
missing: A single checkpoint record joining pendant capture ID, Mac session, browser command/result, evidence capsule ID, and relay job ID
A user-facing resume route that reopens the recorded app/tab and reports which parts are unavailable
A pendant-connected capture event; today the relay has no registered pendant

proposals.user_asks: “Watch this page and tell me only if something important changes.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets a hands-free alert for a price, appointment, ticket, shipment, or research page without repeatedly checking it. The browser extension observes the authenticated page, the Mac creates a redacted content hash and decides whether the change is meaningful, the relay schedules checks while the Mac sleeps, and the pendant speaks only a confirmed delta.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background model for periodic diff classification; realtime is used only to phrase the final spoken alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Check on the requested interval; after a detected change, deliver a concise alert within 10 s when the pendant link is available, otherwise queue it.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.002–$0.01 per check using hashing and a small classifier; realtime speech is the dominant cost only when an alert fires.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents must stay on the Mac; send only a redacted diff, source host, and content hash to the relay. Require confirmation for sensitive domains, provide an immediate stop command, and expire watchers by default.
missing: A durable watcher scheduler joining browser session affinity, evidence capsule revisions, and relay announcements
A meaningful-change policy that distinguishes page chrome/ads from the watched region
A browser-originated authenticated change event; current relay read_web_page has no ID, hash, or persistence
A pendant playback acknowledgement before marking an alert heard

proposals.user_asks: “What actually happened, and what should I do next?”
proposals.why_useful: After any spoken request, the system would give one honest account across the whole chain instead of saying “done” when only the Mac ran. It correlates the pendant's capture-quality verdict, relay job and socket state, Mac action receipts, browser command/result, screenshots, and (when available) playback confirmation, then tells the owner exactly where the chain stopped and offers the next reversible recovery.
proposals.model_tier: A cheap deterministic correlator produces the evidence graph and confidence labels; use realtime only to explain the short result conversationally, escalating to a stronger model for ambiguous screenshots or competing receipts.
proposals.latency_budget: For completed work, answer within 2 s from existing receipts; if a fresh screenshot or browser poll is needed, under 8 s. Never block the owner on a missing pendant acknowledgement.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 because it is structured joins; screenshot interpretation is the variable cost, roughly $0.02–$0.10 only when needed.
proposals.security_concerns: Screenshots and browser results can contain private content. Keep raw evidence on the Mac, expose redacted snippets and hashes to the relay, require confirmation before proposing a retry with side effects, and clearly distinguish observed, inferred, and unknown states.
missing: A stable cross-surface correlation key propagated from voice turn through relay job, Mac job, browser command, and pipeline run
A perception reducer that treats Mac completion as distinct from pendant playback and labels unknown rather than guessing
A screenshot/evidence attachment on job receipts, with redaction and bounded retention
A pendant-originated playback event; the existing device_playback reader has zero emitters

proposals.user_asks: “If I lose my phone or laptop, make sure I can still recover the important things.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner would have a cross-surface emergency recovery mode: the pendant can locally seal a tiny manifest of critical contacts, active tasks, and recovery instructions; the Mac can periodically encrypt and attest the corresponding evidence; the relay can hold the encrypted escrow while offline. A replacement device could authenticate and reconstruct only the owner's explicitly marked essentials, rather than losing the continuity graph with one machine.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background summarization and deterministic encryption/manifest generation; realtime is used only for spoken enrollment, confirmation, or recovery guidance.
proposals.latency_budget: Enrollment under 30 s; periodic Mac-side refresh under 2 s; emergency recovery begins within 10 s of authentication.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low ongoing model cost, typically under $0.01 per refresh; storage and key-management dominate rather than inference.
proposals.security_concerns: This is exceptionally sensitive. Use owner-held recovery keys, threshold approval or a second factor, client-side encryption so the relay cannot read contents, per-item expiry/revocation, and never include browser cookies, passwords, raw audio, or unrestricted screen captures.
missing: An owner-controlled encrypted escrow format and key rotation protocol
A recovery ceremony spanning a replacement browser/Mac and a locally authenticated pendant
A device-independent export of selected evidence, tasks, and context-graph entities rather than raw workspace files
A durable relay route for encrypted recovery bundles with auditable access receipts

proposals.user_asks: “Never let any of you send, buy, publish, or delete anything unless I physically confirm it.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner would get a real cross-device safety boundary rather than trusting a model prompt. The relay classifies the requested side effect, the Mac/browser prepares but does not commit it, and the pendant's physical button plus a spoken transaction summary authorizes exactly one bounded action. A stale page, changed amount, or changed recipient invalidates the approval.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic policy engine for action classification, target/amount hashing, and expiry; use a small model only to summarize the pending transaction; realtime handles the short confirmation exchange.
proposals.latency_budget: Preparation can take seconds; after a physical confirmation, commit within 3 s and return a receipt. No irreversible action may proceed without the bounded approval.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.01 per transaction; browser/Mac inspection and cryptographic receipt handling dominate, not model tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: The authorization must be device-bound, single-use, short-lived, and include a hash of the exact final action. Protect against clickjacking, confused-deputy browser sessions, replay, and an attacker who can speak near the pendant. Require a physical button gesture for high-risk classes and expose a local cancel gesture.
missing: A policy-enforcement gate below every irreversible Mac and browser action, not merely a planner instruction
A pendant-signed nonce/approval protocol with monotonic expiry and replay protection
A final-state re-read immediately before commit, with target and content hash comparison
Receipts that prove which physical approval authorized which exact side effect

proposals.user_asks: “That was wrong—freeze everything needed to understand it and prevent a repeat.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner would be able to turn a frustrating failure into a reproducible incident without manually gathering logs. The pendant preserves the utterance and capture-quality frame, the relay freezes its job/session trace, the Mac captures pre/post UI state and receipts, and the browser records the exact tab/result. A later run can compare against the incident and warn before repeating the same failure.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic snapshot assembly and hashing first; a cheaper background model writes the incident summary and extracts a regression condition; realtime only acknowledges and explains the immediate finding.
proposals.latency_budget: Freeze the evidence within 2 s of the owner's phrase; produce a short explanation within 10 s; background analysis may take minutes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually $0.01–$0.05 per incident, dominated by optional screenshot/audio analysis; hashes and structured receipts are nearly free.
proposals.security_concerns: Incident bundles can contain private screens, URLs, transcripts, and action parameters. Redact locally before relay upload, classify sensitivity, allow the owner to inspect/delete, and keep raw audio/screenshots on the Mac unless explicitly exported.
missing: A cross-surface incident transaction that atomically snapshots relay, Mac, browser, and pendant evidence
A bounded pre-trigger ring buffer for Mac/browser observations and pendant quality metrics
A redaction-and-diff pipeline that can compare incidents without exposing secrets
A regression guard that can consume an incident's condition before permitting a future action

proposals.user_asks: "What actually changed while I was away, and which parts are only assumptions?"
proposals.why_useful: The current continuity export is a truncated snapshot, while pipeline completion can mean only that the Mac acted and browser/relay records have different retention. A change-oriented witness would compare bounded watermarks across relay, Mac, browser, and pipeline, report concrete transitions, and label each gap as unknown instead of silently treating absence as zero.
proposals.model_tier: background for snapshot diffing; realtime only to narrate the already-computed result
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a normal bounded diff; no model call for collection or classification
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01, dominated by one cheap structured summarization call; collection is local HTTP and browser metadata
proposals.security_concerns: Do not export page bodies or secrets; compare IDs, timestamps, statuses, hashes, and explicit retention bounds. Mark truncated/count-capped sources as unknown. Require confirmation before exposing sensitive browser titles.
missing: A durable per-source high-water mark and tombstone cursor (the existing snapshot is truncated and not a diff)
A relay endpoint that returns cursor-valid changes rather than only current state
A browser event cursor for tab/command transitions

proposals.user_asks: "Is the pendant really connected and usable right now, or am I only looking at the Mac bench?"
proposals.why_useful: Today the relay registry can omit a pendant structurally, while source-level USB assumptions can be mistaken for a live wearable. This owner-facing answer would perform a bounded USB identity probe, read the firmware health frame, cross-check relay registration/heartbeat, and return one of bench-only, connected-not-registered, registered-but-stale, or end-to-end-ready with timestamps and evidence.
proposals.model_tier: No LLM for probing; cheap text model only to explain the structured verdict
proposals.latency_budget: 3 seconds for serial probes and relay status; fail closed if either side is unavailable
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; local serial reads dominate
proposals.security_concerns: Read-only, bounded allowlisted ports and byte counts; never transmit raw serial logs or firmware secrets. USB presence is not owner location and must be labelled bench-only.
missing: The granted mac_usb_serial_diagnostics capability must be implemented as an actual bounded Mac action (it is not in the current route/action inventory)
Firmware health frame transport for the currently absent nRF device and ESP32 bridge
A relay-side join key tying a firmware session/build ID to a registered device without using the admin key
built_from: GET /v1/devices/status (relay route, currently authoritative but capped)

proposals.user_asks: "When you say there was nothing waiting for me, what did you actually check?"
proposals.why_useful: The system currently conflates an empty result with an unreadable or count-capped source. A negative-evidence receipt would list the exact stores, cursors, query limits, and freshness used, distinguish none-found from not-readable, and preserve a compact receipt the owner can inspect later. This is perception of absence, not another catch-up digest.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic structured collection and comparison; use a cheap model only to phrase the receipt
proposals.latency_budget: Under 1 second from already-live snapshots; remote checks bounded to 3 seconds
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost; bounded metadata receipt under a few KB
proposals.security_concerns: Receipt contains metadata only: no page bodies, message text, or secrets. Access must follow the source's existing scopes; disclose when a source was skipped or truncated.
missing: Standard result semantics across continuity readers: found, none, unreadable, truncated, expired, and not-applicable
A compact durable receipt store with source cursors and query bounds
Relay/browser APIs must expose their applied limits and freshness in machine-readable form

proposals.user_asks: "Before you use my browser or speak something aloud, show me exactly what data would leave this Mac, where it would go, and prove afterward what actually left."
proposals.why_useful: Today browser reads can cross the Mac/relay/model boundary without a unified, owner-visible disclosure receipt. The Mac has redaction and evidence primitives, but relay browser reads have no stable ID or hash, and announcement storage can retain page-derived speech without source provenance. This capability gives the owner a real data-flow boundary rather than a generic privacy promise.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic policy and hashing first; use the realtime model only to explain a blocked or permitted transfer in plain language
proposals.latency_budget: Preview under 300 ms for local browser data; remote transfer is blocked until the receipt is committed. Post-transfer verification under 1 second.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for normal cases; bounded metadata receipts under a few KB. Hashing and redaction are local CPU work.
proposals.security_concerns: The preview must never contain the very secret it is protecting. Redaction must happen before preview persistence; sensitive destinations require explicit confirmation. Receipts need access control and must record hashes/field classes, not raw page text or audio.
missing: A cross-surface data-flow receipt protocol with transfer ID, source, destination, classification, redaction result, content hash, and disposition
Relay browser reads must return a stable ID and hash and must attach that ID to any routine, speech, job, or announcement derived from the read
Mac and browser provenance stores must be mounted into the live routes and joined to relay receipts
A policy decision point that can pause relay/model transfer until owner confirmation for sensitive classifications

proposals.user_asks: "If I tell you to forget something, prove where it went and remove or quarantine every copy you made."
proposals.why_useful: There is no end-to-end revocation: browser evidence has tombstones, but relay announcements are never deleted, audio retention is not automatically swept, and Mac jobs/pipeline records have separate caps. The owner needs a propagation-aware erasure result, not a claim that one local memory row was deleted.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic locator and deletion workflow; cheap model only to summarize the receipt, never to decide whether a secret should be erased
proposals.latency_budget: Preview under 1 second; execution and verification under 5 seconds where all surfaces are online, otherwise return an explicit pending/quarantined state
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost; storage and verification are bounded metadata scans
proposals.security_concerns: Erasure requests are irreversible and require confirmation, strong owner authentication, and an immutable minimal audit receipt containing only hashes and destination classes. Offline nodes must not silently report success.
missing: A content lineage ID connecting browser capsules, relay reads, spoken announcements, audio, jobs, memory facts, and pipeline records
Authenticated delete/quarantine endpoints on relay and Mac for every retained artifact, including announcement and audio stores
A durable erasure ledger with retry state and honest verification semantics
A policy for backups, model-provider retention, and already-heard audio that cannot be physically recalled

proposals.user_asks: "Take that answer apart: what independent evidence supports it, what contradicts it, and what would change your mind?"
proposals.why_useful: Current context projection can elevate a machine-written, pinned preference above live machine truth, while completion and delivery states have different meanings. The owner cannot currently trigger an adversarial review of one claim across its independent sources. This capability would expose provenance conflicts before they become actions.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap structured contradiction pass over source records; reserve realtime reasoning for genuinely conflicting high-impact claims
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for local claims; remote source checks bounded to 4 seconds
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01; dominated by structured source reads, not generation
proposals.security_concerns: Do not reveal hidden memory or private browser content merely because a claim is challenged. Return source class, timestamp, hash, and access-controlled excerpts. A contradiction must lower confidence, not trigger autonomous deletion or action.
missing: A claim identity and provenance graph shared by memory, browser evidence, relay jobs, pipeline stages, and device events
Independent-source quorum rules that distinguish corroboration from duplicated copies of the same assertion
A user-facing claim review route that records the challenge, revised confidence, and unresolved alternatives

proposals.user_asks: Before you tell me something you saw or before another part of you acts on it, show me which parts are directly observed, which are inferred, and which could already be stale.
proposals.why_useful: The system currently has grounded/asserted claim fields in browser provenance but does not enforce them at the boundary where judgement and speech consume context. This capability would prevent a stale tab title, relay 'delivered' state, or Mac-completed job from being silently upgraded into a fact about what the owner saw or heard. It is useful because it turns perception into a trust contract the other faculties can rely on.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background classifier for provenance joins and freshness; realtime model only verbalizes the resulting trust labels
proposals.latency_budget: Under 300 ms for cached records; under 2 seconds when it must inspect the current browser or Mac state
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low: mostly deterministic joins, hashes, and age checks; occasional small model call for ambiguity classification
proposals.security_concerns: Do not retain raw page text or screenshots merely to explain provenance. Return capsule IDs, source host/path, capture time, hash, sensitivity class, and a short redacted claim. Sensitive claims require confirmation before being spoken or acted on.
missing: A mounted browserProvenance route and consumer; the module exists but is currently unmounted
A relay-to-Mac provenance bridge that returns stable read IDs and content hashes for cloud browser reads
A single claim-envelope contract accepted by judgement and action, with states observed, grounded, inferred, stale, and unknown
Freshness rules by source type, including the explicit rule that socket bytes and Mac completion are not playback

proposals.user_asks: Can I rely on you right now, and exactly which parts of you are reachable, stale, or only pretending to be complete?
proposals.why_useful: The current status export reports many components but can still hide semantic gaps: the Mac bridge can be online while no pendant exists, a browser can heartbeat while a command is pending, and a relay can accept audio without proving playback. This capability gives the owner a reachability contract rather than a green dashboard: per-surface liveness, freshness age, last verified operation, and the strongest claim that surface can support.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic probes and policy rules first; a small background model turns the matrix into plain language only when needed
proposals.latency_budget: 1-3 seconds for active read-only probes; cached answers under 200 ms
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost when rendered from structured probes; network and browser heartbeat probes dominate
proposals.security_concerns: Probe only read-only health endpoints and do not include tab content, credentials, or audio. Surface stale timestamps and missing devices rather than guessing. Require confirmation before any probe that opens or changes a session.
missing: A typed reachability contract separating transport, authentication, observation, and actuation for each surface
An active pendant-registration/heartbeat source; today no nRF9160 is registered and the converse path does not update the registry
A browser command round-trip probe with a nonce and expiry, distinct from extension heartbeat
A semantic health policy that marks relay socket-delivered audio as not-heard until the accepted playback lifecycle telemetry exists

proposals.user_asks: What is actually visible to me right now, and do the browser, screen, and accessibility views agree?
proposals.why_useful: Now that the exact AI Pendant Agent has Accessibility and Screen Recording, perception can cross-check three independent views instead of trusting one stale channel. A screenshot can catch overlays and modal dialogs the DOM misses; accessibility can reveal focus and labels; the browser bridge can provide URL/session identity. Reporting disagreements prevents actions against the wrong tab or hidden dialog.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime vision only for the current screenshot when the owner asks; deterministic browser/accessibility joins and a cheap vision model for routine disagreement detection
proposals.latency_budget: 1-2 seconds for a current-state answer; under 500 ms for browser-only cached state
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate only when a screenshot is required; image tokens dominate, while DOM/accessibility metadata is cheap
proposals.security_concerns: Screenshots may contain passwords, financial data, or private messages. Redact known sensitive regions before sending to a model, keep raw screenshots local with short TTL, and require confirmation before exposing or acting on sensitive content.
missing: A perception endpoint that atomically captures screenshot, focused app, accessibility tree summary, and browser snapshot with one capture ID
A local redaction pass for screen images and accessibility values before model upload
A disagreement schema (same tab, same focus, same visible title, overlay present) with freshness timestamps
A policy that blocks action when the three views disagree on target identity

proposals.user_asks: Is this browser session, Mac session, and relay conversation definitely the same task and the same me, or could one of them be stale or crossed?
proposals.why_useful: The system has separate browser, Mac, and relay identities, but no owner-visible binding that proves they refer to the same live task. A stale browser tab or reused relay context could otherwise feed observations into the wrong action. This capability would expose a task-binding verdict before sensitive context is joined or an action is taken.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic cryptographic/session checks; no model call unless the owner asks for a plain-language explanation
proposals.latency_budget: Under 250 ms with cached session state; under 2 seconds when a fresh browser challenge is required
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; dominated by one browser challenge-response and local signature verification
proposals.security_concerns: Never expose raw session identifiers, cookies, or extension nonces in speech. Bind only pseudonymous task IDs and expiry windows. If binding fails, refuse cross-surface joins rather than guessing.
missing: A relay-issued task nonce propagated into Mac and browser commands
A browser extension challenge-response proving the active tab/session owns that nonce
A Mac-side attestation tying the action ledger and browser result to the same task nonce
An owner-visible 'bound / stale / crossed' verdict consumed by judgement and action

proposals.user_asks: Before you say this aloud, did any part of the answer come from a secret, private screen, or sensitive page—and can you safely summarize it without leaking the value?
proposals.why_useful: Current redaction and provenance structures protect stored evidence, but nothing is a final speech-time gate across browser text, screenshots, Mac state, and relay-generated summaries. This would stop a private tab title, password fragment, message, or financial value from being spoken merely because it entered context upstream.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic sensitivity classifier and redaction first; a small model only for safe paraphrase when the owner has authorized spoken summaries
proposals.latency_budget: Under 150 ms for known-sensitive fields; under 1 second for a novel combined answer
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: local classification and masking dominate; model cost only for paraphrasing redacted content
proposals.security_concerns: Raw sensitive values stay on the Mac and are never sent to the relay or realtime model. Default to omission, not euphemistic guessing. Require explicit owner policy for categories such as messages, passwords, health, finance, and intimate content.
missing: A speech-boundary interceptor that sees the final grounded claims before TTS or realtime output
One sensitivity taxonomy shared by evidence capsules, screenshots, browser claims, and Mac automation results
Local redaction/paraphrase routines that preserve meaning without transmitting the secret
A durable owner policy for which categories may be spoken, summarized, or always omitted

proposals.user_asks: Has my system become less safe since the last time I trusted it—did permissions, browser sessions, relay credentials, or automation scope change?
proposals.why_useful: A current green status is not evidence that the trust boundary stayed stable. The owner needs a security-drift report that notices permission changes, new browser identities, relay credential rotation, scope changes, and unexpected automation surfaces, then distinguishes owner-approved changes from unexplained ones.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic baseline comparison and policy evaluation; use a cheap background model only to explain a flagged diff
proposals.latency_budget: Under 1 second from a cached baseline; 2-4 seconds when refreshing all surfaces
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low: structured metadata and hashes only; no page bodies or screenshots required
proposals.security_concerns: The baseline itself is sensitive. Store only salted fingerprints, permission classes, device/session pseudonyms, and timestamps. Never expose bearer tokens or raw credential material. A newly broadened permission should be reported but not automatically revoked.
missing: A signed, owner-approved security baseline spanning Mac TCC permissions, browser extension identities, relay device credentials, and action scopes
Change events for permission grants/revocations and relay credential/scope updates
A durable approval record distinguishing owner-approved changes from unexplained drift
A policy engine that blocks sensitive actions when the baseline is stale or unexplained drift is present

proposals.user_asks: Make sure scheduled briefings reach me even when the pendant is unavailable.
proposals.why_useful: Today a completed Mac run can leave 471 KB of audio held at the relay with the pendant absent, and the owner receives no alternate delivery. This would detect that precise state, produce a short text/notification fallback on the Mac, and retain the full audio for later instead of silently losing the briefing.
proposals.model_tier: background model for classification and concise fallback drafting; no realtime call unless the owner asks a follow-up
proposals.latency_budget: Detect within 60 seconds of a routine result; fallback notification in under 5 seconds after the relay reports held_by_relay.
proposals.cost_estimate: ~$0.001–$0.01 per routine, dominated by one short summarization; zero model cost when the existing brief text is already available.
proposals.security_concerns: Fallback may expose briefing text in a macOS notification or browser surface; honor the existing routine sensitivity and require confirmation before sending outside the device. Never claim the pendant heard it.
missing: A relay-to-Mac delivery-policy event carrying held_by_relay/awaitsDevice and an expiry, rather than requiring inference from pipeline traces
A Mac notification or browser inbox target for routine fallback
A user policy for which routines may be text-fallbacked and how long audio remains valid

proposals.user_asks: Before you tell me a routine finished, check that its evidence agrees and explain any contradiction.
proposals.why_useful: The live pipeline contains a concrete contradiction: the spoken text claims 58.5 seconds of audio while the same run's telemetry reports 9.824 seconds and 471,570 bytes. A perception fence should prevent a false 'done' or misleading owner report when duration, byte count, stage state, and delivery state disagree.
proposals.model_tier: cheap deterministic validator first; background model only to phrase an explanation when fields conflict
proposals.latency_budget: Under 100 ms for numeric/state checks; under 2 seconds for a human-readable explanation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for validation; <$0.001 for an occasional explanation.
proposals.security_concerns: Telemetry can include command text and snippets; keep raw payload local, send only field names and bounded discrepancy facts to any model. Never auto-retry or mark success based on a model judgment.
missing: A shared evidence contract defining which fields are authoritative for audio duration, bytes, and completion
A relay/local-agent status that can be 'contradictory' instead of collapsing to completed/failed
A reader in the owner-facing briefing and job-status paths that surfaces the contradiction and withholds completion language

proposals.user_asks: Before acting in my browser, tell me if the active tab and the session you remember are different.
proposals.why_useful: The live browser is on a YouTube tab while the stored session affinity still points to news.google.com. Acting on the remembered session without noticing this split can click or read the wrong site. The guard would compare fresh extension state, session affinity, and the requested target, then pause with a one-sentence clarification instead of guessing.
proposals.model_tier: deterministic URL/host comparison; use the realtime model only to ask the short clarification during an active voice turn
proposals.latency_budget: Under 300 ms before any browser action; clarification within one voice turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: Zero for comparison; negligible realtime tokens for a clarification.
proposals.security_concerns: URLs and tab titles can reveal sensitive activity. Keep comparisons on the Mac, redact query strings by default, and require confirmation when the mismatch involves a logged-in or destructive action.
missing: A first-class browser context snapshot with active tab, session affinity, last-seen timestamps, and confidence in one schema
A precondition hook in browser_run_actions/mac vision that can block execution on context mismatch
An explicit owner policy for when a host change is safe versus when to ask

proposals.user_asks: When I ask for a briefing, tell me only information that was fresh at the requested cutoff, and say exactly what was too old or unverifiable.
proposals.why_useful: A scheduled news brief can be generated successfully while its sources, cached browser pages, or relay-held audio are stale. The owner needs temporal truth, not merely a completed run. This would enforce per-claim freshness across browser captures, Mac research, and relay scheduling, then speak a bounded uncertainty statement instead of silently blending old and new material.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap deterministic timestamp/provenance checks first; background model for compressing the resulting freshness ledger into one spoken sentence.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds of validation after research completes; no more than 3 seconds added to a scheduled brief.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for timestamp checks; <$0.005 per briefing for a short uncertainty summary.
proposals.security_concerns: Source URLs, page titles, and private browser captures must remain local unless the owner explicitly requests cloud research. Never treat an undated page as current merely because retrieval succeeded.
missing: A common source-observation record carrying observedAt, publishedAt when known, requested cutoff, and freshness verdict
Browser and relay research paths that preserve those timestamps instead of returning only text
A speech/template layer that names stale or unverifiable claims without exposing sensitive URLs

proposals.user_asks: Let the pendant and Mac agree on whether I am available before interrupting me, and queue low-priority things without making me manage another setting.
proposals.why_useful: The relay, browser, and Mac can each be alive while the owner is actually in a call, speaking to someone else, or actively typing. A single availability decision using pendant voice activity, Mac foreground/meeting state, and browser activity would prevent badly timed interruptions while preserving urgent items.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic state machine for availability and priority; realtime model only for interpreting an ambiguous spoken override.
proposals.latency_budget: Availability updates within 1 second; interruption decision under 100 ms; spoken override responds within one voice turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero steady-state; <$0.001 for rare ambiguous overrides.
proposals.security_concerns: Microphone-derived availability must be reduced to short-lived state, not uploaded audio. Calendar titles and active-window names should stay on the Mac. Emergency/high-priority policy must be explicit and never inferred from model confidence.
missing: A cross-surface availability protocol with leases, expiry, confidence, and reasons
A pendant-side local occupancy signal that works offline, rather than relying on relay registration
Scheduler and announcement delivery that honor the lease and expose why an item was deferred
A user-editable priority/escalation policy

proposals.user_asks: After you change something on my Mac, let me ask 'what changed?' and hear a before-and-after explanation tied to the exact file, browser page, or app state.
proposals.why_useful: Today action receipts and browser results can establish that an operation ran, but they do not give the owner a compact, cross-surface explanation of the resulting state. This would join Mac action ledgers, browser provenance, and relay speech into a durable, owner-auditable change narrative with an undo path where available.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic diff and receipt join first; cheap background model to phrase the spoken explanation, never to invent a change.
proposals.latency_budget: Record the change synchronously; answer a follow-up in under 2 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for structured diffs; <$0.005 when summarization is needed.
proposals.security_concerns: Before/after values may contain secrets. Redact credentials and private page content at capture, retain only bounded hashes/snippets, and require confirmation before replaying sensitive values aloud. Destructive undo remains confirmation-gated.
missing: A cross-surface change identifier joining action ledger step, browser command/result, evidence capsule, job receipt, and spoken response
A durable owner-facing change journal with redaction and retention rules
Diff adapters for files, browser mutations, and application state
A read-only voice/dashboard query over that journal

proposals.user_asks: When I say “what’s that?”, use whatever is in front of me right now and answer the question out loud.
proposals.why_useful: The pendant becomes a genuinely eyes-free pointer to the owner’s current attention: no app name, tab URL, or screenshot description is needed. It can identify the focused UI object, read visible text, and answer in one turn instead of making the owner explain context.
surfaces: pendant captures the utterance and plays the answer
mac-vision captures the focused window and locates the likely object under the cursor or recent focus
browser-extension supplies the authenticated tab DOM/text when the target is in Safari
relay-realtime transcribes, asks the local perception loop for grounding, and speaks a short answer
faculty-perception attaches freshness, source, and confidence so faculty-judgement can refuse guesses
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles the short utterance and final spoken response; a cheaper vision/text model handles screenshot OCR and element localization; no expensive model is used for raw extraction.
proposals.latency_budget: Target 1.5–3 seconds: 300 ms capture/route, up to 1.5 s local vision or DOM extraction, then one realtime turn. If the target is ambiguous, ask one clarification rather than hallucinating.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero incremental API cost when DOM/accessibility text suffices; roughly $0.005–$0.03 for a vision fallback, dominated by screenshot vision tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Screenshots and authenticated page text remain on the Mac unless explicitly sent to the relay; redact passwords, payment fields, and secret locators before any model call. Require a visible/voice confirmation before reading sensitive content aloud.
missing: A focused-target perception endpoint that joins Screen Recording/accessibility coordinates to the browser extension’s active tab
A local redaction and confidence gate for screenshots
A relay request/response contract carrying a short-lived grounding id and source timestamp

proposals.user_asks: Tell me when the information on my Mac and the information on the web disagree, and show me exactly what each source said.
proposals.why_useful: This catches expensive or embarrassing errors—stale dashboards, changed prices, conflicting appointment details, or a local document copied from an outdated page—while preserving the distinction between observed facts and inferred explanations.
surfaces: browser-extension reads the authenticated page and its current DOM
mac-vision or mac-terminal reads the local app/document view without leaving the Mac
relay performs an independent public-web read when a second source is needed
faculty-perception normalizes timestamps, URLs, content hashes, and confidence, then emits a contradiction record
faculty-judgement decides whether to interrupt the owner or wait for a request
pendant speaks only the concise conflict and offers the two source excerpts
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap structured extraction model for each source and a small text model for pairwise comparison; reserve realtime for the owner-facing interruption or follow-up.
proposals.latency_budget: On demand under 5 seconds; background checks should be scheduled and quiet, with interruption only when a high-confidence material contradiction is found.
proposals.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.08 per comparison, dominated by browser/vision extraction and source text; local DOM/accessibility cases can be effectively free.
proposals.security_concerns: Never send private local documents to a public relay read. Keep local evidence on the Mac, hash and redact excerpts, and require confirmation before quoting sensitive data aloud. Public pages must remain marked untrusted.
missing: A cross-source observation schema with source URL/app, capturedAt, content hash, and region
A local-only comparator that can compare private Mac evidence with public relay evidence without exporting the private body
A user policy for which contradiction severities may interrupt

proposals.user_asks: While I am working, quietly notice what I am trying to do from my screen and browser, and tell me the single next fact or action that would unblock me when I ask.
proposals.why_useful: It turns passive computer use into a useful second set of eyes: it can recognize a blocked login, missing attachment, error dialog, or form validation failure and answer “what’s blocking me?” without the owner narrating the screen.
surfaces: mac-vision watches only explicit snapshots or a user-triggered watch, not continuous raw recording
browser-extension reports the active tab, visible error state, and pending command state
mac-terminal and mac-planner inspect local job receipts or command output when the blocker is outside the browser
faculty-perception builds a compact state transition with evidence and freshness
faculty-judgement ranks one unblocker and respects quiet hours
relay-realtime and pendant deliver the answer on request
proposals.model_tier: A cheap local classifier handles stable UI states and diffs; use a stronger model only for ambiguous multi-app interpretation; realtime is only the final conversational turn.
proposals.latency_budget: Snapshot-to-state under 1 second locally; answer under 2 seconds on request. Watching is event-driven and rate-limited rather than a continuous vision stream.
proposals.cost_estimate: Mostly local compute; $0–$0.02 per ambiguous interpretation. Storage is bounded to hashes and short observations, not screenshots.
proposals.security_concerns: Explicit opt-in watch sessions with a physical/voice stop; exclude password managers, banking, private messages, and camera feeds by app policy. Do not retain screenshots by default; retain only redacted state transitions.
missing: An event-driven screen-diff/watch session with app and region exclusion policies
A blocker taxonomy and confidence-calibrated next-step ranking
A bounded observation ledger joinable to browser commands and Mac action receipts

proposals.user_asks: During a meeting, keep a private, time-aligned record of what was said, what appeared on my screen, and which commitments were actually made; when I ask afterward, tell me only what is supported by the recording and screen evidence.
proposals.why_useful: This gives the owner a reliable answer to “what did we agree to?” instead of a generic summary that blends spoken claims, slides, and model guesses. It can distinguish a commitment that was explicitly spoken from one merely inferred from a document or task list.
surfaces: pendant captures microphone audio locally, segments it, and emits quality/sequence metadata without continuously uploading raw audio
mac-vision captures explicit meeting-window frames and visible slide/document regions, keyed to the same monotonic timeline
browser-extension supplies authenticated meeting captions or collaborative-document changes when the owner opts into those tabs
relay stores encrypted session manifests and performs deferred transcription/alignment only after the meeting or on request
faculty-perception aligns transcript spans, screen evidence, speaker/source provenance, and clock uncertainty
faculty-judgement classifies explicit commitments versus suggestions and asks before creating reminders
mac-planner can create a reminder or task only after the owner confirms the evidence-backed draft
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background transcription/alignment model during or after the meeting; use a small extraction model for commitments and contradictions. Reserve realtime only for an owner question asked live through the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Live captions need not be instantaneous: 2–5 seconds is acceptable. Post-meeting evidence indexing may take 1–3 minutes. An owner query should answer within 5 seconds, or explicitly say the relevant segment is still processing.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.05–$0.50 per hour of meeting audio plus vision/text extraction, dominated by transcription and the number of selected screen frames; local-only mode can reduce cloud cost substantially.
proposals.security_concerns: Meeting audio, private screens, and authenticated documents are highly sensitive. Default to local encrypted storage, explicit per-session recording consent, visible recording state, participant-policy reminder, app/tab exclusions, configurable retention, and no reminder/task creation without confirmation. Relay receives only encrypted chunks or derived evidence when the owner enables cloud processing.
