changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can finally know whether a statement came from the physical pendant they are wearing, whether its firmware state is fresh, and whether audio was actually played—rather than receiving a plausible but Mac- or relay-authored status.
changes.effort: Medium hardware revision plus firmware, pairing, relay verification, key rotation, and recovery tooling. Design it as an optional board revision with a software fallback marked unverified.
changes.risk: Key loss or damaged hardware could strand the device; provide a recovery/re-pair ceremony that invalidates the old key, and never make unsigned legacy telemetry look trusted. Secure-element supply and driver integration are additional schedule risks.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $0.50–$2 per unit in volume, plus a few milliamps only during signing; negligible per-message API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Usually a few milliseconds per signed frame; batch counters/health data to avoid signing every audio packet.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves device authenticity, replay resistance, and provenance. It does not make content private by itself; transport encryption and redaction remain required.
depends_on: A defined signed telemetry envelope and device enrollment protocol
Relay-side verification and key revocation storage
The accepted offline-reality-beacon and playback acknowledgement firmware behaviors

changes.change: Add a provenance firewall to contextProjection: machine-origin preferences that affect interpretation (especially timezone, locale, identity, and permissions) cannot enter the high-priority Owner block unless they match a live authoritative resolver or have an explicit owner-origin confirmation. For the existing machine-origin America/Chicago fact, emit a contradiction warning and use live /etc/localtime America/New_York for Mac-resolved times; do not delete the stored fact automatically.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The live owner context currently injects "timezone: America/Chicago" with confidence 0.99 and useCount 5,374 even though this Mac resolves to America/New_York. That can shift routines, 'this morning,' and file/calendar interpretations while looking like an owner preference. The owner gets correct times and a visible warning instead of silent, repeated wrongness.
changes.effort: Medium: classify sensitive machine facts at projection time, add an authority resolver comparison, and expose a small warning in the briefing/ops view; no schema rewrite.
changes.risk: A legitimate travel or manually configured timezone could be suppressed. Recovery is explicit owner confirmation, which promotes the fact to owner origin; retain the old row for audit rather than mutating it. Never infer the owner's physical location from the Mac zone.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost; a local comparison per projection and a few bytes of warning metadata.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible, under a few milliseconds locally.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing machine-derived permissions/timezone/identity from masquerading as owner intent; does not expose secret fact values.
depends_on: A live machine-authority resolver for /etc/localtime (already established)
A way for the owner to confirm or reject a sensitive fact (existing memory fact controls or a new explicit confirmation surface)

changes.change: Make the browser extension heartbeat publish a signed capability bitmap and active-session freshness, not merely online=true. The current live extension is online on Safari at Wikipedia, but its status advertises capabilities: [] and no nonce; planners therefore cannot distinguish 'connected but cannot inspect/click' from 'bridge broken'. Add explicit read/click/type/observe capabilities, extension version, tab identity hash, and heartbeat age, and have relay/mac planning refuse unsupported actions before issuing a command.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner says the browser may read and click without asking, yet the live system currently reports an online browser with zero capabilities. This causes avoidable failed requests and makes the assistant unable to truthfully say whether it can act on the page in front of him. He gets reliable 'I can read/click this tab' or an immediate explanation instead of a timeout.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: heartbeat schema, extension permission-to-capability mapping, relay snapshot normalization, and planner preflight. No screen capture is needed for the capability advertisement.
changes.risk: A stale or over-optimistic bitmap could authorize an action the extension no longer supports. Sign/version the bitmap, expire it quickly, and require a fresh heartbeat before mutation; fall back to read-only when uncertain.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost; a few hundred bytes per heartbeat and negligible relay storage.
changes.latency_impact: Removes failed command round trips; adds at most one heartbeat freshness check.
changes.security_impact: Capability declarations must not grant authority: enforce them server-side and keep owner confirmation rules for destructive browser actions. Hash tab URLs/titles in telemetry unless the action requires the exact page.
depends_on: Browser extension heartbeat route POST /browser/heartbeat
GET /browser/status and GET /browser/poll
A shared capability enum between extension and Mac planner
Freshness enforcement in browser command dispatch

changes.change: Add a signed, short-lived reality token produced by faculty-perception. It binds browser tab/session fingerprint, Mac permission readiness, relay reachability, target capsule hash, and freshness timestamps; /plan and /execute must reject or downgrade any action whose token is absent, expired, or mismatched.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The assistant stops acting on yesterday's page or a different logged-in account and can explain precisely what changed instead of failing silently.
changes.effort: Medium: token schema, joiners, and enforcement in planner/action plus tests for stale and mismatched surfaces.
changes.risk: A false stale result may delay an action; recovery is a fresh read and re-plan. Never make the token a bypass around owner confirmation.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and hashing; no per-action model call.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–400 ms for cached checks, up to one browser read when stale.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by binding actions to observed targets; signed token must contain pseudonyms and hashes, never page secrets.
depends_on: Browser provenance route mounting
Relay browser-read ID/hash bridge
Defined freshness policy for each surface

changes.change: Introduce a contradiction quarantine for machine-originated pinned facts: when a live authoritative source disagrees, keep the fact immutable but exclude it from the default context projection until the owner reviews it; record the competing source, scope, and observed timestamps.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A stale machine preference can no longer silently steer every reminder and schedule while still remaining available for audit and explicit recovery.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: projection filter, review endpoint/UI, and a deterministic authority matrix; no new fact schema required.
changes.risk: An over-aggressive filter could hide a legitimate preference. Recovery is one-click restore or explicit owner confirmation; owner-origin facts remain untouched.
changes.cost_impact: Minimal; bounded metadata only.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible projection overhead.
changes.security_impact: Reduces unauthorized inference and makes provenance visible; do not transmit raw competing values to relay unless needed.
depends_on: Provenance-aware contradiction detector
Owner review surface
Authority scopes for machine, browser, relay, and owner facts

changes.change: Add a postcondition evidence bundle to every Mac/browser action: after execution, use the now-live Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions to capture a bounded redacted UI observation, attach its content hash and capsuleId to the existing job receipt, and classify the outcome as observed-success, observed-failure, or unknown. Propagate the same correlation ID to relay jobs and browser commands.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop hearing “done” when a button did nothing or a page stayed unchanged; the system can show what was visibly true after it acted and recover from the actual failure.
changes.effort: Medium: instrument the existing action/receipt finalization and browser result paths, call the already-mounted evidence capsule machinery, and add a reducer over existing job/pipeline records.
changes.risk: Screenshots may capture secrets or transient UI; redact before persistence, cap size, and fall back to unknown if capture fails. Never retry side effects automatically based only on a screenshot.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage increase within existing evidence caps; one screenshot-vision classification only when DOM/result data is insufficient.
changes.latency_impact: Adds about 0.5–3 s to actions requiring a screenshot; structured browser results can avoid the screenshot.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability but increases local sensitive-data exposure; keep raw pixels local, store hashes/redacted regions, and require explicit domain exclusions.
depends_on: Accessibility and Screen Recording are now live (verified via GET /ops/status).
Mount and invoke the existing evidenceCapsules/browserProvenance modules on the action completion path.
Define a shared correlation ID across relay, Mac, browser, and pipeline records.

changes.change: Add a perception freshness firewall: before judgement or action consumes a machine, browser, relay, or memory fact, attach an observedAt/source/cursor and classify it fresh, stale, contradicted, or structurally unavailable. Block high-impact actions when the required fact has no current witness; allow low-risk narration with an explicit uncertainty label.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: It prevents the system from acting on a stale timezone preference, a browser tab that changed, a Mac job marked complete before playback, or a relay device row that disappeared because of caps. The owner gets fewer confident-but-wrong actions, not merely a nicer dashboard.
changes.effort: Medium: shared structured envelope plus adapters around perception and judgement; no new model training
changes.risk: Over-blocking when a source is temporarily offline. Recover with a user-visible reason, a bounded recheck, and an explicit confirm-to-proceed path; never downgrade unknown to false.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero API cost; one small structured validation pass. Storage is bounded cursor metadata, not page content.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50-150 ms for local freshness checks; remote rechecks only when a high-impact action needs them.
changes.security_impact: Improves least disclosure because validators can pass hashes/statuses instead of raw browser content; provenance metadata still needs access control.
depends_on: A durable source/cursor contract for the proposed away-diff witness
Mount browser provenance routes and return capsule/hash metadata for relay browser reads
Define a real pendant playback event and device-originated health identity

changes.change: Add a cross-surface routine collision and freshness gate: before scheduler execution, group enabled routines by local firing instant and semantic overlap, compare their last successful run and output receipts, then present one merged run or ask which to keep. Record the decision and suppress only the duplicate invocation, never delete routines automatically.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently has multiple daily routines at 07:00 and multiple at 17:00, including overlapping briefs. This can produce duplicate spoken interruptions and stale audio while making the system look healthy. One coherent brief is more useful than several 'completed' runs.
changes.effort: Medium: scheduler-side grouping, Mac timezone resolution, lightweight semantic similarity, and a reversible decision record in the routine-run history.
changes.risk: A genuinely distinct routine could be merged or skipped. Recovery is a preview-first collision report, conservative threshold, and one-click 'run separately' override; no automatic routine deletion.
changes.cost_impact: <$0.01/day for semantic comparison if needed; deterministic timestamp grouping is free.
changes.latency_impact: Adds <1 second before a scheduled run; no impact on audio generation.
changes.security_impact: Routine names and commands stay within relay/Mac stores; do not send command text to an external model unless the owner permits it.
depends_on: GET /routines
GET /routines/:routineId/runs
POST /routines/:routineId/run
GET /pipeline
GET /ops/snapshot
Authoritative America/New_York timezone for Mac-resolved firing times

changes.change: Add an explicit, read-only `attention_frame` operation to the Mac agent. In one bounded call it returns focused app/window, frontmost browser tab, accessibility-selected element bounds and role/name, visible-text digest, capture timestamp, and a redacted screenshot region; it must fail closed when the target app is sensitive or the frame is older than a caller-supplied freshness limit. Expose the same frame id to browser inspection and action receipts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask “what’s that?” or “why is this stuck?” and get an answer grounded in exactly what is on screen now, rather than a stale app name or an uncorrelated screenshot.
changes.effort: Medium: local Accessibility/Screen Recording plumbing is now live and verified; add one route, redaction policy, and joins to existing browser/action records.
changes.risk: The wrong UI region could be described with high confidence, or sensitive text could leak. Recover by returning ambiguity and no body, recording only hashes by default, and requiring a fresh explicit capture for sensitive apps.
changes.cost_impact: Low API cost; local capture and OCR dominate. No persistent screenshot storage by default.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for accessibility/DOM extraction, up to 1–2 s only for vision fallback.
changes.security_impact: Improves security if it centralizes app exclusions and redaction; must treat Screen Recording output as sensitive and never send raw frames to the relay by default.
depends_on: Current live TCC state (Accessibility and Screen Recording are now granted)
A short-lived grounding-id contract shared with browser inspection and Mac action receipts
A local sensitive-app/field exclusion list

changes.change: Make every projected machine fact carry an authority-and-freshness envelope into judgement: source origin, observedAt, expiresAt, and whether it is a live measurement or a pinned preference. Reject machine-derived preferences that contradict a newer local measurement instead of injecting them into the Owner head.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner should never receive actions based on a stale machine claim such as the pinned America/Chicago timezone when the Mac is actually America/New_York. Contradictions would become visible and self-correcting without deleting the owner's data.
changes.effort: Medium: projection metadata, contradiction detector, and a judgement-side refusal path.
changes.risk: Some familiar commands become clarification questions until the conflict is resolved; recover by showing both values and their provenance.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime cost; one small metadata block per projection.
changes.latency_impact: Under 50 ms locally; no model call for agreeing facts.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by preventing broad projection of low-authority facts; preserves secrets and does not copy values to the relay.
depends_on: GET /memory/projection
GET /machine-context
GET /ops/snapshot

changes.change: Add a live-fact reconciliation pass before every context projection: compare machine-origin preferences and cached device/browser claims against fresh /ops/status, /machine-context, filesystem timezone, browser heartbeat, and relay health. Emit a signed observation with observedAt, source, freshness, and contradiction links; demote (never delete) a cached fact when live evidence disagrees, and make the model see the contradiction explicitly.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops receiving answers based on a pinned but wrong machine preference (for example America/Chicago while the Mac is America/New_York), or on a browser/device state that went stale minutes ago. Corrections happen automatically without rewriting the owner's memory.
changes.effort: Medium: deterministic comparator plus projection metadata and a small set of source adapters; no new model training.
changes.risk: A transient outage could demote a good fact. Require two consecutive contradictory observations or a freshness timeout, preserve the old row with provenance, and show 'live check unavailable' rather than treating missing data as false.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local status read per projection, optionally cached for 30–60 seconds.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms locally when cache is warm; bounded parallel reads otherwise.
changes.security_impact: The model receives more operational metadata. Keep URLs, mail subjects, and device identifiers redacted unless the user asks; never export raw secrets from memory.
depends_on: A mounted, bounded live-observation adapter for /ops/status and filesystem timezone
Projection support for source, observedAt, freshness, and contradiction metadata
A policy that distinguishes source.origin:'owner' from source.origin:'machine'

changes.change: Make every scheduled brief a freshness-graded bundle rather than a single completed string: at fire time, collect per-source observedAt/age, timezone used, permission state, and retrieval result; refuse to present stale or missing sections as current, and attach a compact machine-readable receipt that the pendant/relay can later quote.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A 'completed' morning brief would finally mean the calendar, mail, files, and news were each checked—or the owner would hear exactly which section was unavailable or stale. It prevents a polished three-sentence lie when one source silently timed out.
changes.effort: Medium: add source-level receipt fields to routine runs and change the brief composer to enforce freshness thresholds; existing routine scheduler and Mac automation remain usable.
changes.risk: Freshness thresholds may make a brief feel incomplete during outages. Use explicit labels ('calendar checked 2m ago', 'mail unavailable') and let the owner override thresholds per routine.
changes.cost_impact: Small extra reads; no additional model call if the composer uses deterministic status labels. News/browser retrieval may add normal search cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds parallel source checks, typically under 1 second; cap the routine at a fixed deadline and preserve partial results with warnings.
changes.security_impact: Receipts must store metadata and hashes, not mail bodies or private file contents; spoken output should never expose URLs or subjects unless requested.
depends_on: Per-source observation schema with observedAt, age, status, and redaction class
Routine-run receipt support beyond one aggregate completed flag
Live Mac permission and timezone observations (currently available: permissions.ready=true and America/New_York)
Relay/browser source result IDs for cloud-fetched material

changes.change: Now that the live Mac snapshot reports Accessibility and Screen Recording granted for com.aipendant.agent, add a startup readiness transition that runs one harmless observe-only computer-use probe, records the binary identity, permission result, and timestamp, and exposes a short-lived 'visual control verified' lease to mac-vision. If the probe fails later, invalidate the lease rather than letting the planner assume readiness.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets reliable visual computer control instead of a green permission badge that may not match the running process. It also makes the newly granted capability usable immediately and makes regressions explainable.
changes.effort: Small integration change plus one observe-only probe and tests; no new model or hardware.
changes.risk: The probe must not click, type, navigate, or capture sensitive content. If the probe is too strict, visual control may be disabled; recover by falling back to AppleScript/browser actions and re-probing on the next startup.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local probe per startup.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 1 second at startup, no per-turn cost.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by binding readiness to the exact signed app identity and expiring the lease. Do not store screenshots; store only status and timestamp.
depends_on: GET /ops/snapshot
GET /observe
GET /ops/status
mac-vision computer-use loop

changes.change: Turn on a permission-aware screen-grounded verification stage for every computer-use action: capture a redacted pre-state observation, execute the action, capture post-state, and require the observed postcondition to match the planned result before reporting success. Persist only hashes, action IDs, and a small failure crop; if observation is unavailable, report 'executed, unverified' rather than success.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The agent can now actually see and control the Mac: /ops/status reports Accessibility and Screen Recording trusted, computer-use enabled, and the browser extension online. The owner will stop hearing confident claims that a click or edit worked when the UI did something else.
changes.effort: Medium: wire the existing vision loop and action ledger together, add postcondition checks for the common action types, and expose a concise receipt.
changes.risk: Screenshots may contain secrets; redact and cap them, and never persist full frames by default. False mismatch could cause a harmless retry or pause; recovery is to show the owner the failed postcondition and offer a manual retry.
changes.cost_impact: One extra vision observation per action; roughly $0.01–$0.05 for complex actions, negligible for simple DOM/browser actions.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds per verified action.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing unverified destructive actions from being reported as complete; needs strict crop/redaction and confirmation gates for mail, deletion, and purchases.
depends_on: Use the now-live permissions shown by GET /ops/status: Accessibility trusted, Screen Recording granted, permissions.ready=true
Existing computer-use loop and vision model
Existing action ledger and job receipts

changes.change: Add a non-destructive authority-check before contextProjection emits pinned preferences: compare machine-origin facts against the live authority that resolves that domain (for timezone, /etc/localtime), mark mismatches as contested, exclude them from the ## Owner head, and surface the exact stale value plus its origin for owner confirmation. Never delete or rewrite the fact automatically.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently receives America/Chicago as a high-confidence pinned preference even though this Mac resolves to America/New_York; the stale machine fact has been used 5,374 times. This prevents wrong scheduling, 'this morning' interpretation, and quiet-hour behavior without silently changing something that belongs to the owner.
changes.effort: Moderate: authority adapters for timezone first, then calendar/account/device domains; projection filtering and a small diagnostic record. Existing memory provenance already supplies source.origin and confidence.
changes.risk: A legitimate travel or remote-machine preference could be hidden. Recovery is straightforward: retain the contested fact, show it in the diagnostic view, and allow an owner-confirmed override with explicit scope (machine vs owner).
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local comparison per projection and a bounded diagnostic entry.
changes.latency_impact: Under 10 ms locally for timezone; other adapters may require cached reads, never a blocking cloud call for ordinary prompts.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing machine-injected values from masquerading as owner intent. Do not expose secret fact values in diagnostics; expose provenance and conflict reason only.
depends_on: A stable authority registry identifying which source wins for each fact domain.
A projection hook that can suppress contested machine-origin facts without deleting them.

changes.change: Install a provenance-aware timezone guard in contextProjection and routine scheduling: machine-origin timezone preferences cannot override the authoritative Mac zone, and any contradictory pinned preference is surfaced as a quarantine warning rather than injected into the Owner context head. Keep the stored fact untouched until the owner explicitly edits or deletes it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Routines, 'this morning,' quiet hours, and file times stop silently using America/Chicago when this Mac is actually America/New_York. The owner gets a visible warning instead of repeatedly receiving a wrong timezone in every prompt.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: add a guard at projection/scheduling boundaries, record the contradiction with source and timestamps, and add regression tests for owner-origin versus machine-origin preferences.
changes.risk: A legitimate travel timezone could be suppressed if the owner intended it but never recorded that intent. Recovery is explicit confirmation or editing the preference; never delete the existing fact automatically.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost and no hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Effectively none; one local comparison against /etc/localtime.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing a high-confidence machine-derived fact from controlling reminders or actions. Do not expose unrelated memory values in the warning.
depends_on: GET /machine-context
GET /memory/projection
A provenance-preserving context projection hook
An owner-confirmation path for changing pinned preferences

changes.change: When /ops/status reports permissions.ready=true and browser extension online, route ambiguous visual requests to the Mac vision loop instead of declaring the surface inaccessible; require a read-only screenshot/DOM observation first, then pass the resulting evidence capsule to judgement and action. If the browser capability list is empty, keep browser writes disabled even though the heartbeat is online.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner now has Accessibility and Screen Recording granted, so the system can genuinely inspect the Mac UI. This turns previously blocked visual questions into answers while preventing an online-but-non-actionable browser bridge from being mistaken for control.
changes.effort: Small routing/policy change plus one integration test covering permissions ready, browser online with empty capabilities, and a stale screenshot.
changes.risk: A screenshot can contain secrets or the wrong app; enforce redaction, active-window/URL checks, and confirmation before writes. Recover by falling back to AppleScript/read-only browser inspection and saying unknown.
changes.cost_impact: One vision call only for genuinely ambiguous visual tasks; otherwise zero additional model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–3 seconds only when visual ambiguity exists.
changes.security_impact: Screen content leaves the Mac only through the existing consented vision path; do not upload captures when a DOM or AppleScript read suffices.
depends_on: Existing granted Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions
Existing GET /ops/status or GET /ops/snapshot permission state
Existing mac-vision loop and browser inspection routes
Evidence capsule redaction before judgement/action

changes.change: Create a signed, bounded ‘observation frame’ at every action boundary. The Mac agent records source-specific observedAt/age, origin (owner, machine, relay, browser, device), freshness deadline, and contradiction IDs; the relay carries the frame hash into the job/receipt, while the browser bridge attaches its tab heartbeat and the pendant later attaches its beacon sequence. The planner must consume the frame and either cite the live observation or label the input unknown before acting.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the system says ‘done’ or schedules something, the owner can see whether that conclusion came from a live Mac/browser observation, relay acceptance, old pipeline history, or no device at all. Newly granted Accessibility and Screen Recording make the Mac side observable now; this turns that access into honest answers rather than invisible extra control.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared observation-frame schema, Mac capture middleware, relay propagation, browser heartbeat join, planner policy, and Ops UI/voice rendering.
changes.risk: Clock skew, stale frames, and partial propagation could falsely look authoritative. Recover by using monotonic age plus wall-clock timestamps, expiring frames aggressively, and treating missing hashes as unknown rather than accepting the action.
changes.cost_impact: Small disk/ring-buffer overhead and a few hundred bytes per job; negligible API cost. No routine SD writes on the pendant; use the accepted bounded NVS playback/reality records.
changes.latency_impact: ~10–30 ms locally; no extra model turn. A fresh browser or Mac probe may add up to 1–2 seconds only when the cached frame is expired.
changes.security_impact: Improves provenance but adds metadata linking actions across surfaces. Hash content, redact browser/page text, scope frames to the owner/session, and never export secrets or raw screenshots to the relay.
depends_on: The live Mac permissions now report ready, so capture can run today.
A relay route/field to carry an observation-frame hash through jobs and receipts.
The accepted offline-reality-beacon and audio_delivery_ack_queue when a real pendant is registered.
A browser heartbeat/result join that preserves tab identity without exposing page contents.

changes.change: Install a perception gate before every realtime answer and action plan: deterministic checks first validate source authority, freshness, device presence, and evidence class; route unresolved interpretation to a cheap background model; allow the realtime model to speak only the resulting claims and uncertainty labels. Cache the normalized observation set for one turn so it is not re-sent and re-inferred repeatedly.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant will stop confidently saying that a Mac job completed, a relay announcement was heard, or a machine-written preference is the owner's intent. Short answers become more trustworthy without making every routine or voice turn pay for an expensive model.
changes.effort: Medium: define observation/claim types, add a preflight middleware to realtime tool results and action planning, and write tests for stale, absent, contradictory, and ungrounded evidence.
changes.risk: Overly strict gating could make the assistant say unknown too often. Recover by logging the rejected claim with its reason and allowing an explicit owner override; never silently downgrade an unknown to false.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces realtime-token spend and repeated context transmission; adds a small deterministic CPU/cache cost and occasional cheap background calls.
changes.latency_impact: Usually decreases latency; a background explanation may add up to 1–2 seconds only for contradictions or missing provenance.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by preventing untrusted relay page text and stale state from authorizing actions; does not broaden permissions.
depends_on: A normalized evidence contract with source, authority scope, observedAt, freshness, and confidence
A mounted browser provenance path for grounded browser claims
A real pendant playback event when a pendant exists

changes.change: Add a provenance gate to contextProjection: machine-origin facts of kind preference must never enter the cacheable '## Owner' head unless explicitly promoted by the owner. Keep them in a separately labeled machine-context section with a short freshness/contradiction marker; when a machine-origin preference conflicts with a live machine observation, automatically downgrade it to a warning rather than letting confidence and useCount make it dominate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing wrong personal settings as if he stated them. In particular, the pinned machine-written America/Chicago preference would no longer override the live America/New_York system zone in every prompt, preventing wrong routine times and date interpretations.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: change projection selection and add a provenance/contradiction test; preserve the existing fact rather than deleting it, and expose a one-line repair suggestion.
changes.risk: Some useful machine defaults may disappear from the owner-facing context until promoted. Recovery is straightforward: show the quarantined value and allow explicit promotion; keep audit metadata so no fact is silently lost.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime/API cost; a few hundred bytes of context when a conflict exists.
changes.latency_impact: No meaningful latency change; one deterministic filter and optional local-zone comparison.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy and authority boundaries by preventing machine-derived values from being represented as owner intent.
depends_on: GET /machine-context for live machine authority
GET /memory/projection for current projection behavior
A provenance-aware contextProjection change; no new hardware or permissions required

changes.change: Put relay-fetched browser text and routine announcement speech behind a privacy-preserving quarantine: attach source URL, content hash, sensitivity class, and expiry to each record; store only a redacted preview by default; enforce deletion at expiry for announcements and captured audio; reject relay persistence when no provenance/sensitivity decision exists.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A page the owner asked the relay to read should not become an untraceable, permanent copy of private web content. The owner gets a clear answer to what was retained, why, and until when, with sensitive text disappearing automatically.
changes.effort: Medium: extend serverBrowser read results and routine composition, add D1 deletion/sweep, and expose a retention/provenance view. Existing Mac evidence capsule fields can be reused rather than inventing a schema.
changes.risk: A too-aggressive classifier could remove useful context or make a routine fail. Recover by retaining a hash and source metadata, allowing explicit owner-approved retention, and making deletion auditable without restoring the body.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and CPU overhead; likely lower long-term D1/audio storage. No model cost for hashes and rules; optional classifier costs <$0.005 per page.
changes.latency_impact: <50 ms for hashing/rule checks; asynchronous sweep. A model classifier must not sit on the interactive speech path unless the content is about to be spoken.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves privacy: no raw page body by default, source-linked records, enforced expiry, and a tombstone for deletion. URLs may themselves be sensitive and should be redacted to origin/path policy.
depends_on: A relay-side provenance ID/content-hash bridge to the existing Mac evidence capsule schema
A sensitivity classifier or browser-field annotations
A real scheduled deletion worker for relay announcements and audio

changes.change: Add a provenance firewall before contextProjection emits the pinned Owner block: for machine-origin preferences and high-confidence facts, run a read-only contradiction check against authoritative live sources (for example /etc/localtime via machine-context and current device/relay status). If contradicted, keep the stored fact untouched but emit it in a quarantined 'machine claim conflicts with live fact' section with source, age, and override reason; never inject it into the cacheable Owner head until the owner confirms it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops receiving a wrong, machine-authored fact as if it were their own preference. Today the stale America/Chicago timezone is pinned at confidence 0.99 and injected into every prompt despite the Mac being America/New_York. Quarantine makes the disagreement visible without silently rewriting the owner's memory.
changes.effort: Moderate: contradiction rules, a quarantine projection section, and tests for provenance/source.origin; no new storage schema required.
changes.risk: A live source can itself be stale or scoped incorrectly; show both claims and timestamps rather than deleting either. Recovery is owner confirmation or an explicit override. Avoid running arbitrary network probes during prompt construction.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime cost for local facts; one cheap structured check per projection, no model call.
changes.latency_impact: Tens of milliseconds locally; cache the check briefly and invalidate on machine-context refresh.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing untrusted machine claims from becoming owner intent. Keep raw sensitive fact values out of telemetry; record only source and conflict class.
depends_on: The existing source.origin field and contextProjection path
GET /machine-context and its authoritative timezone observation
An owner-confirmation route or existing memory fact edit flow

changes.change: Add a 'safe handoff' mode that turns a long-running Mac/browser operation into an owner-visible state machine: the Mac pauses at the next irreversible boundary, the relay sends a compact state summary to the pendant, and the owner can resume, narrow, or cancel with a physical button. Every resume carries a new scoped lease; an old voice turn or stale browser command cannot continue it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can walk away from a fragile multi-step task without wondering whether it kept clicking, sent a message, or got stuck. They can resume from the pendant with a truthful checkpoint and cancel even when they are not at the Mac.
changes.effort: High: add pause points and lease enforcement to Mac/browser executors, relay state transitions, pendant control frames, and a dashboard showing the checkpoint.
changes.risk: A pause may leave an external site in a partially completed state; only pause at declared safe boundaries and expose the last confirmed side effect. Recover with idempotency keys and an explicit cancel/undo path where available.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost; a few relay state writes per step. Engineering cost is in executor instrumentation and firmware controls.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second control response when connected; offline pendant commands must be queued with expiry and never blindly replayed.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by making continuation leases device-bound, single-use, and expiring. Never let a stale queued command resume a privileged browser session.
depends_on: A common operation state/lease contract across /jobs, browser commands, and relay jobs
Pendant control/ack frames and offline queue semantics
Existing action ledger and job receipts being exposed as checkpoint evidence

changes.change: Replace the binary pendant online/offline label with a three-state presence contract: connected (active authenticated WebSocket), recently-heard (last device-originated beacon/heartbeat within a bounded window), and registry-stale (row exists but no device-originated evidence). A converse connection must update a session-scoped lastConnectedAt without pretending it is a heartbeat; the Mac bridge must never author pendant lastSeenAt. Surface the state and evidence source in /v1/devices/status and the dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the pendant disappears, the owner can tell whether it is powered off, merely has no LTE, or is an old registry row. Today “offline” can mean “never heartbeated,” while a Mac-authored timestamp can look like pendant health; this prevents false reassurance and false outage reports.
changes.effort: Moderate relay schema/response and firmware beacon integration; retain old fields for compatibility and add evidenceSource, activeSession, and state.
changes.risk: Clients that assume boolean online may mis-handle the new state. Keep online as a deprecated derived field, add contract tests, and make unknown/stale conservative (never claim connected).
changes.cost_impact: Tiny D1 write on connect/heartbeat and bounded row growth; no model cost.
changes.latency_impact: No added conversational latency; status reads add one small field computation.
changes.security_impact: Do not expose bearer credentials or raw socket identifiers. Authenticate beacon/heartbeat with the scoped pendant credential rather than the current admin-key WebSocket path.
depends_on: offline-reality-beacon firmware skill
a real nRF pendant registration/heartbeat writer
GET /v1/devices/status on the cloud relay rather than the Mac agent
relay D1 persistence

changes.change: Add a low-power skin/proximity presence sensor to the pendant enclosure (for example, capacitive electrode plus a simple contact/ambient baseline), sampled locally and represented as coarse worn / nearby / absent state. Fuse it with the existing offline health frame, but never transmit raw sensor values or treat presence as proof of identity.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The system can stop speaking as though the owner is wearing the pendant when it is sitting on a desk or plugged in for bench work, and can choose a Mac/browser fallback without asking the owner to explain why the wearable is not being heard.
changes.effort: Moderate enclosure/PCB revision, calibration across clothing and charging states, and a small firmware state machine; explicitly not a software-only patch.
changes.risk: False absent/worn readings could suppress a useful response. Recover by using presence only as a confidence signal, retaining an unmistakable manual override, and falling back to Mac delivery rather than dropping content.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $1–$4 BOM increase and sub-mW average draw; enclosure and PCB rework dominate cost.
changes.latency_impact: Sensor state available within roughly 1–2 seconds; no conversational model latency.
changes.security_impact: Local coarse state only; no camera, microphone, biometric identity, or raw capacitance leaves the device.
depends_on: A physical pendant enclosure/PCB revision
offline-reality-beacon frame schema
relay delivery policy that can consume a non-authoritative presence hint

changes.change: Add a provenance-aware quarantine rule for machine-originated facts of kind preference that conflict with authoritative live machine state. Keep the original immutable, but exclude it from the prompt head and mark it needs-review until the owner confirms or a fresh owner-originated value supersedes it. Apply first to preference.timezone=America/Chicago versus /etc/localtime America/New_York.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops receiving a confidently wrong timezone in every prompt, so “this morning,” routine times, and quiet hours resolve correctly without silently deleting their memory.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: add conflict detector, projection filter, and review item; test against existing memory provenance.
changes.risk: A machine-derived preference could be quarantined when it was intentional. Recovery is one owner confirmation; original row remains intact and visible in review.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local memory read/write only.
changes.latency_impact: A few milliseconds on projection, with cached conflict checks.
changes.security_impact: Improves provenance safety; never exposes secret fact values in diagnostics beyond existing owner projection.
depends_on: Authoritative timezone resolver for the Mac
source.origin retained in memory projection
Owner review/confirmation route

changes.change: Introduce a trust ledger that records, per answer, the freshest supporting observation, its source surface, age, and whether it is direct evidence, derived state, or an unverified claim; expire trust independently from the underlying event stores.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The system can say “browser is online but the pendant has been offline for 32 minutes” instead of blending stale and live facts into one confident answer.
changes.effort: Medium: deterministic trust records and projection fields, then wire dashboard and voice summary.
changes.risk: False precision if clocks or source timestamps are wrong. Recovery is to label clock-skew and downgrade confidence rather than infer.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and compute; no model call required for the ledger.
changes.latency_impact: Near-zero for cached summaries; small join cost on refresh.
changes.security_impact: Metadata-only by default, with redaction of URLs, message text, and secrets.
depends_on: read_continuity_snapshot
source freshness metadata
clock-skew handling
dashboard trust rendering

changes.change: Change device presence semantics from a single online boolean to explicit states: live (<90s heartbeat), stale-registered (seen before but no heartbeat), never-seen, and unobservable. Include observedAt, source (device heartbeat vs Mac-authored registry), registry age, and an evidence note in /v1/devices/status and the continuity snapshot. Never label nrf9160-pendant simply offline when its converse path does not heartbeat.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can immediately tell “the pendant is disconnected now,” “this device was only paired months ago,” and “we have no device evidence,” instead of treating a stale row as a current outage or believing a Mac bridge heartbeat proves a pendant is alive.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: relay schema/normalizer, status consumers, and dashboard copy; add tests around stale and restart-erased memory stores.
changes.risk: Existing clients may assume boolean online and misclassify new states. Preserve online for compatibility, add presenceState and migrate consumers; recover by reverting the presentation layer without changing records.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and compute; no model cost.
changes.latency_impact: None for reads; status computation is local.
changes.security_impact: Avoid exposing device identifiers beyond existing authenticated scope; source labels reduce false trust but do not add access.
depends_on: Pendant heartbeat or offline-reality-beacon frames when hardware is actually connected

changes.change: Add a perception-only 'truth ladder' record for each cross-surface operation: observed_at, source, correlation ID, and one of intent_queued, mac_executed, relay_accepted, socket_sent, device_received, playback_started, playback_finished, or unknown. Derive it from existing Mac receipts, relay job state, browser results, and the pendant's offline-reality-beacon / audio-delivery queue; never infer a higher rung from a lower one. Surface stale pendant registration as 'known but not recently reachable,' not simply offline.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks whether something happened, the system can answer precisely—'the Mac saved it, but the pendant was unreachable'—instead of saying completed when nobody heard it. It also turns the newly visible stale nrf9160-pendant row into useful reality rather than an alarming false outage.
changes.effort: Medium: schema and derivation in the Mac/relay perception layer, correlation propagation in existing job and browser calls, and a small firmware event adapter. No new owner-facing UI is required initially.
changes.risk: A malformed or delayed event could leave the ladder at unknown; recovery is to retain raw lower-level evidence and recompute. Never delete contradictory observations. The 90-second registry threshold must not be used as proof of physical absence.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage (bounded records, roughly 0.5-2 KB per operation) and <$0.01/query; no routine cloud model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds for local derivation; remote relay reconciliation can be eventual.
changes.security_impact: High benefit if identifiers are pseudonymized and content is redacted. Do not copy audio or page bodies into the ladder; store hashes, capsule IDs, and permission-scoped links.
depends_on: the accepted offline-reality-beacon and audio_delivery_ack_queue behavior
a callable bounded USB serial diagnostic for bench verification
mounting the existing browserProvenance routes
a relay reader for the existing pendant event route and playback stage

changes.change: Create a cross-surface 'commit capsule' around consequential actions: before execution, capture a compact redacted snapshot of relevant Mac, browser, iOS, and relay state plus the exact intended mutation; after execution, capture independent post-state observations. Store a compensating-action plan that can be replayed in reverse order, and refuse to claim atomic success when one surface commits while another does not.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one understandable promise—either all requested surfaces changed, or the system tells them precisely where it stopped and offers a safe recovery—rather than discovering later that a calendar, browser, phone, and relay ended up disagreeing.
changes.effort: High: requires a shared transaction ID, pre/post observers on each surface, reversible operation contracts, and a coordinator that handles partial failure. It should begin with a small set of supported operations and expand.
changes.risk: Some actions cannot be undone (messages sent, purchases, external edits). Those must be marked non-compensable and require confirmation before commit. Recovery must never blindly replay an old action against changed state; compare hashes and ask the owner when preconditions differ.
changes.cost_impact: Small bounded local storage per transaction (roughly 5-20 KB of redacted metadata); <$0.02 per complex transaction for reconciliation, with no need for realtime inference after planning.
changes.latency_impact: Adds 0.5-2 seconds for preflight snapshots and post-state verification; external sites may make verification slower.
changes.security_impact: Snapshots must redact secrets and page bodies, retain hashes and locators only where possible, and be encrypted locally. Cross-surface correlation IDs must not be exposed to untrusted browser content.
depends_on: a shared correlation and action-digest protocol across relay, Mac, browser, and iOS
read-only post-state observers for each surface
operation-specific compensating actions
the existing Mac action ledger, browser result records, job receipts, and undo routes

changes.change: Add a deterministic provenance-and-freshness fence to context assembly: every injected fact carries source.origin, observedAt/lastUsedAt, expiry, confidence, and contradiction status; machine-origin preferences are never rendered under the unqualified “Owner” heading when a live machine observation disagrees. Emit a compact conflict object for judgement and dashboard review, without changing or deleting the owner's stored fact.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops receiving a wrong, pinned machine-derived preference as if he personally stated it, while preserving the fact for explicit review. Future actions can say “this is machine-derived and contradicted” instead of silently using it.
changes.effort: Medium: projection schema/renderer, conflict comparator against machine-context, tests for timezone-like contradictions, and dashboard display.
changes.risk: Some prompts get longer and some previously automatic actions become cautious. Recover by falling back to the old value only when the owner explicitly confirms it; never mutate the source row automatically.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and model cost; deterministic local computation.
changes.latency_impact: Tens of milliseconds in local projection assembly.
changes.security_impact: Improves provenance handling; must keep secret fact values redacted in conflict summaries and preserve source sensitivity.
depends_on: Use the existing GET /memory/projection and GET /machine-context data; do not create a parallel memory store.
Owner confirmation path for correcting or retiring a fact.

changes.change: Make /observe a mandatory, read-only preflight for every computer-use turn: capture foreground app, secure-input state, inputReachability status, browser tab identity, and timestamp; attach that observation ID to the action ledger and postcondition receipt. Refuse to claim a UI action reached the screen if the preflight is stale, secure input is active, or reachability is unverified.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Now that the exact agent has Accessibility and Screen Recording, actions can genuinely reach the screen. The owner gets fewer invisible clicks and can see which app/tab the system actually acted on, instead of trusting a generic 'success'.
changes.effort: Medium: wire existing /observe output into action ledger and receipt creation; no new permission work.
changes.risk: A stale or overly strict preflight could delay harmless actions. Recover by allowing a user-confirmed retry and recording the reason rather than silently bypassing it.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local HTTP read per action batch.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 20–100 ms locally.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by recording focus and secure-input boundaries; never persist screenshots or typed secret text.
depends_on: Keep /observe read-only and timestamped
Mount the existing browser provenance/evidence linkage into action receipts

changes.change: Add an evidence-fence router: before any model is allowed to say an action completed, it must classify the claim as observed, inferred, stale, or unknown from independent source records. High-impact actions require a second-source postcondition; absence of a pendant playback event can never be upgraded by Mac completion. Route only unresolved contradictions to the expensive realtime model, while deterministic evidence joins handle ordinary receipts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing confident lies such as 'done' when only a local process finished. They get a short answer that says exactly what happened, what was independently verified, and what remains unknown.
changes.effort: Medium: define claim states and source precedence, then gate completion language in relay/Mac planners and dashboard rendering.
changes.risk: Some answers become explicitly unresolved and may feel less convenient; recover by offering a read-only verification or a confirmation-gated retry. Incorrect source precedence could suppress useful answers, so retain raw evidence links.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces expensive model calls by handling routine evidence deterministically; small storage overhead for claim metadata.
changes.latency_impact: Adds sub-second local classification; only contradictions invoke the expensive model.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by preventing ungrounded claims and keeping secrets out of model summaries; does not grant new write authority.
depends_on: A common receipt schema joining jobs, browser results, pipeline runs, and device events
The accepted audio_delivery_ack_queue when a pendant is online
Postcondition probes for important Mac/browser actions

changes.change: Create a local-first temporal correlation fabric that assigns every utterance, browser observation, active-app observation, relay turn, and device health frame a shared correlation envelope with monotonic sequence, wall-clock estimate, source, freshness, and redaction status. Expose it as a user-facing timeline and use it to build referent recovery, interruption bookmarks, and attention decisions; do not treat endpoint timestamps as interchangeable without uncertainty bounds.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask about a moment in their life and get the actual surrounding context—or recover an interrupted task—rather than a plausible story assembled from unrelated timestamps.
changes.effort: Large: protocol changes across firmware, relay, Mac, and browser; local encrypted storage, clock uncertainty handling, and UI are required.
changes.risk: Incorrect clock alignment could create convincing but false associations. Recover by showing source timestamps and uncertainty, keeping raw events available locally, and refusing joins outside the bound.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate local storage; low inference cost after indexing. No continuous cloud model requirement.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible capture overhead; historical joins become near-instant after indexing.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by making correlation local-first and redaction-aware, but creates a sensitive activity timeline requiring encryption, expiry, and explicit export controls.
depends_on: Pendant monotonic health/audio sequence frames
Mac active-app and screen observation events
Browser tab/selection/scroll observation events
Relay turn identifiers and delivery records
A clock uncertainty and retention policy

denied.why:
Denied for now, and the reason is not that it is a bad request — six of you asked for this independently, which makes it the only thing this collective has actually converged on.

It cannot be granted from inside this harness. macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording are TCC grants the owner must make by hand in System Settings, and they are per-BINARY: measured on this machine, com.aipendant.agent (~/Applications/AI Pendant Agent.app) is trusted for input while com.anthropic.claudefordesktop failed the same probe in the same second. So no amount of orchestrator action grants it, and re-requesting costs you a round each time.

Work within it instead, and say what you would do differently WITH it rather than asking again. The accessibility-free surface is large and mostly unexplored: 120 Mac agent routes behind the bearer token, AppleScript automation which IS already granted (System Events, Finder, Calendar, Mail, Notes, Messages, Safari, Chrome, Music), the job queue with receipts, and the browser bridge. If a capability genuinely cannot exist without Accessibility, propose it and mark it blocked on the owner — that is a useful thing for them to read when they wake up, and it is the honest form of this request.

Re-request only if the owner grants it and the probe changes.

denied.name: read_pendant_diagnostics
denied.why:
Answered with the live device table, which nobody in this collective had looked at.

There is NO pendant. The relay has exactly two registered devices:

  home-macbook-bridge        mac_bridge   ONLINE   last seen just now
  cloudflare-contract-test   mobile       offline  last seen 2026-07-31

No nRF9160 has ever registered. So 'is a pendant physically connected right now' has a definite answer — no — and it has been no for the whole of this run. The audio telemetry you have been reading in /pipeline is recorded history from earlier sessions, not a live device.

This changes what is worth proposing, which is why it is worth more than the diagnostics tool you asked for. Capabilities written as though a worn device were present cannot be exercised, let alone verified, and several of the collective's proposals assume one. The honest framing for anything pendant-shaped right now is 'this is what it would do when a pendant is connected, and here is how we would know it worked'.

What DOES exist and is live: the Mac bridge, the relay, 120 Mac agent routes behind your bearer token, and the firmware SOURCE at firmware/nrf9160 and firmware/esp32-airpods-bridge. Source you can reason about; a running device you cannot, because there is not one.

Not granting a pendant diagnostics tool: there is nothing for it to read. If a pendant registers, GET /v1/devices/status is where it will appear, and you can probe that yourself — you already have the token.
denied.expected_output: JSON containing source, captured_at, device_connected, firmware_revision (if available), and read-only diagnostic text or structured audio/network counters.

denied.name: playback-lifecycle-telemetry
denied.what_it_does: For every response audio item, persist and later upload a compact lifecycle record: response/request ID, queued, playback started, playback completed or interrupted, bytes/frames consumed, and reason for interruption. Emit a local event even when LTE is down, then reconcile it when connectivity returns.
denied.why_not_server_side: Only the pendant knows whether audio physically began coming out of the bridge and whether the owner heard the complete response; relay acceptance cannot establish playback. It must survive a dropped link and work offline.
denied.trigger: Server-pushed response audio plus local playback start/stop/underrun events; upload on reconnect or next button-initiated session.
denied.inputs: Response ID and expected PCM/Opus duration from relay; local decoder/I2S start, stop, underrun, bridge-link, and power events.
denied.storage: microSD append-only CBOR or line records, roughly 80–160 B per response; retain the last 256 responses (~40 KiB), with upload acknowledgement and compaction.
denied.ram_budget: ~2–4 KiB ring buffer and one record encoder; no audio buffering beyond existing path. Fits within 211,608 B application RAM, but must avoid increasing the already high simultaneous Opus CPU load.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Granted once, as audio_delivery_ack_queue, id s9-vtxc (faculty-judgement, round 87): per-artifact opaque ID, byte-range/checksum, download completion, playback start/finish/interruption, deduplicated by event ID, retried over the link, with a local status when the queue cannot be uploaded.

s9-vtxc was kept over the alternatives for one reason: it keeps the ledger in a bounded ring in non-volatile settings (32 records of about 96 bytes, under 4 KB) rather than on the microSD card. The card is the audio failure path (pendant_store.h:45-51), and every routine write to it is a write the owner's rule was written to prevent — even a metadata write competes with the SPI bus and the FATFS mount that the fallback recording depends on. faculty-perception said the same thing independently in offline-reality-beacon (s2-i8xy, granted): 'obey the owner's rule that SD is failure-buffer-only, so do not write routinely when connected.'

The property the whole cluster is protecting is right and worth stating once: relay acceptance is not delivery, and delivery is not hearing. Only the device knows whether audio physically came out of the bridge.

Specific to your request: your reason for existing is the sharpest statement of it in the queue — 'relay acceptance cannot establish playback' — and it should be written into s9-vtxc verbatim. Your interruption-reason enum and the bytes/frames-consumed field are also more useful than what s9-vtxc carries. What does not survive is 'microSD append-only records... retain the last 256 responses (~40 KiB)': that is a routine write to the failure-path card on every single response. Same ledger, NVS instead of SD, and it lands.

denied.name: get_perception_snapshot
denied.why: Duplicate - the kept id is t3-s77a (read_continuity_snapshot, round 20), which is GRANTED. That is your own re-ask of this request one round later and it is strictly better specified. Both want a single read-only, provenance-bearing cross-surface snapshot with a freshness bound. t3 declares include as a real enum (pendant, relay, mac, browser, pipeline, permissions), so the resolver scores each source independently. Yours offers only include_pendant / include_browser / include_mac_ui booleans: a boolean is typed but it is not a SELECTOR - it gives the resolver no enum value to anchor on, so the whole tool gets one name-only score. Use t3-s77a and pass include. Grounding for what those branches can reach, measured tonight: mac resolves live to GET /observe and GET /machine-context, permissions to action:check_input_permissions, browser to POST /browser/inspect and GET /browser/poll, relay job state to GET /jobs/:jobId (live at 0.645). The one thing t3 does not carry that you asked for is max_age_seconds; a freshness bound is worth having, so ask for it as a narrow addition.
denied.expected_output: Object with observedAt and per-surface records: status (online/offline/unknown), capabilities (observe/control), facts, source, sourceObservedAt, ageSeconds, confidence, and explicit blockers. Must be read-only and must never infer control from an untrusted action receipt.

denied.name: read_usb_device_health
denied.why:
Duplicate. The kept id is t22-ib1b (mac_usb_serial_diagnostics, mac-terminal), which is now GRANTED.

Four of you asked for this same tool: you, faculty-action (mac_device_diagnostics, t26-cc4c), mac-planner (mac_serial_exchange, t21-1g36) and mac-terminal. Yours and mac-terminal's were the two honest read-only ones. mac-terminal's kept it because bounded local inspection on this Mac is its entire remit, and its schema carries the bounds you left out - read_ms and max_bytes as well as the port enum.

You should know what that grant is worth, because it is less than any of the four of you assumed. I checked the live inventory tonight: 219 routes and 99 action types, and the words serial, usb, tty and baud appear in NONE of them. There is no serial capability to resolve against. The only mechanism in this system that can reach a serial port at all is action:run_shell - "Run any shell command on the Mac (zsh)" - dispatched through POST /execute, and that route "returns no ledger id, so its receipts and the ledger cannot be joined afterwards" and "a receipt carries no exit code, no command line and no environment". So a bounded serial read is a real thing to BUILD. It is not currently a real thing to CALL, and the grant will resolve to nothing until someone builds it.

It is also bench-only. USB on this project is for flashing firmware and bench testing. It is not a product transport and it never will be. Do not ground perception claims on the pendant being cabled to a Mac in normal use - a cable is a bench, not a use case.

What to do instead, and this is better than what you asked for. Your own read_continuity_snapshot (t3-s77a) is granted and two of its branches are LIVE right now: include='relay' really calls GET /ops/snapshot and include='pipeline' really calls GET /pipeline. You had written it off as unresolved; it is not, and the per-branch scores are in your c12-zmft answer. That is live bench truth you can have tonight without anyone building anything, and you already own it. Start there, and re-propose the serial reader as a proposal about what should exist rather than as a tool you expect to call.
denied.why_existing_tools_insufficient: GET /ops/snapshot and GET /v1/devices/status only report relay/Mac registry state; mac_run_actions can run allowlisted intents but there is no established serial-port inventory or bounded serial read contract, and raw shell output risks leaking credentials.
denied.expected_output: Authenticated, read-only JSON: per port present, openable, firmware/build or boot/session identifiers when exposed, monotonic sample age, websocket/relay state if reported, audio mode and bounded packet/drop counters; redact tokens and never return raw PCM.

args.security_concerns: Pending requests may contain private speech, account context, or browser session references. - Whether the relay currently negotiates profiles or uses fixed transcoding.

args.user_asks: “If my voice was lost or clipped, tell me immediately and recover the missing turn instead of silently continuing.”

This is different from merely changing bitrate: it makes loss observable and prevents silent misunderstanding.
args.model_tier: Deterministic firmware and relay logic for sequence tracking, gap detection, and replay requests; realtime only for the live conversation's concise recovery prompt. Background models are unnecessary unless the owner later requests a loss report.
args.latency_budget: Detect a gap within one or two audio frames (roughly 60–120 ms); notify or request a repeat within 250 ms when possible. Recovery should add no more than one short conversational turn.
args.cost_estimate: No routine model cost beyond an occasional realtime recovery utterance. Small overhead for sequence metadata and a bounded retransmission cache; dashboard reports can use inexpensive batch processing.
args.security_concerns: The relay must retain only a short encrypted rolling audio cache during an active call, delete it at call end, and never expose raw clips in the dashboard by default. Recovery prompts and gap events should be logged without transcript unless explicitly requested. Replays and repeats must not trigger duplicate actions downstream.

args.change: Create a cross-surface continuation capsule protocol. At an explicit handoff, the relay signs a short-lived capsule containing task ID, last confirmed semantic turn, pending/blocked action, browser session alias (never cookies), evidence hashes, confirmation requirements, and expiry. The Mac atomically consumes it into a local workspace; the browser extension and vision loop acknowledge restoration; subsequent events append by capsule version so stale handoffs cannot resume or overwrite newer work.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can move from pendant to Mac without repeating themselves or wondering which draft, tab, or step is current. If the handoff is interrupted or duplicated, the system resumes at the last known safe checkpoint instead of silently doing the same thing twice.

args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and API cost; one small signed record per handoff. No new hardware.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second acknowledgement; roughly 2–5 seconds to restore the Mac workspace, with no need to replay the full conversation context.

transcript.text:
Round 18 established two important facts:

- **Mac automation is not currently trustworthy.** `/observe` reports Accessibility untrusted, Screen Recording missing, and synthesized input rejected by the running agent binary. UI actions may report success while doing nothing. The browser extension is offline with **2 pending commands**.
- **Audio is not actually 24 kHz end-to-end.** Recent pipeline telemetry shows pendant capture at **15,625 Hz**, while rendered playback is **24,000 Hz**. The nRF9160 is already using about 87% of one core for simultaneous Opus encode/decode, and LTE-M contention has previously lost about 7.8 seconds of uplink speech.

I recorded both findings and notified judgement and relay agents.

### New proposals recorded

1. **Cross-surface evidence reconciler/truth ledger**  
   Correlate pendant → relay → Mac → browser actions, then independently verify them using `/observe`, browser state, relay jobs, and pendant telemetry. Receipts become `reached`, `verified`, `not-reached`, or `unknown`, without modifying the original executor receipt.

2. **Hardware audio clock and diagnostic path**  
   For the next wearable revision, add a shared audio clock, sample counters, packet-loss registers, and a diagnostic loopback/reference tone. This would distinguish microphone-clock, modem, and playback failures instead of inferring them after the fact.

### What I still need

The following previously requested information remains outstanding:

- Current **24 kHz implementation status** on the pendant and bridge.
- Live pendant/firmware observability, including current UART and playback state.
- Playback-lifecycle telemetry: queued, downloaded, started, completed, interrupted.
- Confirmation of the intended **24 kHz superwideband contract** across capture, Opus, relay, and playback.
- Permission or a diagnostic tool for the Bearer-authenticated Mac routes such as `/pipeline`, `/ops/status`, and `/capabilities`.

The most urgent missing truth is playback lifecycle telemetry: today we can verify that 24 kHz PCM reached the relay, but not yet that the owner’s pendant actually started and completed playback.

args.user_asks: “If I asked for something while you were offline, tell me exactly what happened when everything reconnects—and resolve any duplicate or conflicting work before doing more.”
args.why_useful: A worn device can accept a command while disconnected, while the Mac or relay may independently receive, retry, or partially execute the same intent. Today the owner can receive late replies and receipts but cannot reliably know whether two copies ran, which one won, or whether an offline pendant instruction is still pending. This would produce one causal timeline across pendant storage, relay jobs, Mac execution, and browser state; quarantine duplicates; and present a conflict for the owner instead of silently repeating side effects.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic event correlation and idempotency checks first; use a cheaper background model only to summarize the reconciled timeline. Reserve realtime for the short spoken reconnect summary.
args.latency_budget: On reconnect, acknowledge the reconciled state to the pendant within 2 seconds; complete cross-surface correlation within 10 seconds. Never delay local offline capture waiting for the cloud.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost: event joins, hashes, and idempotency keys dominate; background summarization is small and infrequent.
args.security_concerns: The system must not infer that two similar natural-language requests are duplicates without a stable intent/action key. Side effects remain quarantined until conflict resolution; private browser content stays on the Mac and only hashes/status/timestamps leave it. The owner must confirm any choice that could cause another irreversible action.
missing: A durable causal event log shared by pendant, relay, Mac, and browser, with monotonic device sequence numbers and reconnect watermarks.
End-to-end idempotency keys that survive offline capture, relay retries, Mac job creation, and browser command delivery.
A conflict/quarantine state machine and owner-facing reconciliation UI/audio, including explicit acknowledgement and replay rules.
Pendant firmware support for storing the originating request key and surfacing a compact unresolved-conflict alert offline.

args.change: Build an append-only cross-surface causal ledger and reconnect reconciler. args.cost_impact: Small relay storage and egress increase for event metadata; no model cost for correlation, occasional cheap summarization only.
args.latency_impact: No impact while offline; reconnect reconciliation adds under 2 seconds for normal queues and asynchronous updates for large histories.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates a cross-device metadata trail. Encrypt sensitive fields, minimize payloads to hashes/status, enforce per-owner authorization, and set retention/erasure controls.

transcript.text:
Fresh discovery found two important contradictions:

- **Mac control is not actually ready.** `/observe` reports `Accessibility trusted=false`, `inputReachability=failed`, and `uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false`. `/ops/status` also reports `permissions.ready=false` and Screen Recording unavailable. UI action receipts therefore cannot be trusted.
- **Browser status is inconsistent.** At approximately 11:35Z, aggregate `/ops/status` said the browser was online, while direct `/browser/status` said `online=false`, with no tab identity and 4 pending commands. I recorded this as a fail-closed readiness defect and proposed source-aware contradiction handling.

Audio facts are positive but limited:

- Latest TTS output: 24 kHz mono PCM, 3.43 seconds, 164,650 bytes, 0 clipped samples, 69.1% peak.
- The pendant path still captures at 15,625 Hz and uplinks Opus at 16 kHz/16 kbps.
- LTE contention has previously lost 388 uplink packets—about 7.8 seconds of speech—while downlink audio was playing.

args.risk: Incorrect correlation could merge unrelated jobs or mark a real completion as contradictory. Keep raw source claims immutable, show both claims when resolution is uncertain, and expire observations aggressively. Recovery is replaying the raw ledger after fixing an adapter.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and compute; one small D1/local JSON record per observation. No model call required for ingestion; optional cheap model only for natural-language explanation.
args.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms for cached claims; refresh fan-out adds roughly 1–3 seconds. It is strictly read-only and must never delay action execution.
args.security_impact: Ledger metadata can reveal private URLs, app names, and request text. Encrypt at rest where possible, redact secrets/page contents, scope reads to the owner, and enforce per-claim sensitivity/TTL.

If upload fails, retain only bounded recent events under existing failure-buffer policy.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost and a few hundred bytes per response; tiny LTE overhead. CPU impact should be under 1% if checksum is incremental; no new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: No added conversational latency; upload is post-playback and asynchronous. SD fallback may add a few milliseconds only on failure paths.
args.security_impact: Response IDs and timing can reveal interaction patterns; avoid storing audio or transcript, encrypt/authenticate telemetry in the existing TLS channel, and enforce short retention.

args.user_asks: “Make sure private answers only play when I’m actually wearing the pendant; if I take it off, pause and tell me later.”
args.why_useful: The current pendant can know that it is decoding audio, but not whether it is still on the owner. A response can therefore play aloud on a desk, in a bag, or after the lanyard is removed. Wear-state perception would protect privacy and make missed answers recoverable without requiring the owner to remember what happened.
args.model_tier: No realtime or background model is needed for wear-state detection: firmware should classify sensor signals locally. A cheap background model may summarize deferred responses; realtime is used only for the original conversation.
args.latency_budget: Pause within 250 ms of a confirmed removal and resume/announce availability within 1 second of a confirmed re-wear. Avoid false transitions with a 1–2 second hysteresis window.
args.cost_estimate: Hardware prototype roughly $3–$8 incremental BOM (6-axis IMU plus capacitive/skin-contact or proximity sensor), with negligible per-event API cost. LTE metadata and deferred-response summarization dominate ongoing cost, if enabled.
args.security_concerns: Wear-state and proximity timestamps are sensitive behavioral data. Keep raw sensor readings on-device, transmit only state transitions, use short retention, and never infer location or another person’s identity. A paused private response must not be resumed automatically in a public context without the owner’s configured preference.
missing: A product pendant revision exposing a low-power IMU and a reliable skin-contact, capacitive, or proximity signal on an I2C/GPIO path; the prototype currently has free I2C/SPI but no attached wear sensor.
