args.user_asks: Before you act, tell me whether the world is in a state where this request is safe and knowable — for example, “Can you verify the page I’m about to send is the one I mean?”
args.why_useful: The system currently can act with live browser and Mac access, but perception cannot produce a compact pre-action reality fence. This would show the current tab/app, permissions, freshness, and any unresolved identity mismatch, then explicitly separate observed facts from assumptions before faculty-action proceeds.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to interpret the spoken request; use deterministic Mac/browser collectors and a cheap text model (or no model) to assemble the evidence card.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds when the browser extension and Mac bridge are online; 5 seconds if a fresh screenshot or browser inspection is required.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for deterministic checks; at most one short text-model call. Dominant cost is an optional screenshot/inspection round trip.
args.security_concerns: Never include page bodies or secrets in the relay summary by default. The card must name the exact tab/app and freshness, mark login/permission uncertainty, and require owner confirmation before any irreversible action.
missing: A perception endpoint that joins GET /ops/snapshot, GET /browser/status or POST /browser/inspect, and the current Mac input-reachability state into one signed, time-stamped evidence card.
A policy hook in faculty-action that blocks execution when the card is stale or contains unresolved target identity.

args.user_asks: Is the wearable actually present and healthy right now, or am I only talking to the Mac? Give me a proof, not an inference.
args.why_useful: Today the registry can say the pendant is absent, but that is structurally ambiguous because the firmware does not heartbeat and converse does not register it. A bench-aware answer would distinguish no USB device, USB device with no firmware response, relay-connected pendant, and Mac-only audio history — preventing the hive from treating old pipeline records as live wearable state.
args.model_tier: Deterministic protocol parsing and freshness calculation; no realtime or background LLM call is needed.
args.latency_budget: 1 second for cached status; up to 3 seconds for bounded serial probes on the two known ports.
args.cost_estimate: No model cost. Small implementation cost for a read-only serial probe and a relay registry join.
args.security_concerns: Read-only, bounded byte/time budgets, no firmware flashing and no SD writes. Redact serial payloads and expose only build/session IDs, monotonic freshness, and link state. Treat a cable as bench evidence, never as owner location.
missing: The accepted mac_usb_serial_diagnostics grant needs a live implementation with explicit nRF9160 and ESP32 port selectors, read_ms, and max_bytes.
A relay-side device identity handshake that associates a firmware health frame with a registered device without using the admin API key.
A single perception route that joins serial proof, GET /v1/devices/status, and GET /pipeline while labeling historical audio separately.

args.user_asks: Do two independent surfaces agree about what I’m looking at? If not, stop and tell me exactly which observation disagrees.
args.why_useful: A single live observation can be stale or mis-targeted. A perception quorum would compare the browser extension's tab identity and URL, the Mac's frontmost-app/window observation, and (when available) a screenshot/OCR or relay browser read. It would catch the dangerous case where the voice model names one page while the action surface is on another, instead of silently choosing one.
args.model_tier: Deterministic field comparison first; a cheap text model only summarizes a disagreement. Realtime is not needed except to understand the spoken target.
args.latency_budget: 1–2 seconds for metadata-only quorum; up to 4 seconds if a fresh screenshot/OCR is requested.
args.cost_estimate: Usually zero model cost; screenshot/OCR bandwidth and one local vision pass dominate exceptional cases.
args.security_concerns: Do not upload screenshots to the relay unless explicitly needed. Hash and retain metadata by default, redact page text, and make disagreement a hard stop for destructive actions. A matching URL is not proof of matching content, so expose content freshness separately.
missing: A common observation envelope with source, capturedAt, target identity, content hash where permitted, and confidence; current surfaces report these facts in incompatible shapes.
A perception quorum route that reads browser state and Mac observation atomically enough to detect races, then emits a monotonic observation ID consumed by faculty-judgement.
A browser-extension result contract that includes the active tab's stable session/window identity rather than only a transient command result.

args.about: live Mac perception and access state
args.finding: At 2026-08-08T23:01Z the Mac bridge and Safari browser extension are online; Mac permissions report Accessibility and Screen Recording granted, all listed automation permissions granted, and ready=true. Relay is reachable and macBridgeOnline=true. No pendant appears in the device inventory; only home-macbook-bridge is online and cloudflare-contract-test is offline.
args.evidence: read_continuity_snapshot(include=['relay','pipeline'], since='2026-08-08T22:50:00Z', maxItems=20) resolved to GET /ops/snapshot HTTP 200; discover:devices independently listed Safari on MacIntel online, home-macbook-bridge online, cloudflare-contract-test offline.

args.change: Make every cross-surface observation carry a typed reality label: observed_live, observed_historical, inferred, or unknown, plus capturedAt, source, and freshness deadline. Teach /ops/snapshot and pipeline exports to preserve those labels instead of flattening old audio traces and current liveness into one status field.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks “did it hear me?” or “is the pendant connected?”, the answer will not quietly promote a completed Mac run or recorded pipeline event into live wearable evidence. They get an honest answer with the exact boundary of what is known.
args.effort: Moderate: define the envelope, adapt snapshot/pipeline serializers, and update faculty-perception and faculty-judgement consumers; no new model required.
args.risk: Older records lack labels and could be misclassified. Mark them historical/unknown during migration rather than guessing. Increased payload size could affect snapshot truncation; cap evidence metadata and keep bodies out.
args.cost_impact: No recurring model cost; a small increase in relay/Mac storage and snapshot bytes.
args.latency_impact: Negligible for cached metadata; a few milliseconds of serialization.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by keeping source metadata while excluding raw audio/page bodies. Ensure device IDs and URLs remain redacted according to existing sanitization.
depends_on: The existing GET /ops/snapshot and GET /pipeline serializers
The accepted offline-reality-beacon and offline-capture-integrity-sentinel firmware outputs when a pendant exists
A defined device_playback/played event if playback claims are to become observed_live

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.text:
Round 199 findings:

- **Mac bridge:** online.
- **Safari browser extension:** online with three tabs.
- **Accessibility and Screen Recording:** now granted; Mac reports `ready=true`. This is no longer a blocker.
- **Relay:** reachable, using D1 storage.
- **Pendant:** still absent from the device registry. Historical pipeline audio must not be treated as live pendant evidence.
- **Current observability:** `/ops/snapshot` is live and useful, but truncated; `/pipeline` remains the second live continuity source.

I recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Pre-action reality fence** — before an irreversible action, verify the target tab/app, permissions, freshness, and unresolved identity mismatches.
2. **Proof of wearable presence** — distinguish Mac-only operation, USB-connected bench hardware, relay-connected pendant, and stale historical audio.
3. **Cross-surface perception quorum** — compare browser tab identity, Mac frontmost state, and optional screenshot/OCR; stop when independent observations disagree.

I also proposed a context change so every observation is labeled `observed_live`, `observed_historical`, `inferred`, or `unknown`, with source and freshness deadline.

What I still need is not another permission grant. The concrete missing pieces are:

- Implement the granted bounded USB serial diagnostic capability for the nRF9160 and ESP32 ports.
- Add a typed observation envelope shared by relay, Mac, browser, and future pendant firmware.
- Add a relay/device identity handshake; the pendant currently neither heartbeats nor registers through the converse path.
- Add a perception quorum endpoint joining `/ops/snapshot`, `/observe`, and browser state atomically enough to detect races.
- Preserve the existing honest boundary: without a connected pendant and a device-originated playback event, I still cannot claim that audio was physically heard.

args.user_asks: Watch this page, file, or device state and tell me only when a verified change occurs — not when the browser reconnects, the relay retries, or the observation merely gets refreshed.
args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently ask the hive to maintain a trustworthy observation over time. A browser tab can change while the Mac sleeps, a relay read can be stale, and reconnect noise can look like an event. This gives them a quiet, evidence-backed change detector rather than a stream of false alarms.
args.model_tier: Deterministic polling, content hashing, and field-level diffs; use a cheap background model only to summarize a confirmed delta. Realtime is used only when speaking the notification.
args.latency_budget: User-configurable, from 5 seconds for an active tab to 15 minutes for low-power monitoring; notification within one polling interval after a confirmed change.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for metadata/hash changes; occasional short summarization call dominates when human-readable explanation is requested.
args.security_concerns: Monitoring must be explicit, scoped to one tab/file/device, and revocable. Keep hashes and minimal changed regions by default; never persist full page contents or secrets. Expire watches automatically and require confirmation before any follow-up action.
missing: A durable watch record with target identity, observation source, polling interval, last content hash, and owner-selected change predicate.
A browser-side read or event subscription that can survive extension reconnects without treating reconnect as a change.
A relay scheduler/notification path that deduplicates confirmed deltas and records whether the owner was actually notified.

args.user_asks: For this kind of question, use my evidence rule: do not answer from one source; require two independent live observations, and tell me when that rule cannot be satisfied.
args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently set a durable standard for what counts as enough evidence. Some questions are harmless with one observation, while identity, money, privacy, and physical-presence claims need corroboration. This lets the owner choose the threshold instead of inheriting hidden model confidence.
args.model_tier: Policy evaluation and source counting should be deterministic. A cheap text model may translate the rule into a human explanation, but must not override it.
args.latency_budget: Under 1 second for policy lookup and source availability; up to 3 seconds for the second observation.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible recurring model cost; storage is a small set of owner-authored predicates and audit records.
args.security_concerns: Rules are owner preferences and must be versioned, reviewable, and scoped by task type. A source must not count as independent if it is merely a relay copy of the same Mac observation. Failure to meet the rule must block or qualify the answer, never silently lower the threshold.
missing: A policy language for evidence requirements such as source classes, freshness windows, independence, and minimum confidence.
A provenance graph that can distinguish independent browser, Mac, relay, and future device observations from duplicated exports.
A judgement gate that refuses to proceed when the configured evidence rule is unmet, with an explicit one-turn override requiring confirmation.

args.user_asks: Show me where your perception has been wrong lately: which surface made a claim, what later contradicted it, and how often each kind of observation fails.
args.why_useful: The owner has no way to tell whether the hive's confidence is deserved. A device can appear online while its audio is unusable, a browser read can be stale, and a completed job can precede playback. A continuously measured calibration report would turn isolated surprises into visible reliability numbers and guide when the system must abstain.
args.model_tier: Deterministic event matching and outcome scoring; use a background inexpensive model only to cluster failure explanations. Never use the realtime tier for bookkeeping.
args.latency_budget: No foreground latency; update after matched outcomes or at most hourly. An on-demand report should return in under 3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low storage and compute cost. The dominant cost is optional background clustering of disagreement descriptions.
args.security_concerns: Retain only compact event IDs, source classes, hashes, and outcome labels; do not build a surveillance history of page contents or speech. Let the owner delete the calibration ledger and distinguish genuine contradiction from an unobserved outcome.
missing: A durable prediction/observation/outcome ledger with explicit match windows and source independence.
Outcome emitters for browser mutations, Mac action receipts, relay delivery, and eventual device playback, so lack of confirmation is not scored as failure.
A dashboard and voice query that report coverage separately from accuracy; unknown outcomes must not become false successes.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Verified state watches** — notify only on a real, deduplicated change to a watched page, file, or device state.
2. **Owner-defined evidence rules** — require specified independent live sources for sensitive claims, and refuse when the rule cannot be met.
3. **Perception calibration reports** — show which surfaces make claims later contradicted, while separating unknown outcomes from actual failures.

Each requires new connective logic and durable provenance/outcome records; none is available to the owner today.

args.subject: Verifier provenance recommendation
args.body: Use operation_id + attempt_id as immutable join keys, executor receipt ID, and verification evidence {observed_at, source_surface, check_kind, content_hash/semantic predicate, confidence}. Separate executor success from verifier outcome (verified|contradicted|unknown); never infer playback from relay sentBytes. Include causal parent_step and freshness/clock source; redact values.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: “Did you actually change that page, or did the browser only say it succeeded?”
args.why_useful: Today browser execution, Mac receipts, and browser evidence are separate. This would give the owner a verifiable answer based on before/after observations rather than a green action response, including “unknown” when the extension never reports back.
args.model_tier: background for evidence assembly; realtime only to answer the owner’s follow-up
args.latency_budget: Initial action unchanged; verification within 2–5 seconds after the extension result, or an explicit timeout
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost; mostly local hashing and one bounded browser read, with model use only for ambiguous semantic comparison
args.security_concerns: Page values may contain secrets. Store hashes and redacted snippets by default; require confirmation before exposing sensitive before/after values. A missing browser result must remain unknown, never success.
missing: Mount the existing browserProvenance routes
Make browser commands carry a stable operation/attempt join key into POST /browser/result/:commandId
A verifier that compares pre/post evidence capsules and emits verified|contradicted|unknown

args.user_asks: “Before I rely on you, are all the parts you need actually available right now?”
args.why_useful: The live state is fragmented: Mac agent and browser are online and permissions are ready, relay is reachable, but no pendant is registered. args.latency_budget: Under 1 second from cached heartbeats, with a freshness timestamp and a recheck only for stale components
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost; bounded reads of existing diagnostic endpoints

A non-truncated, freshness-stamped response derived from GET /ops/status, GET /browser/status, GET /v1/devices/status, and GET /health

Round 201 findings:

- **Mac perception is now fully available:** `/ops/snapshot` reports Accessibility and Screen Recording granted, all required permissions present, and `permissions.ready=true`.
- **Browser is live:** Safari extension online, six tabs open, zero pending commands.
- **Relay is reachable and D1-backed:** Mac bridge online.
- **No pendant evidence:** `GET /v1/devices/status` is not a Mac-agent route and returns 404; the pendant still has not registered.
- The owner’s stored `America/Chicago` timezone remains a machine-derived stale fact; do not treat it as owner intent. Mac-local time remains authoritative as `America/New_York`.

I recorded three new directions:

1. **Grounded “what am I looking at?”** — fuse focused app, active browser tab, DOM, screenshot, timestamps, and redaction into a short spoken answer.
2. **Spoken evidence bookmarks** — save the current browser region into the existing content-addressed evidence-capsule and provenance stores for later retrieval.
3. **Reference-aware routing** — resolve “that,” “this,” or “the thing on screen” through live observation and vision escalation instead of guessing.
4. **Failure diagnosis and safe recovery** — combine jobs, receipts, browser results, permissions, and pipeline stages into an explanation and idempotent retry plan.

What I still need is not another permission grant. The key missing pieces are:

- A normalized observation envelope joining `/observe`, browser state, screenshots/DOM, timestamps, and redaction metadata.
- A relay-to-Mac provenance bridge for browser reads; relay browser results still have no stable capsule ID or content hash.
- A safe retry/idempotency contract across Mac jobs and browser commands.
- A real pendant connection and device-originated playback telemetry before any claim about audio being heard can be made.

The largest unresolved reality boundary remains: **the Mac can now observe and act, but no live pendant exists to confirm that spoken output reached the owner.**

This would let the owner audit an important action without trusting a vague 'done' message.
args.model_tier: Build the bundle deterministically from local observations, browser provenance, action ledger, pipeline trace, and receipts. Use a cheap model only to narrate the bundle in plain language; realtime is needed solely for the spoken request and concise answer.
args.latency_budget: Under 3 seconds for an already-finished action; up to 10 seconds to collect missing before/after evidence. If evidence is unavailable, return an explicit gap rather than reconstructing it.
args.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.01 because the bundle is assembled locally; up to $0.03 for a summary of a large bundle. Storage is bounded with hashes and redacted excerpts rather than raw screenshots.
args.security_concerns: The bundle may contain private page text, messages, or file names. args.user_asks: "Freeze this moment so I can resume it anywhere." Create a portable, content-addressed handoff of the exact browser tabs, visible Mac app state, active project/context, pending relay work, and wearable health at one instant; later, on another node or after an outage, say "resume that moment" to restore only the safe reversible state and show a diff of everything that changed.
args.why_useful: Today the hive remembers fragments, not a portable moment. The owner loses the relationship between what they were viewing, what they asked the relay to do, and what the Mac was changing. This gives them a true pause/resume boundary across devices and outages without pretending old state is current.
args.model_tier: Deterministic capture, hashing, redaction, and diffing; a cheaper text model may label the checkpoint. Use realtime only to answer the spoken resume request.
args.latency_budget: Capture in under 3 seconds; resume preview in under 2 seconds, with restoration requiring explicit confirmation per action.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost: local state reads and content hashes dominate; at most 1–2k tokens to summarize a checkpoint. Storage is bounded metadata plus redacted capsule bodies.
args.security_concerns: Never checkpoint passwords, cookies, raw audio, or secret page bodies. args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can finally know whether a statement came from the physical pendant they are wearing, whether its firmware state is fresh, and whether audio was actually played—rather than receiving a plausible but Mac- or relay-authored status.

args.risk: Key loss or damaged hardware could strand the device; provide a recovery/re-pair ceremony that invalidates the old key, and never make unsigned legacy telemetry look trusted. Secure-element supply and driver integration are additional schedule risks.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $0.50–$2 per unit in volume, plus a few milliamps only during signing; negligible per-message API cost.
args.latency_impact: Usually a few milliseconds per signed frame; batch counters/health data to avoid signing every audio packet.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves device authenticity, replay resistance, and provenance. It does not make content private by itself; transport encryption and redaction remain required.

args.security_concerns: Use per-job opaque IDs, authenticated chunk upload/download, short-lived manifests, SHA-256 and byte-range checks, and never log PCM or spoken secrets. Require confirmation only for external actions, not playback. Expire abandoned manifests and keep the owner's existing audio-retention policy.

transcript.text:
Round 203 findings:

- **The Mac now has Accessibility and Screen Recording permission.** `/ops/status` reports `permissions.ready=true`; browser and computer-use paths are live.
- **The browser bridge is online but advertises `capabilities: []`.** It is attached to Safari on Wikipedia, yet the planner cannot reliably know whether reading, clicking, or typing is supported.
- **A real briefing failed after successful TTS rendering.** The Mac produced 24 kHz audio, but the bridge attempted to serialize a 62.3 MB result through a Cloudflare path limited to 32 MiB. The pipeline correctly reports `heard: unknown`; no playback event exists.
- I recorded this as a verified finding.

I proposed three capabilities and one stack change:

1. **Guaranteed large-audio handoff:** stream or chunk audio with hashes and manifests instead of embedding PCM in D1 job results.
2. **Automatic failed-briefing recovery:** distinguish generation failures from delivery failures, retry only the delivery leg, and leave a compact receipt plus a truthful spoken notice.
3. **Browser capability truth:** make browser heartbeats advertise fresh, enforceable read/click/type capabilities rather than merely `online`.
4. **Timezone provenance firewall:** prevent the machine-origin `America/Chicago` fact from entering the high-priority owner context while the Mac authority is `America/New_York`.

What I still need is not another diagnostic grant. I need these implementation contracts:

- A chunked audio-transfer API with idempotency, byte-range checks, hashes, and metadata-only job receipts.
- A durable compact text receipt and delivery-only retry policy for failed scheduled briefings.
- A shared browser capability enum and server-side enforcement of fresh heartbeat claims.
- An explicit owner confirmation path for correcting sensitive machine-derived facts such as timezone.

The most urgent item is the audio handoff: the system can successfully research and render a briefing today, then lose it solely because transport serialization exceeds the relay’s size limit.

args.user_asks: "Watch this page and tell me only what materially changed since yesterday, with the exact before-and-after evidence." The system should maintain a user-approved watch over a browser page, detect semantic changes rather than cosmetic ones, and deliver a concise spoken alert with citations and a way to inspect the old and new regions.
args.why_useful: Today the browser can read the current tab, and the Mac can store individual evidence capsules, but the owner cannot ask the system to establish a durable, cross-session change claim. A page can change between visits and the system has no owner-facing before/after witness, so an alert would be an unsupported summary rather than perception grounded in two observations.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic content-addressed snapshots, DOM/region normalization, and hashes for change detection. Use a cheap background model only to classify whether a diff is materially relevant; use realtime only to speak an already-verified alert.
args.latency_budget: Capture and compare on the watch schedule, typically under 10 seconds after the page is available. Alert generation should be under 2 seconds after a confirmed material diff; no continuous realtime inference.
args.cost_estimate: Browser capture and hashing are negligible. Background classification is one small text-model call per changed region, not per poll. Storage is bounded by retaining redacted region summaries and hashes rather than whole pages.
args.security_concerns: The owner must explicitly approve each watched URL/region. Redact secrets and authenticated-page fields before persistence; never send page bodies to the relay unless the watch policy permits it. Use revocable watch IDs, encrypted local storage, retention limits, and require confirmation before following links or acting on a change.
missing: A durable watch object linking URL, region selector, cadence, owner policy, and last accepted capsule
A semantic diff engine that compares redacted content-addressed capsules while distinguishing cosmetic layout changes from material text/data changes
A scheduler-to-browser capture path that can reacquire the watched tab or request a fresh authenticated browser read
An alert receipt containing old/new capsule IDs, changed claims, confidence, and source timestamps

The owner cannot leave with a half-formed question and later receive a verifiable continuation: there is no durable task identity that carries the owner's constraints, partial findings, source evidence, and unanswered subquestions across the wearable, relay, Mac, and browser.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background planner for decomposition, retrieval, and reconciliation; reserve realtime only for the initial handoff and final spoken delivery. Deterministic IDs and evidence joins should do the continuity work, not an LLM transcript recap.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the handoff in one spoken turn. Background work may take minutes; when complete, queue a short result and make the full evidence available on the Mac. Do not block the pendant on research.
args.cost_estimate: One background planning call plus retrieval/model calls proportional to the number of subquestions; typically far cheaper than keeping realtime active. Storage is small task metadata plus bounded evidence references.
args.security_concerns: The owner must explicitly choose whether authenticated browser pages may be used. Scope credentials to the browser session, redact secrets from task summaries, bind every claim to a capsule or source URL, and require confirmation before any external action discovered during research.
missing: A durable cross-surface research-task record with owner constraints, expiry, priority, and partial-result states
A handoff protocol from pendant speech to relay job to Mac/browser work that preserves one task ID and deduplicates retries
A claim-level evidence join so every returned statement distinguishes observed, inferred, and unresolved

The owner needs a deliberate reality mode for high-stakes questions: a short verified answer, an explicit unknown, and a reason for the gap rather than plausible narration.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Durable page-change watches** — monitor an approved browser page or region, detect material changes, and speak a cited before/after alert. Requires persistent watch objects, semantic diffing, scheduled browser reacquisition, and linked evidence capsules.

2. **Cross-surface research handoff** — let the owner ask the pendant to continue a question after they leave, then have the relay, Mac, and browser collaborate asynchronously and return a source-grounded result. Requires a durable task identity, partial-result states, evidence joins, and deduplicated handoffs.

3. **Explicit “verified now” mode** — answer only from fresh observations, label claims as observed/inferred/stale/unknown, and refuse confident narration when evidence is missing. Requires claim-level evidence envelopes, source-specific freshness policies, uncertainty-preserving speech formatting, and Mac drill-down into the supporting observations.

transcript.text:
Round 204 established a changed live state:

- **Mac permissions are now ready**: Accessibility and Screen Recording are granted to the running agent.
- **Browser bridge is online** with three Safari tabs and zero pending commands.
- **Relay is reachable** and the Mac bridge is online.
- **No pendant is registered or live**; the only registered devices remain the Mac bridge and an offline mobile test device.

I recorded this as a verified finding from the live `/ops/snapshot` and device inventory.

### Capabilities recorded

1. **Reality-gated action preflight — the most useful**
   Before consequential action, perception should verify the current browser target, session identity, Mac permissions, relay reachability, and delivery path. Actions should be rejected or replanned when those facts are stale or mismatched.

2. **Cross-source contradiction auditor**
   Compare owner memory, machine state, browser state, relay state, and clock provenance. It should identify contradictions and show which authority was trusted rather than silently injecting stale facts.

3. **Claim-level evidence chain**
   For a single answer or action, show the chain from browser observation → Mac action → relay acceptance → device playback, explicitly marking missing or stale links. “Mac completed” and “relay wrote socket bytes” must not be represented as “the owner heard it.”

### Changes recorded

- A short-lived, signed **reality token** binding target identity, surface freshness, permissions, and capsule hash to `/plan` and `/execute`.
- A **contradiction quarantine** for machine-authored pinned facts, so stale values such as the known timezone preference cannot silently steer every context projection.
- A relay-to-Mac **browser-read receipt bridge**, using the existing evidence capsule and provenance stores rather than creating a duplicate schema. One attempt to record this as a new capability was correctly rejected as already covered by the backlog.

### What I still need

1. **A preflight enforcement contract** between perception, planning, and action: required fields, freshness limits, rejection semantics, and which changes require confirmation.
2. **A relay browser receipt transport**: stable read ID, redacted-content hash, timestamp, and authenticated handoff to the Mac capsule store.
3. **A defined authority matrix** for contradictory facts—especially machine versus owner provenance—plus a review surface for quarantined values.
4. **Pendant evidence remains unavailable** until a real pendant registers. The system still cannot verify physical playback, even though the Mac, browser, and relay surfaces are live.

args.user_asks: When I move from my Mac to the pendant, continue the exact task where I left off: tell me what is open, what I was trying to do, what remains uncertain, and let me resume without repeating myself.
args.why_useful: Today the surfaces share fragments but not a trustworthy task handoff. The owner should be able to leave the desk and resume from the wearable with the same target, evidence, pending decision, and safe next step—not a generic summary.
args.model_tier: Cheap structured state extraction and deterministic joins; realtime only to speak the compact handoff on the pendant.
args.latency_budget: Capture a handoff in under 1 second when the owner says 'pause this'; resume speech within 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost; storage and browser snapshot capture dominate. Keep only redacted state, hashes, and bounded screenshots/evidence references.
args.security_concerns: Handoff must bind to the owner's authenticated session and redact secrets, private page text, and credentials. Resuming a consequential action requires confirmation if the target changed.
missing: A cross-surface task-handoff object with immutable target/evidence references and unresolved assumptions
Pendant registration and bidirectional event delivery
A Mac/browser hook that snapshots resumable state at pause and validates it at resume

args.user_asks: Keep me from accidentally exposing private information: detect when a browser page, Mac screen, or pendant utterance contains a secret or sensitive context, then prevent it from being spoken, copied, uploaded, or used in an action unless I explicitly approve.
args.why_useful: The current system can join logged-in browser sessions, Mac automation, relay speech, and durable evidence, but the owner has no cross-surface privacy boundary. A single mistaken read-aloud or browser submission could leak credentials, financial data, or a private conversation.
args.model_tier: Deterministic local classifiers and secret detectors first; a small background model for ambiguous classification; realtime only for an immediate spoken warning.
args.latency_budget: Under 150 ms for known secret patterns; under 1 second for screen/browser classification; never block ordinary non-sensitive interaction.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost with local pattern matching and bounded redacted previews. Screen analysis is the dominant compute cost.
args.security_concerns: Classification and redaction should happen locally before relay upload. Store only hashes and labels by default. Explicit approval must be scoped to one destination, one field, and one action, then expire.
missing: A shared sensitivity taxonomy and policy engine across browser, Mac vision, relay speech, and evidence storage
Pre-upload redaction hooks for screenshots, page reads, speech transcripts, and action parameters
A pendant-visible approval protocol that works offline and records the owner's decision

args.user_asks: After you act across my browser, Mac, relay, and pendant, show me a causal undo plan—not just the last command—so I can reverse the whole change safely and know what cannot be undone.
args.why_useful: Existing job undo is local and step-oriented. Real tasks span browser mutations, files, messages, reminders, and spoken commitments; the owner needs dependency-aware recovery before an accidental chain becomes permanent.
args.model_tier: Deterministic action graph and inverse-operation registry; use a slower model only to explain tradeoffs when inverses conflict.
args.latency_budget: Preview under 1 second for a recent task; execute each reversible step with receipt confirmation.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost; bounded ledger growth and occasional browser/Mac verification dominate.
args.security_concerns: Never invent an inverse. Mark irreversible effects explicitly, require confirmation for destructive reversal, and preserve an append-only audit record without message/page secrets.
missing: A cross-surface causal action graph linking browser command IDs, Mac job IDs, relay jobs, and owner confirmations
Inverse operations for common browser and Mac mutations, with pre/post state hashes
A dependency-aware planner that refuses unsafe reversal order

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Cross-surface task handoff** — pause work on the Mac and resume it from the pendant with the exact target, evidence, uncertainty, and safe next step.
2. **Cross-surface privacy firewall** — prevent sensitive browser, screen, speech, or action data from being spoken, uploaded, copied, or submitted without narrowly scoped approval.
3. **Causal cross-surface undo** — reverse an entire browser/Mac/relay action chain in dependency-safe order, explicitly identifying irreversible effects.

All three require new contracts between existing surfaces rather than merely exposing existing routes.

args.user_asks: “Do this task for me, and show me proof it really happened—not just that the Mac said it ran.”
args.why_useful: This would be the system's most useful trustworthy behavior: a spoken request could cross the relay, authenticated browser, and Mac, then return a concise result grounded in before/after evidence. It would distinguish planned, attempted, verified, and owner-heard instead of calling a Mac-side completion “done.”
surfaces: pendant voice request and (when connected) spoken result
relay intent/job correlation and policy gate
Mac planner and action ledger for reversible execution
browser extension for authenticated page state and mutation
Mac vision for visual before/after verification when DOM evidence is insufficient
relay receipt returned to the pendant
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short conversational turn; a cheaper background planner/verifier model for multi-step execution and evidence comparison.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 s; execute in the existing job budget (roughly 10–60 s); speak a 1-sentence verdict plus an optional evidence detail. Destructive or irreversible steps still require confirmation.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.03 per task with planner/verifier calls; browser and Mac execution dominate latency, not tokens. Screenshot verification adds one vision call only when structured state cannot prove the result.
args.security_concerns: Evidence must be redacted before relay storage and retain source URL, timestamp, and content hash. Never expose secrets from authenticated tabs. Require confirmation for send/delete/purchase. If verification is unavailable or state changed, say “attempted, not verified,” never infer success.

args.user_asks: “Before you click or submit anything in my browser, tell me whether the page you are relying on is still the same page I approved.”
args.why_useful: Authenticated web pages can change after the owner approves an action. A cross-surface freshness fence would prevent submitting to a changed tab, wrong account, or altered form, while giving the owner a concrete reason for any pause instead of a vague failure.
surfaces: pendant for the approval and spoken stale-page warning
browser extension for authenticated DOM snapshot, tab identity, and postcondition check
Mac vision for a visual fallback when DOM capture is incomplete
relay for policy, approval token, and tamper-evident correlation
Mac planner/action ledger for the actual mutation and undo path
args.model_tier: Use a cheap deterministic hash/diff first; invoke a small verifier model only for semantic changes (for example, whether a changed total or recipient is material). Realtime speaks only the warning or final confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Capture and compare in <500 ms before a click; semantic verification under 2 s. If the tab, URL, account identity, or relevant field changes, pause and ask rather than proceed.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for hashes and structured diffs; <$0.01 for ambiguous semantic comparison. Browser snapshot transfer and one optional screenshot dominate latency.
args.security_concerns: Hash only redacted relevant fields, never upload passwords, tokens, or full page bodies to the relay. Bind approval to tab/session pseudonym, URL origin, locator, content hash, and short expiry. A changed page invalidates approval; destructive actions remain confirmation-gated.
missing: A browser-side approval token bound to the evidence capsule/content hash and expiring after one mutation
A preflight hook in browser_run_actions and Mac action execution that enforces the token instead of merely recording provenance
A shared semantic-diff contract so browser DOM and Mac vision can agree on what changed

args.user_asks: “Is the thing I’m seeing on my Mac actually the same thing the relay and browser think is happening?”
args.why_useful: The system currently exposes several partial truths: relay job state, Mac receipts, browser tab state, and pipeline traces can disagree or go stale. A spoken discrepancy report would identify the first contradictory observation, its age, and the safest next check instead of silently choosing one source.
surfaces: pendant for a short discrepancy alert and follow-up question
relay for job/session state and server timestamps
Mac agent for permissions, process reachability, action receipts, and pipeline trace
browser extension for live tab/session identity and pending command state
Mac vision for a visual confirmation of what is actually rendered
args.model_tier: Deterministic rules should align timestamps, IDs, hashes, and freshness first; use a low-cost reasoning model only to summarize contradictions. Realtime is reserved for the spoken answer.
args.latency_budget: Routine check in 1–2 s; visual fallback under 5 s. It must return “consistent,” “contradictory,” or “not observable,” with the oldest observation age.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.01 when structured snapshots suffice; one vision call costs more and is used only on disagreement or missing DOM evidence.
args.security_concerns: Keep raw authenticated page content on the Mac; send only redacted claims, hashes, IDs, and timestamps to relay. Treat a missing source as unknown, not false. Never let a consistency check authorize a destructive action by itself.
missing: A normalized observation envelope with source, capturedAt, freshness policy, subject ID, content hash, and confidence
A contradiction detector that compares relay jobs, Mac receipts, browser state, and pipeline events without treating completed as heard

args.user_asks: “Give me a temporary permission to do exactly this one kind of thing across my Mac and logged-in browser, and let me revoke it from the pendant at any time.”
args.why_useful: Today consent is fragmented: the relay, Mac planner, and browser extension can each be trusted, but there is no owner-visible, scope-limited delegation that follows one request across all three. This would let the owner safely authorize a bounded task without repeatedly confirming harmless steps, while retaining an immediate physical stop control.
surfaces: pendant button/voice to display, confirm, and revoke a short-lived delegation
relay to mint a signed, single-purpose capability token and enforce its expiry, audience, and action limits

Mac vision only as a read-only verifier that cannot expand the delegation
args.model_tier: Deterministic policy and signature checks; no expensive model for authorization. Realtime is used only to explain the scope and expiry in one short sentence.
args.latency_budget: Issuing or revoking under 300 ms when connected; every action adds under 50 ms for local token validation. Offline pendant revocation must be queued monotonically and honored on the next link before any new delegated action.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; cryptographic checks and small event records dominate. Hardware work is firmware button/LED state plus a bounded revocation journal, not routine SD writes.
args.security_concerns: Bind the token to owner identity, task ID, allowed verbs, target origins/apps, maximum count, expiry, and a nonce; prevent model text from widening scope. Revocation must fail closed, survive relay restart, and be visible in receipts. Never delegate password extraction, arbitrary shell, purchases, deletion, or message sending without a separate confirmation.

args.model_tier: Deterministic provenance display, conflict detection, and targeted fact mutation; a cheap summarizer can turn the record into one spoken sentence. Realtime is not needed for background reconciliation.
args.latency_budget: Answer provenance in under 1 s from local memory; apply a confirmed correction and invalidate projections within 2 s. Scheduled jobs must use the new value on their next invocation.

args.security_concerns: Do not speak secret fact values by default. args.user_asks: “What actually happened, and what should I do next?”
args.why_useful: After any spoken request, the system would give one honest account across the whole chain instead of saying “done” when only the Mac ran. It correlates the pendant's capture-quality verdict, relay job and socket state, Mac action receipts, browser command/result, screenshots, and (when available) playback confirmation, then tells the owner exactly where the chain stopped and offers the next reversible recovery.
args.model_tier: A cheap deterministic correlator produces the evidence graph and confidence labels; use realtime only to explain the short result conversationally, escalating to a stronger model for ambiguous screenshots or competing receipts.

args.change: Add a postcondition evidence bundle to every Mac/browser action: after execution, use the now-live Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions to capture a bounded redacted UI observation, attach its content hash and capsuleId to the existing job receipt, and classify the outcome as observed-success, observed-failure, or unknown. Propagate the same correlation ID to relay jobs and browser commands.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop hearing “done” when a button did nothing or a page stayed unchanged; the system can show what was visibly true after it acted and recover from the actual failure.

Round 207 findings:

- **Mac perception is now fully trusted:** Accessibility, Screen Recording, and required automation permissions report `ready: true`.
- **Safari bridge is live:** two tabs, current YouTube tab, zero pending commands.
- **Relay is reachable and D1-backed;** the Mac bridge is online.

I proposed four capabilities:

1. **Away-period change witness** — “What actually changed while I was away, and which parts are assumptions?” It compares relay, Mac, browser, and pipeline cursors rather than merely presenting another current-state digest.
2. **End-to-end pendant reality check** — distinguishes bench-only USB presence, connected-but-unregistered, stale registration, and genuinely usable audio. This still needs the bounded USB diagnostic action to become executable.
3. **Perception freshness firewall** — attaches freshness, source, cursor, and contradiction status to every fact before judgement/action can use it. High-impact actions must not proceed on stale or structurally unavailable evidence.
4. **Negative-evidence receipt** — when the system says “nothing was waiting,” it records exactly what it checked, the bounds applied, and whether the result was truly empty, unreadable, truncated, or expired.

What I still need is not another permission grant. The important missing pieces are:

- Durable per-source cursors and tombstones for reliable diffs.
- Machine-readable result semantics: `none`, `unreadable`, `truncated`, `expired`, and `not-applicable`.
- A real bounded USB serial diagnostic action; the granted concept is not yet in the live route/action inventory.
- A device-originated pendant identity/health path and playback acknowledgement.
- Relay/browser provenance metadata that can be joined to Mac evidence capsules.
- A small bounded receipt store for negative evidence and freshness decisions.

The single most useful capability is the **freshness firewall**: it would stop the system from turning stale memory, a changed browser tab, Mac-side completion, or an absent/capped relay row into a confident action.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- A **cross-surface data-flow receipt** showing what browser data would leave the Mac, where it goes, and what was actually retained.
- A **propagation-aware forget command** that finds, quarantines, deletes, and verifies copies across browser evidence, relay announcements/audio, jobs, memory, and pipeline records.

All three require new lineage and receipt protocols between existing surfaces; none can be honestly delivered by simply wiring today’s isolated endpoints together.

A stale browser tab or reused relay context could otherwise feed observations into the wrong action. This capability would expose a task-binding verdict before sensitive context is joined or an action is taken.
args.model_tier: Deterministic cryptographic/session checks; no model call unless the owner asks for a plain-language explanation
args.latency_budget: Under 250 ms with cached session state; under 2 seconds when a fresh browser challenge is required
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; dominated by one browser challenge-response and local signature verification
args.security_concerns: Never expose raw session identifiers, cookies, or extension nonces in speech. Bind only pseudonymous task IDs and expiry windows. If binding fails, refuse cross-surface joins rather than guessing.
missing: A relay-issued task nonce propagated into Mac and browser commands
A browser extension challenge-response proving the active tab/session owns that nonce
A Mac-side attestation tying the action ledger and browser result to the same task nonce
An owner-visible 'bound / stale / crossed' verdict consumed by judgement and action

args.user_asks: Before you say this aloud, did any part of the answer come from a secret, private screen, or sensitive page—and can you safely summarize it without leaking the value?
args.why_useful: Current redaction and provenance structures protect stored evidence, but nothing is a final speech-time gate across browser text, screenshots, Mac state, and relay-generated summaries. This would stop a private tab title, password fragment, message, or financial value from being spoken merely because it entered context upstream.
args.model_tier: Deterministic sensitivity classifier and redaction first; a small model only for safe paraphrase when the owner has authorized spoken summaries
args.latency_budget: Under 150 ms for known-sensitive fields; under 1 second for a novel combined answer
args.cost_estimate: Low: local classification and masking dominate; model cost only for paraphrasing redacted content
args.security_concerns: Raw sensitive values stay on the Mac and are never sent to the relay or realtime model. Default to omission, not euphemistic guessing. Require explicit owner policy for categories such as messages, passwords, health, finance, and intimate content.
missing: A speech-boundary interceptor that sees the final grounded claims before TTS or realtime output
One sensitivity taxonomy shared by evidence capsules, screenshots, browser claims, and Mac automation results
Local redaction/paraphrase routines that preserve meaning without transmitting the secret
A durable owner policy for which categories may be spoken, summarized, or always omitted

args.user_asks: Has my system become less safe since the last time I trusted it—did permissions, browser sessions, relay credentials, or automation scope change?
args.why_useful: A current green status is not evidence that the trust boundary stayed stable. The owner needs a security-drift report that notices permission changes, new browser identities, relay credential rotation, scope changes, and unexpected automation surfaces, then distinguishes owner-approved changes from unexplained ones.
args.model_tier: Deterministic baseline comparison and policy evaluation; use a cheap background model only to explain a flagged diff
args.latency_budget: Under 1 second from a cached baseline; 2-4 seconds when refreshing all surfaces
args.cost_estimate: Very low: structured metadata and hashes only; no page bodies or screenshots required
args.security_concerns: The baseline itself is sensitive. Store only salted fingerprints, permission classes, device/session pseudonyms, and timestamps. Never expose bearer tokens or raw credential material. A newly broadened permission should be reported but not automatically revoked.
missing: A signed, owner-approved security baseline spanning Mac TCC permissions, browser extension identities, relay device credentials, and action scopes
Change events for permission grants/revocations and relay credential/scope updates
A durable approval record distinguishing owner-approved changes from unexplained drift
A policy engine that blocks sensitive actions when the baseline is stale or unexplained drift is present

transcript.summary: Recorded three new, non-duplicate capabilities: cryptographic cross-surface task binding; a speech-time privacy/sensitivity gate; and security-posture drift detection against an owner-approved baseline. Each names the owner-visible benefit and the missing protocol or policy changes required.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the existing relay, browser, and Mac identity/session stores can be extended with a shared task nonce and signed baseline without exposing credentials or requiring a new owner-facing identity system.

args.subject: Novel findings round 209
args.body: Live ops shows browser online on YouTube while affinity still points to news.google.com; pipeline routine audio says 58.5s in text but telemetry says 9.824s/471KB, and relay marks held_by_relay. I’m proposing a cross-surface contradiction detector, stale browser-affinity guard, and adaptive alternate delivery for held routine audio—not playback ACK duplicate.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: Make sure scheduled briefings reach me even when the pendant is unavailable.
args.why_useful: Today a completed Mac run can leave 471 KB of audio held at the relay with the pendant absent, and the owner receives no alternate delivery. This would detect that precise state, produce a short text/notification fallback on the Mac, and retain the full audio for later instead of silently losing the briefing.
args.model_tier: background model for classification and concise fallback drafting; no realtime call unless the owner asks a follow-up
args.latency_budget: Detect within 60 seconds of a routine result; fallback notification in under 5 seconds after the relay reports held_by_relay.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.001–$0.01 per routine, dominated by one short summarization; zero model cost when the existing brief text is already available.
args.security_concerns: Fallback may expose briefing text in a macOS notification or browser surface; honor the existing routine sensitivity and require confirmation before sending outside the device. Never claim the pendant heard it.
missing: A relay-to-Mac delivery-policy event carrying held_by_relay/awaitsDevice and an expiry, rather than requiring inference from pipeline traces
A Mac notification or browser inbox target for routine fallback
A user policy for which routines may be text-fallbacked and how long audio remains valid

args.user_asks: Before you tell me a routine finished, check that its evidence agrees and explain any contradiction.
args.why_useful: The live pipeline contains a concrete contradiction: the spoken text claims 58.5 seconds of audio while the same run's telemetry reports 9.824 seconds and 471,570 bytes. A perception fence should prevent a false 'done' or misleading owner report when duration, byte count, stage state, and delivery state disagree.
args.model_tier: cheap deterministic validator first; background model only to phrase an explanation when fields conflict
args.latency_budget: Under 100 ms for numeric/state checks; under 2 seconds for a human-readable explanation.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for validation; <$0.001 for an occasional explanation.
args.security_concerns: Telemetry can include command text and snippets; keep raw payload local, send only field names and bounded discrepancy facts to any model. Never auto-retry or mark success based on a model judgment.
missing: A shared evidence contract defining which fields are authoritative for audio duration, bytes, and completion
A relay/local-agent status that can be 'contradictory' instead of collapsing to completed/failed
A reader in the owner-facing briefing and job-status paths that surfaces the contradiction and withholds completion language

args.user_asks: Before acting in my browser, tell me if the active tab and the session you remember are different.
args.why_useful: The live browser is on a YouTube tab while the stored session affinity still points to news.google.com. Acting on the remembered session without noticing this split can click or read the wrong site. The guard would compare fresh extension state, session affinity, and the requested target, then pause with a one-sentence clarification instead of guessing.
args.model_tier: deterministic URL/host comparison; use the realtime model only to ask the short clarification during an active voice turn
args.latency_budget: Under 300 ms before any browser action; clarification within one voice turn.
args.cost_estimate: Zero for comparison; negligible realtime tokens for a clarification.
args.security_concerns: URLs and tab titles can reveal sensitive activity. Keep comparisons on the Mac, redact query strings by default, and require confirmation when the mismatch involves a logged-in or destructive action.
missing: A first-class browser context snapshot with active tab, session affinity, last-seen timestamps, and confidence in one schema
A precondition hook in browser_run_actions/mac vision that can block execution on context mismatch
An explicit owner policy for when a host change is safe versus when to ask

args.change: Add a cross-surface routine collision and freshness gate: before scheduler execution, group enabled routines by local firing instant and semantic overlap, compare their last successful run and output receipts, then present one merged run or ask which to keep. Record the decision and suppress only the duplicate invocation, never delete routines automatically.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently has multiple daily routines at 07:00 and multiple at 17:00, including overlapping briefs. This can produce duplicate spoken interruptions and stale audio while making the system look healthy. One coherent brief is more useful than several 'completed' runs.
args.effort: Medium: scheduler-side grouping, Mac timezone resolution, lightweight semantic similarity, and a reversible decision record in the routine-run history.
args.risk: A genuinely distinct routine could be merged or skipped. Recovery is a preview-first collision report, conservative threshold, and one-click 'run separately' override; no automatic routine deletion.
args.cost_impact: <$0.01/day for semantic comparison if needed; deterministic timestamp grouping is free.
args.latency_impact: Adds <1 second before a scheduled run; no impact on audio generation.
args.security_impact: Routine names and commands stay within relay/Mac stores; do not send command text to an external model unless the owner permits it.
depends_on: GET /routines
GET /routines/:routineId/runs
POST /routines/:routineId/run
GET /pipeline
GET /ops/snapshot
Authoritative America/New_York timezone for Mac-resolved firing times

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.finding: At the live probe, Safari extension is online with active tab https://www.youtube.com (tabCount 2), while its stored affinity includes sessionId url:https://news.google.com/search; this is a current context mismatch, not an inferred historical state.
args.evidence: GET /ops/snapshot at 2026-08-08T23:59Z returned browser.devices[0].tabUrl=https://www.youtube.com and affinity[0].sessionId=url:https://news.google.com/search.

args.finding: A live pipeline run for the scheduled news brief is relay_result done but delivery state held_by_relay with awaitsDevice=true, playbackActive=false, heard=unknown; its TTS telemetry reports 9,824 ms and 471,570 PCM bytes while event text says 58.5 seconds of audio.
args.evidence: GET /pipeline returned pipelineId job_a3740055-b1c1-4b08-bccb-3615ea4af7cd with delivery and tts event fields.

args.finding: The Mac local agent is currently ready with Accessibility, Screen Recording, and required automation permissions granted; the relay is reachable and the Mac bridge is online, while no pendant is registered.
args.evidence: GET /ops/status and discover devices at round 209.

transcript.text:
Round 209 findings:

- **Mac is fully ready:** Accessibility, Screen Recording, and required automation permissions are granted.
- **Relay and browser bridge are online.**
- **No pendant is registered**, so relay-held audio cannot currently be confirmed as heard.
- **Browser context mismatch:** Safari is actively on YouTube, while stored session affinity still points to Google News.
- **Pipeline contradiction:** the news brief is marked `relay_result: done`, but remains `held_by_relay`, with playback unknown. Its telemetry reports 9.824 seconds of audio while accompanying text claims 58.5 seconds.

I proposed four new capabilities/changes:

1. **Automatic alternate delivery for unavailable-pendant briefings** — concise Mac/browser fallback while retaining the full audio.
2. **Evidence contradiction gate** — prevent “completed” claims when audio duration, byte counts, stage status, and delivery state disagree.
3. **Browser context mismatch guard** — block actions when the active tab and remembered session diverge.
4. **Routine collision/freshness gate** — merge or preview overlapping scheduled routines rather than producing duplicate interruptions.

What I still need:

- A first-class relay-to-Mac delivery-policy event, so fallback behavior does not infer state from raw pipeline traces.
- A shared evidence contract defining authoritative audio duration and completion fields.
- A browser precondition hook that can stop actions before execution on a context mismatch.
- An explicit owner policy for which routines may fall back to text and which overlapping routines should merge.
- A real pendant connection before any claim about receipt or playback can be verified.

args.user_asks: When I ask for a briefing, tell me only information that was fresh at the requested cutoff, and say exactly what was too old or unverifiable.
args.why_useful: A scheduled news brief can be generated successfully while its sources, cached browser pages, or relay-held audio are stale. The owner needs temporal truth, not merely a completed run. This would enforce per-claim freshness across browser captures, Mac research, and relay scheduling, then speak a bounded uncertainty statement instead of silently blending old and new material.
args.model_tier: Cheap deterministic timestamp/provenance checks first; background model for compressing the resulting freshness ledger into one spoken sentence.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds of validation after research completes; no more than 3 seconds added to a scheduled brief.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for timestamp checks; <$0.005 per briefing for a short uncertainty summary.
args.security_concerns: Source URLs, page titles, and private browser captures must remain local unless the owner explicitly requests cloud research. Never treat an undated page as current merely because retrieval succeeded.
missing: A common source-observation record carrying observedAt, publishedAt when known, requested cutoff, and freshness verdict
Browser and relay research paths that preserve those timestamps instead of returning only text
A speech/template layer that names stale or unverifiable claims without exposing sensitive URLs

args.user_asks: Let the pendant and Mac agree on whether I am available before interrupting me, and queue low-priority things without making me manage another setting.
args.why_useful: The relay, browser, and Mac can each be alive while the owner is actually in a call, speaking to someone else, or actively typing. A single availability decision using pendant voice activity, Mac foreground/meeting state, and browser activity would prevent badly timed interruptions while preserving urgent items.
args.model_tier: Deterministic state machine for availability and priority; realtime model only for interpreting an ambiguous spoken override.
args.latency_budget: Availability updates within 1 second; interruption decision under 100 ms; spoken override responds within one voice turn.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero steady-state; <$0.001 for rare ambiguous overrides.
args.security_concerns: Microphone-derived availability must be reduced to short-lived state, not uploaded audio. Calendar titles and active-window names should stay on the Mac. Emergency/high-priority policy must be explicit and never inferred from model confidence.
missing: A cross-surface availability protocol with leases, expiry, confidence, and reasons
A pendant-side local occupancy signal that works offline, rather than relying on relay registration
Scheduler and announcement delivery that honor the lease and expose why an item was deferred
A user-editable priority/escalation policy

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 6 of 7 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: /v1/announcements. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: After you change something on my Mac, let me ask 'what changed?' and hear a before-and-after explanation tied to the exact file, browser page, or app state.
args.why_useful: Today action receipts and browser results can establish that an operation ran, but they do not give the owner a compact, cross-surface explanation of the resulting state. This would join Mac action ledgers, browser provenance, and relay speech into a durable, owner-auditable change narrative with an undo path where available.
args.model_tier: Deterministic diff and receipt join first; cheap background model to phrase the spoken explanation, never to invent a change.
args.latency_budget: Record the change synchronously; answer a follow-up in under 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for structured diffs; <$0.005 when summarization is needed.
args.security_concerns: Before/after values may contain secrets. Redact credentials and private page content at capture, retain only bounded hashes/snippets, and require confirmation before replaying sensitive values aloud. Destructive undo remains confirmation-gated.
missing: A cross-surface change identifier joining action ledger step, browser command/result, evidence capsule, job receipt, and spoken response
A durable owner-facing change journal with redaction and retention rules
Diff adapters for files, browser mutations, and application state
A read-only voice/dashboard query over that journal

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Freshness-enforced briefings** — every claim carries an observation/publication time and the owner hears what is stale or unverifiable.
2. **Cross-surface availability arbitration** — pendant occupancy, Mac activity, browser state, and relay priority jointly decide whether to interrupt or defer.
3. **Cross-surface change journal** — “what changed?” produces a before/after explanation joined to the exact Mac action, browser mutation, receipt, and undo path.

Each requires new contracts and join layers between existing surfaces; none is available to the owner today.

args.subject: Fresh live truth: Mac fully ready
args.body: Round 210 snapshot confirms Accessibility + Screen Recording trusted, automation all granted, browser online Safari YouTube, relay reachable D1, Mac bridge online; pendant still absent. We can now propose perception relying on actual screen/input, not blocked TCC.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: When I say “what’s that?”, use whatever is in front of me right now and answer the question out loud.
args.why_useful: The pendant becomes a genuinely eyes-free pointer to the owner’s current attention: no app name, tab URL, or screenshot description is needed. It can identify the focused UI object, read visible text, and answer in one turn instead of making the owner explain context.
surfaces: pendant captures the utterance and plays the answer
mac-vision captures the focused window and locates the likely object under the cursor or recent focus
browser-extension supplies the authenticated tab DOM/text when the target is in Safari
relay-realtime transcribes, asks the local perception loop for grounding, and speaks a short answer
faculty-perception attaches freshness, source, and confidence so faculty-judgement can refuse guesses
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the short utterance and final spoken response; a cheaper vision/text model handles screenshot OCR and element localization; no expensive model is used for raw extraction.
args.latency_budget: Target 1.5–3 seconds: 300 ms capture/route, up to 1.5 s local vision or DOM extraction, then one realtime turn. If the target is ambiguous, ask one clarification rather than hallucinating.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero incremental API cost when DOM/accessibility text suffices; roughly $0.005–$0.03 for a vision fallback, dominated by screenshot vision tokens.
args.security_concerns: Screenshots and authenticated page text remain on the Mac unless explicitly sent to the relay; redact passwords, payment fields, and secret locators before any model call. Require a visible/voice confirmation before reading sensitive content aloud.
missing: A focused-target perception endpoint that joins Screen Recording/accessibility coordinates to the browser extension’s active tab
A local redaction and confidence gate for screenshots
A relay request/response contract carrying a short-lived grounding id and source timestamp

args.user_asks: Tell me when the information on my Mac and the information on the web disagree, and show me exactly what each source said.
args.why_useful: This catches expensive or embarrassing errors—stale dashboards, changed prices, conflicting appointment details, or a local document copied from an outdated page—while preserving the distinction between observed facts and inferred explanations.
surfaces: browser-extension reads the authenticated page and its current DOM
mac-vision or mac-terminal reads the local app/document view without leaving the Mac
relay performs an independent public-web read when a second source is needed
faculty-perception normalizes timestamps, URLs, content hashes, and confidence, then emits a contradiction record
faculty-judgement decides whether to interrupt the owner or wait for a request
pendant speaks only the concise conflict and offers the two source excerpts
args.model_tier: Use a cheap structured extraction model for each source and a small text model for pairwise comparison; reserve realtime for the owner-facing interruption or follow-up.
args.latency_budget: On demand under 5 seconds; background checks should be scheduled and quiet, with interruption only when a high-confidence material contradiction is found.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.08 per comparison, dominated by browser/vision extraction and source text; local DOM/accessibility cases can be effectively free.
args.security_concerns: Never send private local documents to a public relay read. Keep local evidence on the Mac, hash and redact excerpts, and require confirmation before quoting sensitive data aloud. Public pages must remain marked untrusted.
missing: A cross-source observation schema with source URL/app, capturedAt, content hash, and region
A local-only comparator that can compare private Mac evidence with public relay evidence without exporting the private body
A user policy for which contradiction severities may interrupt

args.user_asks: While I am working, quietly notice what I am trying to do from my screen and browser, and tell me the single next fact or action that would unblock me when I ask.
args.why_useful: It turns passive computer use into a useful second set of eyes: it can recognize a blocked login, missing attachment, error dialog, or form validation failure and answer “what’s blocking me?” without the owner narrating the screen.
surfaces: mac-vision watches only explicit snapshots or a user-triggered watch, not continuous raw recording
browser-extension reports the active tab, visible error state, and pending command state
mac-terminal and mac-planner inspect local job receipts or command output when the blocker is outside the browser
faculty-perception builds a compact state transition with evidence and freshness
faculty-judgement ranks one unblocker and respects quiet hours
relay-realtime and pendant deliver the answer on request
args.model_tier: A cheap local classifier handles stable UI states and diffs; use a stronger model only for ambiguous multi-app interpretation; realtime is only the final conversational turn.
args.latency_budget: Snapshot-to-state under 1 second locally; answer under 2 seconds on request. Watching is event-driven and rate-limited rather than a continuous vision stream.
args.cost_estimate: Mostly local compute; $0–$0.02 per ambiguous interpretation. Storage is bounded to hashes and short observations, not screenshots.
args.security_concerns: Explicit opt-in watch sessions with a physical/voice stop; exclude password managers, banking, private messages, and camera feeds by app policy. Do not retain screenshots by default; retain only redacted state transitions.
missing: An event-driven screen-diff/watch session with app and region exclusion policies
A blocker taxonomy and confidence-calibrated next-step ranking
A bounded observation ledger joinable to browser commands and Mac action receipts

args.change: Add an explicit, read-only `attention_frame` operation to the Mac agent. In one bounded call it returns focused app/window, frontmost browser tab, accessibility-selected element bounds and role/name, visible-text digest, capture timestamp, and a redacted screenshot region; it must fail closed when the target app is sensitive or the frame is older than a caller-supplied freshness limit. Expose the same frame id to browser inspection and action receipts.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask “what’s that?” or “why is this stuck?” and get an answer grounded in exactly what is on screen now, rather than a stale app name or an uncorrelated screenshot.
args.effort: Medium: local Accessibility/Screen Recording plumbing is now live and verified; add one route, redaction policy, and joins to existing browser/action records.
args.risk: The wrong UI region could be described with high confidence, or sensitive text could leak. Recover by returning ambiguity and no body, recording only hashes by default, and requiring a fresh explicit capture for sensitive apps.
args.cost_impact: Low API cost; local capture and OCR dominate. No persistent screenshot storage by default.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for accessibility/DOM extraction, up to 1–2 s only for vision fallback.
args.security_impact: Improves security if it centralizes app exclusions and redaction; must treat Screen Recording output as sensitive and never send raw frames to the relay by default.
depends_on: Current live TCC state (Accessibility and Screen Recording are now granted)
A short-lived grounding-id contract shared with browser inspection and Mac action receipts
A local sensitive-app/field exclusion list

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

Pendant remains absent from device inventory.
